docs.title: MatchMiner-AI
docs.text:
Welcome to the matchminer-ai package documentation.

matchminer-ai is a Python package for running clinical trial matching inference workflows. The package provides modular functions for summarizing trials and patient histories, generating embeddings of each, retrieving candidate matches, scoring match quality, and assessing exclusion criteria.

This package is based on Altreuter et al., MatchMiner-AI: An Open-Source Solution for Cancer Clinical Trial Matching. If you use matchminer-ai, please cite the study below.

Contributions to the package and documentation are welcome through GitHub. See our contribution instructions for more information.

Pre-v1 package

This package is currently pre-v1 and under active development. APIs, configuration options, and outputs may change.

docs.title: Candidate Matching
docs.text: generate_candidate_matches ranks TrialSpace vectors from embed_for_matching by cosine similarity over the entire supplied corpus. Each table needs exactly one identifier column (patient_id, cohort_trial_id or space_trial_id) and an embedding vector column. Pass patients first for patient-centric retrieval and cohorts first for trial-centric retrieval; k=None returns the full ranking. Results keep both identifiers, similarity_score and one-based rank. config is accepted for call compatibility and unused. Vectors from different TrialSpace models cannot be mixed; changing models requires regenerating both sides.

docs.title: generate_candidate_matches
docs.text:
generate_candidate_matches(query_df: DataFrame, corpus_df: DataFrame, *, k: int | None = 20, config=None) -> pd.DataFrame

Return top-k corpus matches per query, preserving entity IDs and rank.

Inputs are TrialSpace tables from embed_for_matching, ranked by cosine similarity. Reverse the arguments for the other retrieval direction. k=None returns all corpus entities. config is accepted for call compatibility and unused. Results include both identifiers, similarity_score, and one-based rank.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/matching/match.py 
def generate_candidate_matches(
    query_df: pd.DataFrame,
    corpus_df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    k: int | None = 20,
    config=None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return top-k corpus matches per query, preserving entity IDs and rank.

    Inputs are TrialSpace tables from ``embed_for_matching``, ranked by cosine
    similarity. Reverse the arguments for the other retrieval direction.
    ``k=None`` returns all corpus entities. ``config`` is accepted for call
    compatibility and unused. Results include both identifiers,
    ``similarity_score``, and one-based rank.
    """
    # Validate required schema for IDs and embeddings.
    query_id_col = _resolve_id_column(query_df, "query_df")
    corpus_id_col = _resolve_id_column(corpus_df, "corpus_df")
    if "embedding" not in query_df.columns:
        raise ValueError("query_df must include embedding")
    if "embedding" not in corpus_df.columns:
        raise ValueError("corpus_df must include embedding")
    if k is not None and (type(k) is not int or k <= 0):
        raise ValueError("k must be a positive integer or None")

    # Parse embeddings and ensure consistent vector dimensionality.
    query_embeddings = _stack_embeddings(query_df["embedding"])
    corpus_embeddings = _stack_embeddings(corpus_df["embedding"])
    if query_embeddings.numel() == 0 or corpus_embeddings.numel() == 0:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            columns=[query_id_col, corpus_id_col, "similarity_score", "rank"]
        )

    # Normalize embeddings and compute cosine similarity matrix.
    query_norm = _normalize_rows(query_embeddings)
    corpus_norm = _normalize_rows(corpus_embeddings)
    similarity = query_norm @ corpus_norm.T

    # Extract top-k corpus matches per query.
    query_ids = query_df[query_id_col].astype(str).tolist()
    corpus_ids = corpus_df[corpus_id_col].astype(str).tolist()

    records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    num_corpus = similarity.shape[1]
    top_k = num_corpus if k is None else min(k, num_corpus)
    for row_idx, query_id in enumerate(query_ids):
        scores = similarity[row_idx]
        if top_k == 0:
            continue
        if top_k == num_corpus:
            ranked_idx = torch.argsort(scores, descending=True)
        else:
            ranked_idx = torch.topk(scores, k=top_k, largest=True).indices
        for rank, corpus_idx in enumerate(ranked_idx, start=1):
            corpus_idx_int = int(corpus_idx)
            records.append(
                {
                    query_id_col: query_id,
                    corpus_id_col: corpus_ids[corpus_idx_int],
                    "similarity_score": float(scores[corpus_idx_int]),
                    "rank": int(rank),
                }
            )

    result = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)
    if result.empty:
        return result

    return result

docs.title: Adaptive trial-centric cutoff
docs.text:
Rank the entire patient corpus, attach the package-format patient and trial summary columns, then select the leading prefix reported by the search:

from matchminer_ai.matching import (
    find_trial_centric_cutoff,
    generate_candidate_matches,
)

ranking = generate_candidate_matches(trial_embeddings, patient_embeddings, k=None)
candidate_pairs = (
    ranking.merge(patient_summaries, on="patient_id")
    .merge(trial_spaces, on="space_trial_id")
)
cutoff = find_trial_centric_cutoff(
    candidate_pairs,
    check_method="trial_checker",  # or "llm"
    score_threshold=0.20,           # use 1 for the default LLM threshold
    patients_per_side=10,
    initial_cutoff_proportion=0.10, # start 10% down when few patients qualify
)
pairs_for_both_checkers = candidate_pairs.sort_values("rank", kind="stable").iloc[
    : cutoff.cutoff
]

LLM probes send the probe patient and trial summaries to the configured LLM backend. Use only endpoints authorized for the sensitivity of those inputs.

To test whether the adaptive result depends on the first boundary position, run the offline stability helper on synthetic or otherwise explicitly authorized data:

from matchminer_ai.matching import assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability

stability = assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability(
    candidate_pairs,
    initial_cutoff_proportions=(0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90),
    score_threshold=0.20,
    patients_per_side=10,
)
print(stability.cutoff_runs)

This diagnostic scores the complete ranking once with score_match_quality and reuses those scores for every start. selected_cutoff_spread measures allocation sensitivity; reasonable_consideration_count_spread measures how many threshold-passing patients that sensitivity adds or omits. These are research QA signals, not patient eligibility determinations.

docs.title: find_trial_centric_cutoff
docs.text:
find_trial_centric_cutoff(candidate_pairs: DataFrame, *, check_method: str = 'trial_checker', score_threshold: float | None = None, patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE, initial_cutoff_proportion: float = DEFAULT_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTION, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None) -> TrialCentricCutoffResult

Find how many TrialSpace-ranked patients should receive both checkers.

The input must contain the complete patient ranking for one trial space, normally produced with generate_candidate_matches(..., k=None) and joined to the patient and trial summary text. By default the search starts halfway down the ranking; initial_cutoff_proportion can move that first probe when the expected qualifying fraction is substantially smaller or larger. At each proposed cutoff it scores the patients immediately above and below the boundary, then bisects toward the top when failures are the majority (or the window is tied) and toward the bottom when passes are the strict majority. Overlapping probe windows reuse prior scores.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default candidate_pairs DataFrame

Complete TrialSpace-ranked patient pairs for exactly one trial space. Required columns are patient_id, space_trial_id, rank, cancer_history_summary, and clinical_space_summary.

required check_method ('trial_checker', 'llm')

Use the decision model's 0-1 match-quality score or the LLM checker's 0-6 score for the boundary probes.

"trial_checker" score_threshold float

Score at or above which a probe patient passes. Defaults to 0.20 for the decision model and 1 for the LLM checker.

None patients_per_side int

Number of patients to probe on each side of a proposed cutoff. Windows are clipped at the top and bottom of the ranking.

10 initial_cutoff_proportion float

Proportion of the complete ranking at which to place the first cutoff probe. Must be between 0 (the top) and 1 (the bottom). Later probes use the same bisection behavior regardless of this starting point.

0.5 config MMAIConfig

Package configuration passed to the selected checker.

None progress_callback callable

Called after each iteration as (completed, maximum, message).

None

Returns:

Type Description TrialCentricCutoffResult

The selected cutoff, unique probe scores, and iteration diagnostics.

Notes

This heuristic assumes that checker pass rates generally decline with TrialSpace rank. It estimates a compute cutoff; it does not establish patient eligibility or replace review of the complete current protocol.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/matching/adaptive_cutoff.py 
def find_trial_centric_cutoff(
    candidate_pairs: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    check_method: str = "trial_checker",
    score_threshold: float | None = None,
    patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE,
    initial_cutoff_proportion: float = DEFAULT_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTION,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None,
) -> TrialCentricCutoffResult:
    """Find how many TrialSpace-ranked patients should receive both checkers.

    The input must contain the complete patient ranking for one trial space,
    normally produced with ``generate_candidate_matches(..., k=None)`` and
    joined to the patient and trial summary text. By default the search starts
    halfway down the ranking; ``initial_cutoff_proportion`` can move that first
    probe when the expected qualifying fraction is substantially smaller or
    larger. At each proposed cutoff it scores the patients immediately above
    and below the boundary, then bisects toward the top when failures are the
    majority (or the window is tied) and toward the bottom when passes are the
    strict majority. Overlapping probe windows reuse prior scores.

    Parameters
    ----------
    candidate_pairs : pd.DataFrame
        Complete TrialSpace-ranked patient pairs for exactly one trial space.
        Required columns are ``patient_id``, ``space_trial_id``, ``rank``,
        ``cancer_history_summary``, and ``clinical_space_summary``.
    check_method : {"trial_checker", "llm"}, default "trial_checker"
        Use the decision model's 0-1 match-quality score or the LLM checker's 0-6 score for
        the boundary probes.
    score_threshold : float, optional
        Score at or above which a probe patient passes. Defaults to 0.20 for
        the decision model and 1 for the LLM checker.
    patients_per_side : int, default 10
        Number of patients to probe on each side of a proposed cutoff. Windows
        are clipped at the top and bottom of the ranking.
    initial_cutoff_proportion : float, default 0.5
        Proportion of the complete ranking at which to place the first cutoff
        probe. Must be between 0 (the top) and 1 (the bottom). Later probes use
        the same bisection behavior regardless of this starting point.
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        Package configuration passed to the selected checker.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Called after each iteration as ``(completed, maximum, message)``.

    Returns
    -------
    TrialCentricCutoffResult
        The selected cutoff, unique probe scores, and iteration diagnostics.

    Notes
    -----
    This heuristic assumes that checker pass rates generally decline with
    TrialSpace rank. It estimates a compute cutoff; it does not establish
    patient eligibility or replace review of the complete current protocol.
    """
    method = _normalize_check_method(check_method)
    threshold = _resolve_score_threshold(method, score_threshold)
    radius = _validate_patients_per_side(patients_per_side)
    starting_proportion = _validate_initial_cutoff_proportion(initial_cutoff_proportion)
    ranked = _prepare_ranked_candidates(candidate_pairs)

    def score_rows(rows: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        if method == "trial_checker":
            return score_match_quality(
                rows,
                config=config,
                filter_low_quality=False,
            )
        return score_match_quality_with_llm(rows, config=config)

    return _run_cutoff_search(
        ranked,
        method=method,
        threshold=threshold,
        radius=radius,
        starting_proportion=starting_proportion,
        score_rows=score_rows,
        progress_callback=progress_callback,
    )

docs.title: assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability
docs.text:
assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability(candidate_pairs: DataFrame, *, initial_cutoff_proportions: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] = DEFAULT_STABILITY_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTIONS, score_threshold: float | None = None, patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None) -> TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult

Assess adaptive-cutoff sensitivity to its first boundary position.

This QA helper runs the match-quality check over the complete ranked corpus exactly once, then replays the adaptive search against those cached scores for each requested starting proportion. It reports both the selected cutoff and the number of threshold-passing patients within the selected prefix. A stable result has small spreads across starts.

Unlike :func:find_trial_centric_cutoff, this function intentionally scores every candidate. It is an offline diagnostic for synthetic or otherwise explicitly authorized data, not the compute-saving production path and not an eligibility assessment.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default candidate_pairs DataFrame

Complete TrialSpace-ranked patient pairs for one trial space, with the same required columns as :func:find_trial_centric_cutoff.

required initial_cutoff_proportions sequence of float

Unique first-probe positions between 0 and 1. Defaults to 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 90% of the complete ranking.

DEFAULT_STABILITY_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTIONS score_threshold float

match-quality score at or above which a patient passes for this QA run. Defaults to 0.20 on the 0-1 sigmoid scale.

None patients_per_side int

Number of patients on each side of every replayed boundary probe.

10 config MMAIConfig

Package configuration used for the one complete match-quality pass.

None progress_callback callable

Called after each starting-position replay as (completed, total_starts, message).

None

Returns:

Type Description TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult

Per-start diagnostics, one complete table of cached match-quality scores, and the cutoff and passing-count spreads.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/matching/adaptive_cutoff.py 
def assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability(
    candidate_pairs: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    initial_cutoff_proportions: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] = (
        DEFAULT_STABILITY_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTIONS
    ),
    score_threshold: float | None = None,
    patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None,
) -> TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult:
    """Assess adaptive-cutoff sensitivity to its first boundary position.

    This QA helper runs the match-quality check over the complete ranked corpus exactly
    once, then replays the adaptive search against those cached scores for each
    requested starting proportion. It reports both the selected cutoff and the
    number of threshold-passing patients within the selected prefix. A stable
    result has small spreads across starts.

    Unlike :func:`find_trial_centric_cutoff`, this function intentionally scores
    every candidate. It is an offline diagnostic for synthetic or otherwise
    explicitly authorized data, not the compute-saving production path and not
    an eligibility assessment.

    Parameters
    ----------
    candidate_pairs : pd.DataFrame
        Complete TrialSpace-ranked patient pairs for one trial space, with the
        same required columns as :func:`find_trial_centric_cutoff`.
    initial_cutoff_proportions : sequence of float
        Unique first-probe positions between 0 and 1. Defaults to 10%, 25%,
        50%, 75%, and 90% of the complete ranking.
    score_threshold : float, optional
        match-quality score at or above which a patient passes for this QA run.
        Defaults to 0.20 on the 0-1 sigmoid scale.
    patients_per_side : int, default 10
        Number of patients on each side of every replayed boundary probe.
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        Package configuration used for the one complete match-quality pass.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Called after each starting-position replay as
        ``(completed, total_starts, message)``.

    Returns
    -------
    TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult
        Per-start diagnostics, one complete table of cached match-quality scores,
        and the cutoff and passing-count spreads.
    """
    proportions = _validate_stability_proportions(initial_cutoff_proportions)
    threshold = _resolve_score_threshold("trial_checker", score_threshold)
    radius = _validate_patients_per_side(patients_per_side)
    ranked = _prepare_ranked_candidates(candidate_pairs)
    total_candidates = len(ranked)
    scored = _score_complete_ranking_for_stability(
        ranked,
        threshold=threshold,
        config=config,
    )

    score_lookup = scored[["patient_id", "space_trial_id", "match_quality_score"]]

    def cached_score_rows(rows: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return rows[["patient_id", "space_trial_id"]].merge(
            score_lookup,
            on=["patient_id", "space_trial_id"],
            how="left",
            validate="one_to_one",
            sort=False,
        )

    run_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for run_number, proportion in enumerate(proportions, start=1):
        result = _run_cutoff_search(
            ranked,
            method="trial_checker",
            threshold=threshold,
            radius=radius,
            starting_proportion=proportion,
            score_rows=cached_score_rows,
        )
        selected = result.cutoff
        reasonable_count = int(
            scored.loc[
                scored["rank"] <= selected,
                "stability_score_pass",
            ].sum()
        )
        run_records.append(
            {
                "initial_cutoff_proportion": proportion,
                "initial_proposed_cutoff": int(total_candidates * proportion),
                "selected_cutoff": selected,
                "selected_cutoff_fraction": (
                    selected / total_candidates if total_candidates else 0.0
                ),
                "reasonable_consideration_count": reasonable_count,
                "reasonable_consideration_fraction": (
                    reasonable_count / selected if selected else 0.0
                ),
                "search_iteration_count": len(result.search_history),
                "probe_patient_count": len(result.scored_candidates),
            }
        )
        if progress_callback is not None:
            progress_callback(
                run_number,
                len(proportions),
                (
                    f"Stability start {proportion:.0%}: selected top "
                    f"{selected:,} with {reasonable_count:,} "
                    "threshold-passing patient(s)."
                ),
            )

    cutoff_runs = pd.DataFrame.from_records(run_records, columns=_STABILITY_COLUMNS)
    selected_cutoff_spread = int(
        cutoff_runs["selected_cutoff"].max() - cutoff_runs["selected_cutoff"].min()
    )
    reasonable_count_spread = int(
        cutoff_runs["reasonable_consideration_count"].max()
        - cutoff_runs["reasonable_consideration_count"].min()
    )
    return TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult(
        total_candidates=total_candidates,
        score_threshold=threshold,
        patients_per_side=radius,
        initial_cutoff_proportions=proportions,
        cutoff_runs=cutoff_runs,
        scored_candidates=scored,
        selected_cutoff_spread=selected_cutoff_spread,
        reasonable_consideration_count_spread=reasonable_count_spread,
    )

docs.text:
Most users only need these helpers:

  • Use load_default_preset() to start from the built-in default settings and change a few values in Python.
  • Use load_config() to load your own YAML config file.
  • Use load_preset() when loading a named preset packaged with matchminer-ai.

def load_config(path: str | Path) -> MMAIConfig:
    """Load a configuration YAML file from a user-provided path."""
    config_path = Path(path)
    with config_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        data = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"Config {config_path} did not parse into a mapping.")
    return _config_from_data(data, preset_name=str(config_path))

docs.title: Criteria Check
docs.text:
check_eligibility_criteria asks the decision model (match quality) about each line of a cohort's eligibility criteria.

Polarity

Yes (criterion_pass_probability) means the patient does not clearly fail the line: it is met, its information is missing, or the patient could meet it by waiting. No means the patient clearly fails it: an inclusion line clearly not met, or an exclusion line clearly met. A low criterion_pass_probability flags a likely failing line for review, whichever list the line is on.

Each row of the input is one candidate pair with:

  • patient_id;
  • cohort_trial_id (or historical space_trial_id);
  • cancer_history_summary and general_exclusion_criteria_evidence, the summary's two sections (or one complete patient_summary);
  • cohort_criteria_items, the cohort's tagged lines from remove_boilerplate_criteria: a JSON list of number, heading, text, criterion_type (inclusion or exclusion) and boilerplate.

For each pair the model reads one state, the complete patient summary followed by the cohort's complete criteria numbered in their original order under their inclusion and exclusion labels, and one question per line. The question opens Is this patient potentially eligible for this cohort after review of the patient summary and the one criterion named below? If the patient is potentially eligible, answer yes; if the patient is clearly ineligible because of this criterion, answer no, gives the rules (benefit of the doubt, waitable washouts are not failures, a sub-item belongs to the criterion above it, a line that only introduces others fails only when one of them does) and ends by restating the line, for example [12] Exclusion criterion: Active hepatitis B. Lines whose type never validated are skipped and counted in the metadata's unchecked_lines; identical summary and criteria are asked once.

The result has one row per pair and line: criterion_number, criterion_type, boilerplate, criterion_text, criterion_pass_probability and criterion_clearly_fails (criterion_pass_probability < criteria_check.fail_cutoff, 0.5 by default). filter_failing=True keeps only flagged lines.

These are screening signals for human review, not eligibility determinations. The decision model runs locally by default; patient text reaches only the configured model.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.matching.criteria_check
docs.text:
Per-criterion eligibility check with the decision model's criterion question.

For each candidate pair, the decision model reads one state, the patient's complete summary and the cohort's complete numbered eligibility criteria, and answers one question per criteria line, which restates the line with its number and inclusion/exclusion type.

Polarity: P(yes) is the probability that the patient does NOT clearly fail the line (the line is met, its information is missing, or the patient could meet it by waiting). No means the patient clearly fails it: an inclusion line clearly not met, or an exclusion line clearly met. A low criterion_pass_probability therefore flags a likely failing line for review, whichever list the line is on.

def check_eligibility_criteria(
    pairs: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    filter_failing: bool = False,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """
    Check every eligibility-criterion line of each candidate pair with the decision model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pairs : pd.DataFrame
        Candidate patient–cohort pairs.

        Expected columns
        ----------------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id : str
            Cohort identifier (historical ``space_trial_id`` is accepted).
        cohort_criteria_items : str
            The cohort's tagged criteria lines, as
            :func:`~matchminer_ai.trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria` returns them (a JSON list of
            ``number``, ``heading``, ``text``, ``criterion_type`` and ``boilerplate``).
        cancer_history_summary and general_exclusion_criteria_evidence : str
            The patient summary's two sections (or one complete ``patient_summary``).

    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        ``decision_model`` (the model) and ``criteria_check.fail_cutoff`` (default 0.5). Uses the
        default preset when omitted.
    filter_failing : bool, default False
        If True, return only the lines the patient likely fails (``criterion_clearly_fails``).
    return_metadata : bool, default False
        When True, also return the config snapshot and model metadata.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        One row per pair and checkable line (a line whose type never validated is skipped and
        counted in the metadata's ``unchecked_lines``):

        patient_id, cohort_trial_id or space_trial_id
            The pair.
        criterion_number, criterion_type, boilerplate, criterion_text
            The line: its number in the cohort's criteria, "inclusion" or "exclusion", whether it
            is boilerplate, and its text.
        criterion_pass_probability : float
            P(yes): the probability that the patient does **not** clearly fail this line.
        criterion_clearly_fails : bool
            True when ``criterion_pass_probability`` is below ``criteria_check.fail_cutoff``: the
            patient likely fails the line (an inclusion line not met, or an exclusion line met).
    tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        When return_metadata is True, returns the DataFrame plus metadata.
    """
    from matchminer_ai._texts import patient_full_texts, trial_id_column
    from matchminer_ai.trials.cohort_boilerplate import ITEMS_COLUMN, load_criteria_items

    if "patient_id" not in pairs.columns:
        raise ValueError("pairs is missing required columns: patient_id")
    if ITEMS_COLUMN not in pairs.columns:
        raise ValueError(f"pairs needs {ITEMS_COLUMN}: tag the cohorts' criteria lines with "
                         "matchminer_ai.trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria first")
    trial_id = trial_id_column(pairs)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    cutoff = float(resolved_config.raw.get("criteria_check", {}).get("fail_cutoff", 0.5))
    summaries = patient_full_texts(pairs)
    keys, requests, lines, unchecked = [], {}, {}, 0
    for summary, value in zip(summaries, pairs[ITEMS_COLUMN], strict=True):
        items = load_criteria_items(value)
        checkable = checkable_items(items)
        unchecked += len(items) - len(checkable)
        key = json.dumps([summary, items], ensure_ascii=False)
        keys.append(key)
        if key not in requests and checkable:  # identical summary and criteria are asked once
            requests[key] = (criteria_state(summary, items), {criterion_name(i): criterion_question(i) for i in checkable})
            lines[key] = checkable
    ordered = list(requests)
    answers, model_metadata = run_decisions([requests[k] for k in ordered], config=resolved_config)
    by_key = dict(zip(ordered, answers, strict=True))

    records = []
    for (_, row), key in zip(pairs.iterrows(), keys, strict=True):
        for item in lines.get(key, []):
            probability = by_key[key][criterion_name(item)]
            records.append({"patient_id": row["patient_id"], trial_id: row[trial_id],
                            "criterion_number": int(item["number"]), "criterion_type": item["criterion_type"],
                            "boilerplate": bool(item.get("boilerplate")), "criterion_text": str(item["text"]).strip(),
                            "criterion_pass_probability": probability, "criterion_clearly_fails": probability < cutoff})
    columns = ["patient_id", trial_id, "criterion_number", "criterion_type", "boilerplate", "criterion_text",
               "criterion_pass_probability", "criterion_clearly_fails"]
    output = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=columns)
    if filter_failing:
        output = output.loc[output["criterion_clearly_fails"]].reset_index(drop=True)
    if return_metadata:
        model_metadata = {**model_metadata, "unchecked_lines": unchecked}
        return output, {"package": package_metadata(), "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
                        "model_metadata": {"check_eligibility_criteria": model_metadata}}
    return output

docs.title: LLM check
docs.text:
check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm is the LLM alternative, with the same inputs and the same polarity: yes means the patient does not clearly fail the line; no means the patient clearly fails it. It sends one request per tagged line with the per-criterion teacher prompt the decision model's question 7 is trained on, criterion_check.labels.user.txt around the decision model's own criterion state and question (decision_model.criterion_teacher_messages; the criteria label contract, labeling.contract_hash("criteria")). The answer is a JSON object with answer (yes/no), criterion_status (met, not_met, insufficient_information or not_applicable, as the line binds this patient) and reason. On a remote backend it is decoded under decision_model.CRITERION_LABEL_JSON_SCHEMA (llm_criteria_check.structured_outputs), and it is always validated by decision_model.parse_criterion_label: "no" needs not_met on an inclusion line and met on an exclusion line, and a response stopped before its end is invalid. An invalid answer is asked again with the validation error, up to llm_criteria_check.max_attempts (3). A pair's lines go through the RequestQueue, chunk_size × chunks_in_flight (64) in flight, sharing the prompt prefix; identical summary and criteria are asked once.

The llm_criteria_check section uses the training teacher's settings: Nemotron 3.5 Super, thinking on, 32,768 output tokens and sampling_profile: auto, so the served model's own sampling profile applies.

The result has one row per pair and checkable line, with the decision-model check's line columns (criterion_number, criterion_type, boilerplate, criterion_text) and llm_criterion_answer, llm_criterion_clearly_fails, llm_criterion_status, llm_criterion_reason (None or empty when no attempt validated), llm_criterion_finish_reason, llm_criterion_attempts and llm_criterion_parse_status (parsed or parse_failed: <error>); with debug_mode, the last attempt's llm_criterion_answer_text and llm_criterion_reasoning_text. filter_failing=True keeps the lines answered no. An optional progress(done, total) callback reports each line's final answer. With return_metadata=True the metadata gives the criteria_contract and, under model_metadata["check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm"], the endpoint's metadata with lines, requests, retries, parse_failures, unchecked_lines and structured_outputs.

The patient's complete summary reaches the configured LLM endpoint: use an endpoint authorized for the sensitivity of the data.

def check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm(
    pairs: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: "MMAIConfig | None" = None,
    filter_failing: bool = False,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    progress: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """
    Check every eligibility-criterion line of each candidate pair with an LLM, one request per line.

    The LLM alternative to :func:`~matchminer_ai.matching.check_eligibility_criteria`, with the same
    inputs and the same polarity. Each request is the per-criterion teacher prompt that the decision
    model's question 7 is trained on: ``criterion_check.labels.user.txt`` around the decision model's
    own criterion state and question
    (:func:`~matchminer_ai.matching.decision_model.criterion_teacher_messages`; label contract
    ``matchminer_ai.labeling.contract_hash("criteria")``), that is the complete patient summary, the
    cohort's complete numbered criteria and one line restated with its number and type. On a remote
    backend the answer is decoded under ``CRITERION_LABEL_JSON_SCHEMA``
    (``llm_criteria_check.structured_outputs``) and always validated by
    :func:`~matchminer_ai.matching.decision_model.parse_criterion_label`; an invalid answer is asked
    again with the validation error, up to ``llm_criteria_check.max_attempts``. A pair's lines are
    sent through :class:`~matchminer_ai.llm.request_queue.RequestQueue`, so they run in parallel and
    share the prompt prefix.

    **Polarity: an answer of yes means the patient does NOT clearly fail the line** (it is met, its
    information is missing, or the line does not bind this patient); **no means the patient clearly
    fails it: an inclusion line clearly not met, or an exclusion line clearly met.**

    Parameters
    ----------
    pairs : pd.DataFrame
        Candidate patient–cohort pairs, as for :func:`~matchminer_ai.matching.check_eligibility_criteria`:
        ``patient_id``; ``cohort_trial_id`` (or historical ``space_trial_id``);
        ``cohort_criteria_items`` (the cohort's tagged lines, a JSON list of ``number``, ``heading``,
        ``text``, ``criterion_type`` and ``boilerplate``); and the patient summary's two sections,
        ``cancer_history_summary`` and ``general_exclusion_criteria_evidence`` (or one complete
        ``patient_summary``).
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        ``llm_criteria_check`` (the model, its sampling profile, structured outputs, attempts and
        requests in flight) and ``remote``. Uses the default preset when omitted. With
        ``debug_mode`` the last attempt's answer text and reasoning are returned too.
    filter_failing : bool, default False
        If True, return only the lines the LLM judged clearly failed.
    return_metadata : bool, default False
        When True, also return the config snapshot, model metadata and request counts.
    progress : callable, optional
        ``progress(done, total)`` after each line's final answer (``total`` lines are asked).

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        One row per pair and checkable line (a line whose type never validated is skipped and
        counted in the metadata's ``unchecked_lines``):

        patient_id, cohort_trial_id or space_trial_id
            The pair.
        criterion_number, criterion_type, boilerplate, criterion_text
            The line, as :func:`~matchminer_ai.matching.check_eligibility_criteria` returns it.
        llm_criterion_answer : str or None
            ``"yes"`` (does not clearly fail the line) or ``"no"`` (clearly fails it); None when no
            attempt validated.
        llm_criterion_clearly_fails : bool or None
            True when the answer is no; None when no attempt validated.
        llm_criterion_status : str or None
            How the line binds the patient: ``met``, ``not_met``, ``insufficient_information`` or
            ``not_applicable``.
        llm_criterion_reason : str
            The model's brief explanation (empty when no attempt validated).
        llm_criterion_finish_reason : str
            The last attempt's finish reason (``stop`` when complete).
        llm_criterion_attempts : int
            Requests sent for the line.
        llm_criterion_parse_status : str
            ``parsed``, or ``parse_failed: <the last validation error>``.
        llm_criterion_answer_text, llm_criterion_reasoning_text : str
            The last attempt's answer and reasoning; with ``debug_mode`` only.
    tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        When return_metadata is True, returns the DataFrame plus metadata: ``package``,
        ``config_snapshot``, ``criteria_contract`` and ``model_metadata``
        (``check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm``: the endpoint's metadata plus ``unchecked_lines``,
        ``lines``, ``requests``, ``retries``, ``parse_failures`` and ``structured_outputs``).
    """
    from matchminer_ai._texts import patient_full_texts, trial_id_column
    from matchminer_ai.labeling.tasks import contract_hash
    from matchminer_ai.trials.cohort_boilerplate import ITEMS_COLUMN, load_criteria_items
    from .decision_model import checkable_items, criterion_teacher_messages, parse_criterion_label

    if "patient_id" not in pairs.columns:
        raise ValueError("pairs is missing required columns: patient_id")
    if ITEMS_COLUMN not in pairs.columns:
        raise ValueError(f"pairs needs {ITEMS_COLUMN}: tag the cohorts' criteria lines with "
                         "matchminer_ai.trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria first")
    trial_id = trial_id_column(pairs)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    summaries = patient_full_texts(pairs)
    keys, requests, unchecked = [], {}, 0
    for summary, value in zip(summaries, pairs[ITEMS_COLUMN], strict=True):
        items = load_criteria_items(value)
        checkable = checkable_items(items)
        unchecked += len(items) - len(checkable)
        key = json.dumps([summary, items], ensure_ascii=False)
        keys.append(key)
        if key not in requests and checkable:  # identical summary and criteria are asked once
            requests[key] = (summary, items, checkable)
    total = sum(len(checkable) for _, _, checkable in requests.values())
    answers: dict[tuple[str, int], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    counts = {"requests": 0, "retries": 0}
    model_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    structured = False
    if total:
        runtime, settings = _criteria_runtime(resolved_config)
        structured = settings["structured"]
        header = reasoning_system_prompt(runtime.get("model_name"))
        queue = RequestQueue(get_llm_backend(resolved_config), {None: runtime}, chunk_size=settings["chunk_size"],
                             chunks_in_flight=settings["chunks_in_flight"],
                             model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved_config.model_metadata_cache_dir)
        originals: dict[tuple[str, int], list[dict[str, str]]] = {}
        types: dict[tuple[str, int], str] = {}
        for key, (summary, items, checkable) in requests.items():
            for item in checkable:
                number = int(item["number"])
                messages = criterion_teacher_messages(summary, items, number)
                if header:  # only a model family that needs a system reasoning control gets one
                    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": header}, *messages]
                originals[key, number], types[key, number] = messages, str(item["criterion_type"])
                queue.add((key, number, 1), messages)
                counts["requests"] += 1

        def record(item, answer, reasoning, finish_reason, _provenance):
            key, number, attempt = item
            finish = str(finish_reason or "stop")
            state = answers.setdefault((key, number), {})
            state.update(attempts=attempt, answer_text=str(answer or ""), reasoning_text=str(reasoning or ""),
                         finish_reason=finish)
            try:
                state.update(parsed=parse_criterion_label(str(answer or ""), types[key, number], finish), error=None)
            except ValueError as exc:
                state.update(parsed=None, error=str(exc))
                if attempt < settings["max_attempts"]:
                    queue.add((key, number, attempt + 1), originals[key, number] + [{"role": "user", "content": (
                        f"The preceding attempt failed validation: {exc}. Return a complete replacement JSON object "
                        "following the original instructions.")}])
                    counts["requests"] += 1
                    counts["retries"] += 1
                    return
            if progress is not None:
                progress(sum(1 for s in answers.values() if s["parsed"] is not None or s["attempts"]
                             >= settings["max_attempts"]), total)

        model_metadata = dict(queue.run(record))

    records = []
    for (_, row), key in zip(pairs.iterrows(), keys, strict=True):
        if key not in requests:
            continue
        for item in requests[key][2]:
            state = answers.get((key, int(item["number"])), {})
            parsed = state.get("parsed")
            line = {"patient_id": row["patient_id"], trial_id: row[trial_id],
                      "criterion_number": int(item["number"]), "criterion_type": item["criterion_type"],
                      "boilerplate": bool(item.get("boilerplate")), "criterion_text": str(item["text"]).strip(),
                      "llm_criterion_answer": parsed["answer"] if parsed else None,
                      "llm_criterion_clearly_fails": (parsed["answer"] == "no") if parsed else None,
                      "llm_criterion_status": parsed["criterion_status"] if parsed else None,
                      "llm_criterion_reason": parsed["reason"].strip() if parsed else "",
                      "llm_criterion_finish_reason": state.get("finish_reason", ""),
                      "llm_criterion_attempts": int(state.get("attempts", 0)),
                      "llm_criterion_parse_status": "parsed" if parsed else f"parse_failed: {state.get('error')}"}
            if resolved_config.debug_mode:
                line["llm_criterion_answer_text"] = state.get("answer_text", "")
                line["llm_criterion_reasoning_text"] = state.get("reasoning_text", "")
            records.append(line)
    columns = ["patient_id", trial_id, "criterion_number", "criterion_type", "boilerplate", "criterion_text",
               "llm_criterion_answer", "llm_criterion_clearly_fails", "llm_criterion_status", "llm_criterion_reason",
               "llm_criterion_finish_reason", "llm_criterion_attempts", "llm_criterion_parse_status"]
    if resolved_config.debug_mode:
        columns += ["llm_criterion_answer_text", "llm_criterion_reasoning_text"]
    output = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=columns)
    for column in ("llm_criterion_answer", "llm_criterion_clearly_fails", "llm_criterion_status"):
        # None stays None for an unanswered line (a string dtype would turn it into NaN)
        output[column] = pd.Series([r[column] for r in records], index=output.index, dtype=object)
    if filter_failing:
        output = output.loc[output["llm_criterion_clearly_fails"].eq(True)].reset_index(drop=True)
    if return_metadata:
        metadata = {**model_metadata, "unchecked_lines": unchecked, "lines": total, **counts,
                    "parse_failures": sum(1 for s in answers.values() if s.get("parsed") is None),
                    "structured_outputs": structured}
        return output, {"package": package_metadata(), "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
                        "criteria_contract": contract_hash("criteria"),
                        "model_metadata": {"check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm": metadata}}
    return output

docs.title: PDF document OCR
docs.text:
ocr_pdf is a local, page-aware extractor for trial documents and other PDFs. It retains usable embedded text because it is generally more accurate than rendering a digitally produced page, then falls back to RapidOCR for pages that are image-only or nearly empty. It writes a UTF-8 .txt file with form-feed characters between pages and does not overwrite an existing file unless asked.

from matchminer_ai.documents import ocr_pdf

text_path = ocr_pdf("eligibility-checklist.pdf")

For PDFs with damaged embedded text, or form values that appear only when the page is rendered, force OCR for every page:

text_path = ocr_pdf(
    "completed-checklist.pdf",
    "completed-checklist.ocr.txt",
    force_ocr=True,
    overwrite=True,
)

OCR runs locally. The function does not send document text or page images to an LLM, web search, or hosted OCR service. This local processing boundary is important if the API is later used for authorized patient documents. The output still inherits the source document's sensitivity and must be stored and handled under the same controls.

OCR is probabilistic and can omit or misread characters, especially in tables, handwriting, low-resolution scans, and complex layouts. Compare important text with the source PDF before using it in research review. OCR output does not establish trial eligibility or replace review of the complete, current protocol.

ocr_pdf(pdf_path: str | PathLike[str], output_path: str | PathLike[str] | None = None, *, force_ocr: bool = False, dpi: int = 200, min_embedded_text_chars: int = 50, min_ocr_confidence: float = 0.5, overwrite: bool = False, password: str | None = None, progress_callback: PDFOCRProgress | None = None) -> Path

Extract text from a PDF and write one UTF-8 text file.

Pages with a usable embedded text layer retain that exact text. Image-only or nearly empty pages are rendered and processed locally with RapidOCR. Page order is preserved and form-feed characters delimit pages. No PDF content is sent to an LLM, web search, or other network service.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default pdf_path str or PathLike[str]

Local PDF file to process.

required output_path str or PathLike[str] or None

Destination text file. By default, use the PDF path with a .txt suffix.

None force_ocr bool

Render and OCR every page, ignoring embedded PDF text. This can help with damaged text layers or displayed form values, but embedded text is normally more accurate.

False dpi int

Resolution used to render OCR pages. Must be at least 72.

200 min_embedded_text_chars int

Minimum number of alphanumeric characters required to trust a page's embedded text in automatic mode.

50 min_ocr_confidence float

Discard OCR text lines below this threshold in the inclusive range from 0 to 1.

0.5 overwrite bool

Replace an existing destination only when True.

False password str or None

Password for an encrypted PDF. The password is used locally and is not written to the output.

None progress_callback callable or None

Called after each page as callback(page_number, page_count, method), where method is "embedded" or "ocr".

None

Returns:

Type Description Path

Path to the completed UTF-8 text file.

Raises:

Type Description PDFOCRNoTextError

If the document contains pages but no text can be extracted.

PDFOCRError

If the PDF cannot be opened or a page cannot be processed.

FileExistsError

If the destination exists and overwrite is False.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/documents/ocr.py 
def ocr_pdf(
    pdf_path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    output_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    *,
    force_ocr: bool = False,
    dpi: int = 200,
    min_embedded_text_chars: int = 50,
    min_ocr_confidence: float = 0.5,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    password: str | None = None,
    progress_callback: PDFOCRProgress | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Extract text from a PDF and write one UTF-8 text file.

    Pages with a usable embedded text layer retain that exact text. Image-only
    or nearly empty pages are rendered and processed locally with RapidOCR.
    Page order is preserved and form-feed characters delimit pages. No PDF
    content is sent to an LLM, web search, or other network service.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pdf_path : str or os.PathLike[str]
        Local PDF file to process.
    output_path : str or os.PathLike[str] or None, optional
        Destination text file. By default, use the PDF path with a ``.txt``
        suffix.
    force_ocr : bool, optional
        Render and OCR every page, ignoring embedded PDF text. This can help
        with damaged text layers or displayed form values, but embedded text
        is normally more accurate.
    dpi : int, optional
        Resolution used to render OCR pages. Must be at least 72.
    min_embedded_text_chars : int, optional
        Minimum number of alphanumeric characters required to trust a page's
        embedded text in automatic mode.
    min_ocr_confidence : float, optional
        Discard OCR text lines below this threshold in the inclusive range from
        0 to 1.
    overwrite : bool, optional
        Replace an existing destination only when True.
    password : str or None, optional
        Password for an encrypted PDF. The password is used locally and is not
        written to the output.
    progress_callback : callable or None, optional
        Called after each page as ``callback(page_number, page_count, method)``,
        where ``method`` is ``"embedded"`` or ``"ocr"``.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        Path to the completed UTF-8 text file.

    Raises
    ------
    PDFOCRNoTextError
        If the document contains pages but no text can be extracted.
    PDFOCRError
        If the PDF cannot be opened or a page cannot be processed.
    FileExistsError
        If the destination exists and ``overwrite`` is False.
    """
    _validate_options(
        dpi=dpi,
        min_embedded_text_chars=min_embedded_text_chars,
        min_ocr_confidence=min_ocr_confidence,
    )
    source, destination = _validate_paths(
        pdf_path,
        output_path,
        overwrite=overwrite,
    )

    pdfium = _load_pdfium()
    try:
        document = pdfium.PdfDocument(source, password=password)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise PDFOCRError("Could not open the PDF document.") from exc

    pages: list[str] = []
    ocr_engine: Any | None = None
    try:
        page_count = len(document)
        if page_count == 0:
            raise PDFOCRError("The PDF document contains no pages.")

        for page_index in range(page_count):
            page = document[page_index]
            try:
                embedded_text = ""
                if not force_ocr:
                    try:
                        embedded_text = _normalize_page_text(
                            _extract_embedded_text(page)
                        )
                    except pdfium.PdfiumError:
                        # A renderable page can still have a damaged text layer.
                        embedded_text = ""
                if (
                    not force_ocr
                    and _meaningful_character_count(embedded_text)
                    >= min_embedded_text_chars
                ):
                    page_text = embedded_text
                    method: PDFOCRMethod = "embedded"
                else:
                    if ocr_engine is None:
                        ocr_engine = _create_ocr_engine()
                    page_text = _normalize_page_text(
                        _ocr_page(
                            page,
                            ocr_engine,
                            dpi=dpi,
                            min_confidence=float(min_ocr_confidence),
                        )
                    )
                    method = "ocr"
                pages.append(page_text)
                if progress_callback is not None:
                    progress_callback(page_index + 1, page_count, method)
            except Exception as exc:
                if isinstance(exc, (ImportError, PDFOCRError)):
                    raise
                raise PDFOCRError(
                    f"Failed to process PDF page {page_index + 1}."
                ) from exc
            finally:
                page.close()
    finally:
        document.close()

    if not any(_meaningful_character_count(page) for page in pages):
        raise PDFOCRNoTextError("No text was found in the PDF document.")

    document_text = _PAGE_SEPARATOR.join(pages) + "\n"
    mode = "w" if overwrite else "x"
    with destination.open(mode, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        handle.write(document_text)
    return destination

docs.title: Embedding
docs.text:
Retrieval uses TrialSpace, a single-vector Sentence Transformer: each output row holds the input identifier and one normalized embedding vector, and generate_candidate_matches ranks by cosine similarity.

The default model is, for now and on purpose, a local unpublished directory (user, 2026-11-12): the n=5000 training run's round-2 TrialSpace, google/embeddinggemma-2 fine-tuned for one epoch after round 2 by the training repository's finetune_embedder.py (stage receipt d7ef7270…), at /ksg/kehl_mm_data/mmai/v23/data/no_phi/synthetic_dataset_n5000_screened_20261106/trialspace/models/trialspace_round2. Runs where it is missing or unreadable, such as off camus or its NFS mount, fail with FileNotFoundError rather than mix vectors from different models: nothing falls back to ksg-dfci/TrialSpace-0526 or any Hub model. Loading it needs sentence-transformers 6.1 or later (the version that saved it).

embed_for_matching loads and encodes with the functions training's mining uses (embedding.encoder; see below), so the default encodes exactly as training encoded this model:

Setting Default Training (trialspace/mining.py encoder_settings) Weights / compute dtype: float32, autocast: bfloat16 (CUDA only) float32 weights, bf16 autocast Prompts prompt_profile: trialspace: patients patient_summary, cohorts this_space model_prompts("trialspace"), the same per-side prompts Pooling include_prompt_in_pooling: true (mean pooling over prompt and text) the same Model text_only: true (no vision or audio towers) the same Batches batch_size: 32 --encode-batch-size 32 Length max_seq_length: 4096 (the fit's cap) the fit used 4,096; round-3 mining encoded at 8,192 (one synthetic cohort in 15,263 is longer than 4,096 tokens) Output L2-normalized float32 the same

On fabricated texts, the two paths give identical vectors on CPU and on CUDA. CPU vectors are float32 throughout (autocast is CUDA only), so they differ slightly from CUDA vectors (patient-cohort similarities by up to about 0.0015 on those texts); the encoder identity records which was used, so they are not mixed either.

Retrieval reads key text when it is there. Trial processing is kept in separate steps that callers may run or skip, so the cohort text depends on which ran: after remove_boilerplate_criteria it is the key criteria; without that step, the complete criteria, boilerplate included. TrialSpace models trained by matchminer-ai-training learn from merged cohorts' key criteria (merge_equivalent_cohorts, then remove_boilerplate_criteria) and patients' key sections, so inputs prepared the same way match their training:

Side Identifier Text embedded (first column present) Patient patient_id cancer_history_summary (the summary's key section); else the key section of a complete patient_summary, the text before Other relevant history: Cohort cohort_trial_id (or historical space_trial_id) cohort_key_criteria from remove_boilerplate_criteria; else cohort_eligibility_criteria when the boilerplate step did not run; else historical clinical_space_summary

A TrialSpace model trained by matchminer-ai-training saves one prompt per side, named patient_summary (patients) and this_space (cohorts), and the runtime encodes each side with its own prompt. embedding.trialspace_contract holds these names (PATIENT_PROMPT, COHORT_PROMPT) and the retrieval INSTRUCTION and DIRECTIONS shared with training. A model without side prompts and no prompt_profile, such as the historical TrialSpace-0526, encodes both sides with its saved query instruction. Prompts are applied by name and prepended exactly, as in training and its evaluation scripts, and token counts (count_embedding_tokens) count that same text. Releases before November 2026 prepended the literal word "query" instead of 0526's instruction, so embeddings they stored are not comparable with current ones; regenerate them. embed_texts(texts, entity_type="patient" | "trial") selects a side's prompt for plain strings; without entity_type the shared query prompt is used.

The historical ksg-dfci/TrialSpace-0526 (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) was trained on cancer_history_summary and clinical_space_summary text. To use it, set model_path and remove the EmbeddingGemma 2 settings (dtype, autocast, prompt_profile, default_prompt_name, include_prompt_in_pooling, text_only), and never compare its vectors with the default model's.

from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.embedding import embed_for_matching
from matchminer_ai.matching import generate_candidate_matches

config = load_default_preset()
# config.embedding["model_path"] = "/path/to/trained/trialspace"
patients = embed_for_matching(patient_summaries, entity_type="patient", config=config)
cohorts = embed_for_matching(trial_cohorts, entity_type="trial", config=config)
patient_matches = generate_candidate_matches(patients, cohorts, k=20)
trial_matches = generate_candidate_matches(cohorts, patients, k=40)

Cosine similarity is a ranking score, not a probability or a determination of eligibility. Do not mix embeddings from different checkpoint generations; when changing the model, regenerate both sides. Use an immutable checkpoint path/revision, and restart the process when replacing a cached model at the same path. Stored vectors are checked against the encoder that made them: a local directory is named by a digest of the weights actually loaded (and its training stage receipt), with the encoding settings, tokenizer, prompts and library versions.

Encode key patient/cohort text with TrialSpace for bidirectional retrieval.

Retrieval reads key text only, never boilerplate. Patient rows require patient_id and the summary's key section, cancer_history_summary (when only a complete patient_summary is given, its key section is taken: the text before Other relevant history:). Trial rows require cohort_trial_id and cohort_key_criteria (the cohort's criteria without its boilerplate, from remove_boilerplate_criteria); without the boilerplate step, cohort_eligibility_criteria is embedded, and historical space_trial_id / clinical_space_summary remains accepted.

Returns the identifier and one embedding vector per row. config.embedding selects the checkpoint, device and context. A TrialSpace model that saves patient and cohort prompts gets them for each side. With return_metadata=True, also return the configuration and model fingerprint. See docs/api/embedding.md.

def embed_for_matching(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    entity_type: Literal["patient", "trial"],
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Encode key patient/cohort text with TrialSpace for bidirectional retrieval.

    Retrieval reads key text only, never boilerplate. Patient rows require
    ``patient_id`` and the summary's key section, ``cancer_history_summary``
    (when only a complete ``patient_summary`` is given, its key section is taken:
    the text before ``Other relevant history:``). Trial rows require
    ``cohort_trial_id`` and ``cohort_key_criteria`` (the cohort's criteria without
    its boilerplate, from ``remove_boilerplate_criteria``); without the boilerplate
    step, ``cohort_eligibility_criteria`` is embedded, and historical
    ``space_trial_id`` / ``clinical_space_summary`` remains accepted.

    Returns the identifier and one embedding vector per row. ``config.embedding``
    selects the checkpoint, device and context. A TrialSpace model that saves
    patient and cohort prompts gets them for each side. With
    ``return_metadata=True``, also return the configuration and model fingerprint.
    See docs/api/embedding.md.
    """
    summaries = _resolve_texts(df, entity_type)

    id_cols = _resolve_id_columns(entity_type)
    if entity_type == "trial" and "cohort_trial_id" in df.columns:
        id_cols = ["cohort_trial_id"]
    missing = [col for col in id_cols if col not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"df is missing required columns for {entity_type}: {missing}")

    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    output = df.copy()
    embeddings, model_metadata = embed_texts(summaries, config=resolved_config, entity_type=entity_type)
    output["embedding"] = embeddings
    result = output[id_cols + ["embedding"]].copy()
    if return_metadata:
        metadata_payload = {
            "package": package_metadata(),
            "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
            "model_metadata": {
                "embed_for_matching": model_metadata,
            },
        }
        return result, metadata_payload
    return result

def embed_texts(
    texts: list[str],
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    entity_type: Literal["patient", "trial"] | None = None,
) -> tuple[list[list[float]], dict]:
    """Embed summary strings in input order and return vectors plus model metadata.

    Accepts patient or trial text without identifiers or DataFrames. Uses the
    default preset when config is omitted and reuses the cached inference model.
    ``entity_type`` selects the TrialSpace model's patient or cohort prompt when
    it has them. Model metadata includes model_name and model_sha.
    """
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    embedding_config = dict(getattr(resolved_config, "embedding", {}))
    return generate_embeddings(
        texts,
        embedding_config=embedding_config,
        model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved_config.model_metadata_cache_dir,
        entity_type=entity_type,
    )

docs.title: Large encoding jobs: several GPUs or vLLM embedding servers
docs.text:
open_encoder(EncoderSettings(...)) encodes many texts at once and returns float32, L2-normalized NumPy vectors in input order. It is what the training repository mines with; embed_for_matching loads and encodes with the same functions on one device, its embedding configuration section giving the settings.

  • One device (devices=("cuda:0",)): the model's own encode.
  • Several devices (devices=("cuda:0", "cuda:1", ...)): one spawned worker process per device. The coordinator takes the model's own length order and deals out the batches a one-device run would form, so every text is encoded in the same batch and the vectors equal the one-device vectors on the same GPU type.
  • backend="openai": OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings servers (remote={"server_urls": [...]} or a server_urls_file registry). vLLM serves EmbeddingGemma 2 natively from version 0.32 (build_embedding_server_command gives vllm serve <model> --runner pooling ...; one server per GPU). The client prepends the prompt, truncates and tokenizes exactly as sentence-transformers does, sends token ids to the least-loaded server, and normalizes. vLLM's kernels and bf16 weights give vectors close to (about 0.999 cosine), not equal to, the local backends'.

encoder_identity(settings) names everything that changes the vectors (backend, model and revision, prompts, length, precision, batching) and no paths or devices; store it with the vectors and never mix vectors with different identities. TrialSpace's prompt profile is trialspace_contract.model_prompts("trialspace").

from matchminer_ai.embedding import EncoderSettings, open_encoder
from matchminer_ai.embedding.trialspace_contract import model_prompts

settings = EncoderSettings("google/embeddinggemma-2", revision="914f7f89142e33e77833254d9c9b90c3cef7303b",
                           devices=tuple(f"cuda:{i}" for i in range(8)), batch_size=32, max_seq_length=8192,
                           dtype="float32", autocast="bfloat16", prompts=model_prompts("trialspace"),
                           include_prompt_in_pooling=True, text_only=True)
with open_encoder(settings) as encoder:
    patients = encoder.encode(patient_key_texts, "patient_summary")

Exact search over such vectors in query batches, on one or more devices, is matchminer_ai.matching.retrieval.score_batches (every batch against every document, so the scores do not depend on the number of devices), with stable_top_k for index-order ties.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.embedding.encoder
docs.text:
Sentence-transformers encoding on one or more devices, or over vLLM embedding servers.

:func:open_encoder returns an encoder whose encode(texts, prompt_name) gives float32, L2-normalized vectors in input order:

  • one device: the model's own encode (it sorts the texts by length and encodes batches of batch_size);
  • several devices (devices=("cuda:0", "cuda:1", ...)): one worker process per device. The coordinator takes the model's own length order and deals out the same batches the one-device encoder would form, so every text is encoded in the same batch as on one device and the vectors match it (on the same GPU type);
  • backend="openai": OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings servers (vLLM >= 0.32 serves EmbeddingGemma 2 with vllm serve <model> --runner pooling; see :func:matchminer_ai.llm.vllm_server.build_embedding_server_command). The client applies the prompt and truncation exactly as sentence-transformers does, sends token ids, and normalizes; vLLM's kernels and bf16 weights give vectors close to (about 0.999 cosine), not equal to, the local backends'.

:func:encoder_identity names everything that changes the vectors and no paths, hosts or devices, so vectors made by different backends or settings are never mixed. Training's mining encodes with this module, and embed_for_matching loads and encodes with the same functions (one device), its embedding configuration section giving the settings.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EncoderSettings:
    """What is loaded and how it encodes.

    ``model`` is a Hub id or a local directory; ``model_identity`` replaces it in the identity (for a local
    checkpoint, the id of the stage that wrote it). ``prompts`` overrides or adds named prompts (for
    example the TrialSpace profile, ``trialspace_contract.model_prompts("trialspace")``). ``text_only``
    loads EmbeddingGemma 2 without its vision and audio towers. ``dtype`` sets the weights' precision and
    ``autocast`` the CUDA autocast precision; None keeps the model's and disables autocast.
    """

    model: str
    revision: str | None = None
    cache_dir: str | None = None
    devices: tuple[str, ...] = ("cpu",)
    batch_size: int = 32
    max_seq_length: int | None = None
    dtype: str | None = None
    autocast: str | None = None
    prompts: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    default_prompt_name: str | None = None
    include_prompt_in_pooling: bool | None = None
    text_only: bool = False
    model_identity: str | None = None
    backend: str = "sentence_transformers"
    # backend "openai": server_urls or server_urls_file (a {"servers": [{"url": ...}]} registry),
    # model_name (served name; default the first /v1/models entry), max_concurrent_per_server,
    # request_batch_size, request_timeout, max_retries, api_key_env.
    remote: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.backend not in ("sentence_transformers", "openai"):
            raise ValueError("Encoder backend must be sentence_transformers or openai")
        if self.batch_size < 1 or not self.devices:
            raise ValueError("Encoders need a positive batch size and at least one device")
        if self.dtype not in (None, "float32", "bfloat16") or self.autocast not in (None, "bfloat16"):
            raise ValueError("dtype must be float32 or bfloat16 and autocast bfloat16, or None")
        object.__setattr__(self, "devices", tuple(self.devices))

@contextmanager
def open_encoder(settings: EncoderSettings) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """An encoder for ``settings``: vLLM servers, several worker processes, or this process."""
    if settings.backend == "openai":
        encoder = OpenAIEmbeddingsEncoder(settings)
    elif len(settings.devices) > 1:
        encoder = MultiDeviceEncoder(settings)
    else:
        encoder = LocalEncoder(settings)
    try:
        yield encoder
    finally:
        encoder.close()

def encoder_identity(settings: EncoderSettings) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Everything that changes the vectors (backend, model, revision, prompts, length, precision, batching)."""
    identity = dict(implementation=IMPLEMENTATION, backend=settings.backend,
                    model=settings.model_identity or settings.model, revision=settings.revision,
                    max_seq_length=settings.max_seq_length, prompts=dict(sorted(settings.prompts.items())),
                    default_prompt_name=settings.default_prompt_name, text_only=settings.text_only)
    if settings.backend == "sentence_transformers":
        identity.update(batch_size=settings.batch_size, dtype=settings.dtype, autocast=settings.autocast,
                        include_prompt_in_pooling=settings.include_prompt_in_pooling)
    return identity

docs.title: matchminer_ai.matching.retrieval
docs.text:
Exact similarity search in query batches over one or more devices, with a stable top-k.

For normalized embeddings, score_batches yields cosine similarities of consecutive query batches against every document, in query order. Each device holds a copy of the documents and scores whole batches, so the scores do not depend on how many devices share the work. stable_top_k breaks ties by document index (training's mining has always selected this way). Selection policies on top of the scores (which documents a query may see, lexical or random extras) belong to the caller.

docs.text:
score_batches(queries, documents, *, batch_size: int = 128, devices: Sequence[str] = ('cpu',)) -> Iterator[tuple[int, np.ndarray]]

Yield (start, scores) for query rows start:start + batch_size: float32 queries @ documents.T.

Batches are spread over devices (for example ("cuda:0", "cuda:1")); a few run ahead of the consumer per device.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/matching/retrieval.py 
def score_batches(queries, documents, *, batch_size: int = 128,
                  devices: Sequence[str] = ("cpu",)) -> Iterator[tuple[int, np.ndarray]]:
    """Yield ``(start, scores)`` for query rows ``start:start + batch_size``: float32 ``queries @ documents.T``.

    Batches are spread over ``devices`` (for example ``("cuda:0", "cuda:1")``); a few run ahead of the
    consumer per device.
    """
    import torch

    if batch_size < 1 or not devices:
        raise ValueError("score_batches needs a positive batch size and at least one device")
    queries = np.asarray(queries, dtype=np.float32)
    documents = np.asarray(documents, dtype=np.float32)
    on = {device: torch.as_tensor(documents, device=device) for device in dict.fromkeys(devices)}
    starts = list(range(0, len(queries), batch_size))

    def score(number):
        device = devices[number % len(devices)]
        start = starts[number]
        q = torch.as_tensor(queries[start:start + batch_size], device=device)
        return start, (q @ on[device].T).cpu().numpy()

    window = 2 * len(devices)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(devices)) as pool:
        running = [pool.submit(score, number) for number in range(min(window, len(starts)))]
        for number in range(len(starts)):
            yield running[number].result()
            running[number] = None  # release the batch once yielded
            if number + window < len(starts):
                running.append(pool.submit(score, number + window))

def stable_top_k(scores, k: int) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the ``k`` highest scores, highest first; ties keep index order."""
    return np.argsort(-np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64), kind="stable")[:k].tolist()

docs.title: Exclusion Criteria
docs.text:
The decision model's boilerplate question (exclusion_criteria_check) and its LLM alternative (exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm) read boilerplate text only: the general requirements most cancer trials share, inclusion requirements as well as exclusions. Key criteria are the match-quality stage's. Each row is one candidate pair with:

  • patient_id;
  • cohort_trial_id (or historical space_trial_id or trial_id);
  • cohort_boilerplate_criteria from remove_boilerplate_criteria (or historical general_exclusion_criteria);
  • general_exclusion_criteria_evidence, the patient summary's boilerplate section (or a complete patient_summary, whose text after Other relevant history: is taken).

Cohorts from extract_cohorts need the boilerplate step (trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria) before this stage; see key and boilerplate criteria.

The decision model (match quality) answers one question about the patient's boilerplate section and the cohort's boilerplate criteria: Is this patient potentially eligible for this cohort after review of the patient's other relevant history and these boilerplate criteria? If the patient is potentially eligible, answer yes; if the patient is clearly ineligible, answer no. Yes means potentially eligible; no means the patient clearly fails at least one boilerplate criterion (clearly meets an exclusion or clearly does not meet an inclusion requirement); missing information and waitable washouts are not failures. exclusion_criteria_pass_probability is P(yes), exclusion_criteria_pass is P(yes) ≥ exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff (0.5), and exclusion_score is the probability of the predicted outcome (P(yes) for a pass, 1 − P(yes) for a fail). interpret_exclusion_criteria token offsets refer to the patient_boilerplate_summary and cohort_boilerplate_criteria sources. For a line-by-line check, see criteria check.

The LLM prompt (llm_exclusion_criteria.user.txt) asks whether the patient clearly fails any of the cohort's boilerplate criteria: clearly meets an exclusion or clearly does not meet an inclusion requirement. Missing or undocumented information is not a failure, nor is a requirement the patient could meet by waiting, such as a washout period. It returns llm_exclusion_criteria_pass (None when the answer cannot be parsed).

These are screening signals for human review, not eligibility determinations. The LLM check sends the patient's boilerplate section to the configured LLM endpoint; use only an endpoint authorized for that data.

def exclusion_criteria_check(
    matches: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    filter_excluded: bool = False,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """
    Evaluate with the decision model whether each candidate pair passes the boilerplate criteria.

    The decision model (:mod:`matchminer_ai.matching.decision_model`, configured by
    ``decision_model``) answers its boilerplate question about one state: the patient summary's
    boilerplate section and the cohort's boilerplate criteria (the general requirements most trials
    share, inclusion as well as exclusion; :func:`score_match_quality` handles the key criteria).
    **Yes means the patient is potentially eligible after review of these texts; no means the
    patient clearly fails at least one boilerplate criterion.** Missing information is not a
    failure.

    Parameters
    ----------
    matches : pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame of candidate patient–cohort pairs.

        Expected columns
        ----------------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id : str
            Cohort identifier (historical ``space_trial_id`` or ``trial_id`` is accepted).
        cohort_boilerplate_criteria : str
            The cohort's boilerplate criteria (historical ``general_exclusion_criteria`` is accepted).
        general_exclusion_criteria_evidence : str
            The patient summary's boilerplate section (or a complete ``patient_summary``, whose
            boilerplate section is taken).

    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        MMAI configuration: ``decision_model`` (the model) and ``exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff``
        (default 0.5). Uses default preset when omitted.
    filter_excluded : bool, default False
        If True, return only rows where ``exclusion_criteria_pass`` is True.
    return_metadata : bool, default False
        When True, also return a metadata dict containing the config snapshot
        and model metadata for this run.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        Derived output table containing:

        Columns
        -------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id, space_trial_id or trial_id : str
            The input's trial identifier.
        exclusion_criteria_pass_probability : float
            P(yes): the probability that the patient is potentially eligible, not clearly failing
            any boilerplate criterion.
        exclusion_score : float
            The probability of the predicted outcome: P(yes) for a pass, 1 - P(yes) for a fail.
        exclusion_criteria_pass : bool
            True when P(yes) is at least ``exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff``.
    tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        When return_metadata is True, returns the DataFrame plus metadata.
    """
    trial_id, _, _ = _pair_inputs(matches)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    cutoff = float(resolved_config.raw.get("exclusion_criteria", {}).get("pass_cutoff", 0.5))
    probabilities, model_metadata = _decide(matches, resolved_config)
    output = _result(matches, trial_id, probabilities, cutoff)
    if filter_excluded:
        output = output.loc[output["exclusion_criteria_pass"]].copy()
    output = output.reset_index(drop=True)
    if return_metadata:
        return output, {"package": package_metadata(), "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
                        "model_metadata": {"exclusion_criteria_check": model_metadata}}
    return output
