def interpret_exclusion_criteria(
    matches: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    top_k: int | None = 30,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Interpret specific boilerplate decisions with token attributions.

    Scores each pair as :func:`exclusion_criteria_check` does, then runs one gradient-enabled
    forward pass per pair: gradient times input embedding for the boilerplate question's
    yes-minus-no logit at its answer slot. Returned token offsets are relative to the patient's
    boilerplate section (``patient_boilerplate_summary`` source) and the cohort's boilerplate
    criteria (``cohort_boilerplate_criteria`` source). Positive normalized scores support the
    reported pass/fail decision; negative scores oppose it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    matches : pd.DataFrame
        One or more specific pairs with the same required input columns as
        :func:`exclusion_criteria_check`.
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        Configuration. Uses the default preset when omitted.
    top_k : int or None, default 30
        Retain the most important tokens per source field. Use ``None`` to
        return every retained input token.
    return_metadata : bool, default False
        Return the config snapshot and model metadata with the result.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        One row per input pair with the decision, ``token_attributions``, input
        ``attribution_coverage``, and caveat.
    tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        Result and reproducibility metadata when ``return_metadata`` is True.
    """
    trial_id, evidence, criteria = _pair_inputs(matches)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    cutoff = float(resolved_config.raw.get("exclusion_criteria", {}).get("pass_cutoff", 0.5))
    probabilities, model_metadata = _decide(matches, resolved_config)
    output = _result(matches, trial_id, probabilities, cutoff)
    question = {BOILERPLATE: boilerplate_question()}
    explanations = []
    for patient, cohort, passed in zip(evidence, criteria, output["exclusion_criteria_pass"], strict=True):
        state, ranges = boilerplate_state_with_ranges(patient, cohort)
        explanations.append(oriented(attribute_decision(state, question, BOILERPLATE, ranges, config=resolved_config,
                                                        top_k=top_k), bool(passed)))
    output["attribution_method"] = [item["method"] for item in explanations]
    output["attribution_target"] = ["exclusion_criteria_pass" if passed else "exclusion_criteria_fail"
                                    for passed in output["exclusion_criteria_pass"]]
    output["token_attributions"] = [item["token_attributions"] for item in explanations]
    output["attribution_coverage"] = [item["coverage"] for item in explanations]
    output["attribution_caveat"] = TOKEN_ATTRIBUTION_CAVEAT
    output = output.reset_index(drop=True)
    if return_metadata:
        return output, {"config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
                        "model_metadata": {"interpret_exclusion_criteria": model_metadata},
                        "interpretability": {"method": "gradient_x_input", "top_k_per_source": top_k}}
    return output

def exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm(
    matches: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: "MMAIConfig | None" = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """
    Evaluate a cohort's boilerplate criteria with the configured LLM prompt.

    The prompt (``llm_exclusion_criteria.prompt_file``; the training teacher's boilerplate-label
    prompt) asks whether the patient clearly fails any of the cohort's boilerplate criteria,
    inclusion requirements as well as exclusions, from the patient summary's boilerplate section.

    Parameters
    ----------
    matches : pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame of candidate patient–cohort pairs.

        Expected columns
        ----------------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id : str
            Cohort identifier (historical ``space_trial_id`` or ``trial_id`` is accepted).
        cohort_boilerplate_criteria : str
            The cohort's boilerplate criteria (historical ``general_exclusion_criteria`` is accepted).
        general_exclusion_criteria_evidence : str
            The patient summary's boilerplate section (or a complete ``patient_summary``, whose
            boilerplate section is taken).

    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        MMAI configuration containing LLM exclusion checker settings.
        Uses default preset when omitted.
    return_metadata : bool, default False
        When True, also return a metadata dict containing the config snapshot
        and model metadata for this run.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        Derived output table containing:

        Columns
        -------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id, space_trial_id or trial_id : str
            The input's trial identifier.
        llm_exclusion_criteria_pass : bool | None
            Whether the LLM judged that the patient passes exclusion criteria,
            or None when parsing failed.
        Debug Columns
        -------------
        llm_exclusion_criteria_answer_text : str
            Text the package treated as the LLM answer and used for parsing.
            Included only when debug_mode is true.
        llm_exclusion_criteria_reasoning_text : str
            Optional separate reasoning trace returned by the backend or
            extracted by the configured reasoning parser. Included only when
            debug_mode is true.
        llm_exclusion_criteria_parse_status : str
            Whether the package could parse the answer text. Values are
            ``parsed``, ``parsed_fallback``, or ``parse_failed``. Included only
            when debug_mode is true.
    tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        When return_metadata is True, returns the DataFrame plus metadata.
    """
    from .exclusion_check import _pair_inputs

    trial_id, evidence, criteria = _pair_inputs(matches)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    llm_config = dict(resolved_config.llm_exclusion_criteria)
    prompt_template = _load_prompt_template(str(llm_config["prompt_file"]).strip())
    messages_list = [
        _build_messages(prompt_template.format(patient_boilerplate=patient, trial_boilerplate=cohort))
        for patient, cohort in zip(evidence, criteria, strict=True)
    ]
    responses, reasonings, model_metadata = _run_llm_check(
        matches,
        config=resolved_config,
        section_name="llm_exclusion_criteria",
        messages_list=messages_list,
    )
    parsed = [_parse_exclusion_result(response) for response in responses]

    output = matches[["patient_id", trial_id]].copy()
    output["llm_exclusion_criteria_pass"] = [passed for passed, _ in parsed]
    if resolved_config.debug_mode:
        output["llm_exclusion_criteria_answer_text"] = responses
        output["llm_exclusion_criteria_reasoning_text"] = reasonings
        output["llm_exclusion_criteria_parse_status"] = [
            parse_status for _, parse_status in parsed
        ]
    output = output.reset_index(drop=True)

    if return_metadata:
        metadata_payload = {
            "package": package_metadata(),
            "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
            "model_metadata": {
                "exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm": model_metadata,
            },
        }
        return output, metadata_payload
    return output

docs.title: Structured Clinical Extraction
docs.text:
Research abstraction aids

These records are research data-abstraction aids. They are not clinical documentation, and every item needs human review against the source note before it is used. A missing item does not mean that something was not done. The note text reaches the configured LLM endpoint, so the endpoint must be appropriate for the data.

Two stages turn clinical notes into structured, evidence-linked records that use one data model:

Function One record per Content extract_document_records note The document type; for an imaging report the study that produced it; for a pathology report the procedure that produced its specimen; and the diagnoses, biomarkers, treatments, disease assessments, performance status, lab tests and counseling the note states. extract_patient_records patient Cancer diagnoses with site, histology, dates and stage; biomarkers; treatment lines and regimens with agents, dates and best response; tissue procedures; imaging history; lab tests; counseling, screenings and referrals; key dated events.

Both accept the note table summarize_patients takes: patient_id, note_text and note_date, plus optional note_id (unique) and note_type (the record system's label, shown to the model as a hint). Without note_id, each note gets a stable id from a hash of its patient, date, type and text, and exact duplicate notes are kept once. Dates become YYYY-MM-DD; a missing date stays unknown.

from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.patients import (
    extract_document_records,
    extract_patient_records,
    extraction_items,
)

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote["enabled"] = True
config.remote["server_urls"] = ["http://localhost:8000/v1"]

patients = extract_patient_records(notes, config=config, checkpoint_dir="ckpt/patients")
documents = extract_document_records(
    notes, config=config, patient_records=patients, checkpoint_dir="ckpt/documents"
)
items = extraction_items(documents)  # one row per extracted item

The two stages are independent. Passing patient_records to the document stage lists each patient's known diagnoses (D1, D2, ...) in its prompts so that items can name the cancer they concern (cancer_ids), as the lung abstraction this generalizes did after its patient pass.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
Every record carries schema_version (mmai-clinical-extraction-v2; v1 records, built before lab tests and counseling were added on 2026-11-17, have neither list), its level, patient_id, the selected extensions, and items: one list per item type. A document record adds note_id, note_date, note_type, document_type and document_type_text; a patient record adds note_count, first_note_date, last_note_date, chunk_count and failed_chunks, and gives each item an item_id (D1, B2, T3, ...). record_json_schema(level) returns the JSON schema of a record.

Every item has:

  • item_type and its fields (below). Text the note does not state is "", a choice it does not settle is not_stated (where the vocabulary has it), a list is [], and an integer is 0.
  • dates as {"value": "2024-03", "precision": "month", "source": ...}, with precision day, month, year or unknown (value null). source is document_text (written in the note), note_date (a report's own study or specimen whose date is not written gets the note's date), evidence_note_date (a performed patient-level study or procedure without a written date gets the date of the earliest note quoted: it was done on or before then) or unknown.
  • evidence: one to four exact quotes, each with the note's note_id, note_date and the start/end character offsets of the quote in the note's own text. The model writes the quotes; code locates each one in the note and keeps the note's own text at that span. The words must occur in order; only layout may differ (whitespace and line breaks, letter case, markdown emphasis and heading marks, list markers at the start of a line, typographic quotes and dashes), which a JSON answer cannot reproduce reliably. A paraphrased or invented quote is rejected.

docs.title: Item types
docs.text:
List Item type Levels Fields imaging_studies imaging_study both modality, modality_text, body_regions, body_site_text, contrast, tracer, study_date procedures procedure both procedure_type, procedure_group (derived), procedure_text, image_guidance, specimen_site, laterality, procedure_date, specimen_result, result_text diagnoses diagnosis both primary_site, histology, grade, diagnosis_date, stage_group, t_category, n_category, m_category, stage_basis, staging_system, extent_at_diagnosis biomarkers biomarker both biomarker, biomarker_type, result, alteration, value, method, assay_name, sample_type, origin, test_date treatments treatment both treatment_type, regimen, agents, site, setting, line_of_therapy, treatment_status, start_date, end_date, best_response, end_reason, toxicities disease_assessments disease_assessment document disease_status, disease_sites performance_status performance_status document scale (ecog, karnofsky), score lab_tests lab_test both lab_test (cbc, cmp, bmp, liver_function, renal_function, ldh, coagulation, pregnancy_test, ... other), lab_text, result_text, result_flag, collection_date counseling counseling both topic (smoking_cessation, genetic_counseling, fertility, psychosocial_distress, palliative_care, lymphedema, ... other), topic_text, counseling_kind (counseling, discussion, screening, referral, consultation), provider, details, counseling_date events event patient event_type, description, event_date

Lab tests cover blood, urine and other fluid tests, one item per test or panel per collection; serum tumor markers that follow a cancer (CEA, CA 19-9, PSA) stay biomarkers. Counseling covers counseling, care discussions, supportive-care screenings (such as distress or lymphedema screening) and referrals, one item per topic per encounter.

Imaging studies, procedures, lab tests and counseling also record how they occurred. In a document record, relation is this_report (the study an imaging report reads, or the procedure that produced the specimen a pathology report examines), previously_performed (an earlier or outside study or procedure the note says was done) or planned; source_of_document is true for this_report. In both levels status is performed or planned. Procedures, biomarkers, treatments and events carry cancer_ids (patient level, and document level when patient_records is given). Disease assessments and performance status are properties of one note, so they are document-level only, as in the lung abstraction; their table date is the note date.

An imaging report's record must include the study it reads, and a pathology report's the procedure that produced its specimens (relation this_report), or the answer is retried. Neither was extracted by the lung abstraction: it used the record system's scan type only to select reports, and it recorded a specimen's procedure only as biopsy or surgical excision.

docs.title: Controlled vocabularies
docs.text:
Each choice field has a closed vocabulary (matchminer_ai.patients.extraction.vocabulary) that is rendered into the prompt and enforced by the JSON schema. Most end with other (whose companion text field must then name the value) and not_stated.

Vocabulary Codes Document type imaging_report, pathology_report, molecular_report, laboratory_report, clinic_note, hospital_note, procedure_note, radiation_oncology_note, treatment_record, other Imaging modality ct, mri, pet_ct, pet_mri, pet, xray, ultrasound, echocardiography, mammography, bone_scan, nuclear_medicine_other, fluoroscopy, bone_densitometry, other, not_stated Body region (list) brain, head_and_neck, spine, chest, breast, heart, abdomen, pelvis, extremity, whole_body, other Contrast with_contrast, without_contrast, with_and_without_contrast, not_stated Pathology procedure (group) histologic biopsy: core_needle_biopsy, needle_biopsy_not_specified, excisional_biopsy, incisional_biopsy, punch_or_shave_biopsy, endoscopic_biopsy, bronchoscopic_biopsy, mediastinoscopy, sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy, biopsy_not_specified; aspiration or cytology: fine_needle_aspiration, ebus_tbna, eus_fna, fluid_cytology, brushing_or_washing_cytology; surgical resection: surgical_resection, lymph_node_dissection; bone_marrow_biopsy; peripheral_blood; other; not_stated Image guidance ct, ultrasound, mri, fluoroscopy, stereotactic, none, not_stated Specimen result malignant, suspicious_or_atypical, negative, nondiagnostic, not_stated Biomarker type / result / method / sample / origin mutation, fusion_or_rearrangement, copy_number_change, protein_expression, genomic_signature, serum_tumor_marker, cytogenetic, other / positive, negative, equivocal, indeterminate, not_stated / ngs, pcr, fish, ihc, karyotype, flow_cytometry, serum_assay, other, not_stated / tissue, plasma, blood, bone_marrow, other, not_stated / somatic, germline, not_stated Treatment type / status / setting / best response systemic_therapy, surgery, radiation_therapy, local_therapy, stem_cell_transplant, other / planned, ongoing, completed, discontinued, not_stated / neoadjuvant, adjuvant, definitive, advanced_or_metastatic, maintenance, not_stated / complete_response, partial_response, stable_disease, mixed_response, progressive_disease, not_evaluable, not_stated Disease status no_evidence_of_disease, response, stable, mixed, progression, indeterminate Event type initial_diagnosis, recurrence, progression, new_metastasis, remission, hospitalization, hospice_enrollment, death, clinical_trial_enrollment, other

Sites, histologies, stages, regimens and biomarker names are text as written; they are not normalized. With ncit_agent_codes: true, each treatment also gets agents_ncit: every agent's NCIt concept from the bundled NCIt snapshot (exact name or synonym, then the snapshot's spelling rules), or nulls.

docs.title: Querying records
docs.text:
extraction_items flattens document or patient records to one row per item with the same columns at both levels: patient_id, level, note_id, note_date, document_type, item_type, item_id, a uniform date, date_precision and date_source (the item's primary date, or the note date for a document's assessments), every item field (a date field x becomes x, x_precision and x_source), evidence and the complete item. Questions a workup review asks become DataFrame filters:

import pandas as pd

items = extraction_items(documents)
studies = items[(items.item_type == "imaging_study") & (items.status == "performed")]
ct_chest = studies[(studies.modality == "ct")
                   & studies.body_regions.map(lambda regions: "chest" in regions)]
reference = pd.Timestamp("2024-04-01")
recent = ct_chest[(pd.to_datetime(ct_chest.date) <= reference)
                  & (pd.to_datetime(ct_chest.date) >= reference - pd.Timedelta(days=30))
                  & (ct_chest.date_precision == "day")]

procedures = items[items.item_type == "procedure"]
core_biopsies = procedures[procedures.procedure_type == "core_needle_biopsy"]
any_histology = procedures[procedures.procedure_group == "histologic_biopsy"]

Filter by item_type first: fields of other item types are missing in those rows. A month- or year-precision date is not a day; a query must decide how to treat it, and an undated study mentioned in a note (previously_performed with an unknown date) was done on or before that note's date. These are documentation signals for review, not determinations that a test was or was not done. Extraction-Based Workup Checks compile guideline workup requirements into declarative queries that apply these rules, with deduplication of studies documented in several notes, in code.

docs.title: Validation, retries and failures
docs.text:
Each request's answer is decoded under its JSON schema when the remote backend is enabled and structured_outputs is on, then validated in code: field types and vocabularies, other companions, dates, ids, cancer_ids, the report's own study or procedure, and every quote. A failed answer is retried with its problems named (the model revises its rejected answer when it was complete JSON), up to max_attempts, then once with thinking off (reasoning_off_fallback). When the last attempt's only problems are quotes not found in the note, the items left without a found quote are dropped and counted (partial); any other problem on the last attempt fails the note (document level) or skips the chunk (patient level, listed in failed_chunks). A request that fails in transport fails the note, or stops the patient so that a rerun resumes at that chunk.

Requests are long: Nemotron 3.5 Super often reasons for 10,000-15,000 tokens before an answer, and a patient chunk's answer adds its quotes. Set remote.request_timeout (600 seconds in the default preset) to cover a whole completion on a busy server, for example 7,200 seconds; the shared endpoint pool retries a timed-out request from the start, so a timeout shorter than a completion never finishes.

Returned DataFrames have extraction_status (complete, partial or failed), error, item_count and the record dict (None when failed). return_metadata=True adds the schema version, prompt and response-schema hashes, extensions, model metadata and every request's attempts (finish reason and problem codes, without note text; answers and reasoning only in debug mode). return_qc=True adds failed, partial and truncated counts.

docs.title: Patient-level chunking
docs.text: A patient's notes are read in date order, packed into chunks of patient_extraction.chunk_tokens tokens (a longer note is split with chunk_overlap_tokens overlap), as serial summarization reads them, but without sentence deduplication, so quotes stay exact. Each chunk's request shows the record so far (items with their ids, fields and the numbers of the notes that support them) and returns only the chunk's new and changed items; code merges them, adding each update's evidence to the item's earlier evidence. The lung abstraction instead asked for the whole running JSON again on every chunk, so its cost grew with the square of the record's length, and a later answer could silently drop an item. A chunk whose prompt, with the output reserve, would exceed context_tokens fails the patient rather than being truncated.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text: With checkpoint_dir, the document stage appends each finished note to document_records.jsonl and the patient stage saves each patient after every chunk under patient_records/ (files named by a hash of the patient id). A rerun with unchanged notes, context and extraction contract (schema version, prompt, field guide, extensions and response schema) reuses complete and partial results and retries the rest. Checkpoints hold patient-derived text.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text: Disease-specific item types and prompt guidance are added by extensions, selected by name in document_extraction.extensions and patient_extraction.extensions, without changing the core model. The packaged thoracic extension adds a smoking_history item (smoking_status, pack_years, quit_date) and the thoracic guidance of the lung abstraction: histology and biomarker examples, lobe and nodal-station sites, thoracic operations and EBUS-TBNA. New extensions are registered with register_extension(Extension(name, description, item_types, guidance)); their item types must not reuse a core name, list key or id prefix.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ItemType:
    """One kind of extracted item.

    ``key`` is the record's list of these items and ``name`` one item's
    ``item_type``. ``levels`` are the record levels that extract it.
    ``occurrence`` items (imaging studies, procedures) say how they relate to
    the document (``relation``) or, at the patient level, whether they were
    performed or planned (``status``). ``linkable_levels`` are the levels whose
    items carry ``cancer_ids``: the patient-level ``D`` ids of the diagnoses
    they concern. ``primary_date`` names the field that dates an item for
    timeline queries (None: the document's note date). ``check`` adds
    item-specific validation and returns problem messages.
    """

    name: str
    key: str
    id_prefix: str
    description: str
    fields: tuple[Field, ...]
    levels: frozenset[str]
    occurrence: bool = False
    linkable_levels: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    primary_date: str | None = None
    guidance: str = ""
    check: Callable[[dict], list[str]] | None = None
    max_items: int = 64

    def __post_init__(self):
        names = [f.name for f in self.fields]
        reserved = {"item_id", "item_type", "relation", "status", "cancer_ids",
                    "evidence", "source_of_document"}
        if len(set(names)) != len(names) or reserved & set(names):
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: duplicate or reserved field names")
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{1,3}", self.id_prefix):
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: id_prefix must be 1-3 capital letters")
        if not set(self.levels) <= set(LEVELS) or not self.levels:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: levels must be a nonempty subset of {LEVELS}")
        for item_field in self.fields:
            if item_field.other_text is not None and item_field.other_text not in names:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.name}.{item_field.name}: unknown other_text field")
        if self.primary_date is not None and self.primary_date not in names:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: unknown primary_date field")

    def field(self, name: str) -> Field:
        return next(f for f in self.fields if f.name == name)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Vocabulary:
    """A closed list of codes.

    ``other`` names the escape code whose field needs a free-text value, and
    ``unknown`` the code a document that does not say uses (None when the
    vocabulary has no such code, as for list-valued fields whose empty list
    means "not stated").
    """

    name: str
    description: str
    terms: tuple[Term, ...]
    other: str | None = "other"
    unknown: str | None = "not_stated"

    def __post_init__(self):
        codes = [term.code for term in self.terms]
        if len(set(codes)) != len(codes):
            raise ValueError(f"Vocabulary {self.name} repeats a code")
        for special in (self.other, self.unknown):
            if special is not None and special not in codes:
                raise ValueError(f"Vocabulary {self.name} lacks its {special} code")

    @property
    def codes(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(term.code for term in self.terms)

    def group(self, code: str) -> str | None:
        """The coarser group of ``code`` (None when the vocabulary has none)."""
        for term in self.terms:
            if term.code == code:
                return term.group
        raise KeyError(f"{code!r} is not a {self.name} code")

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """The codes and their meanings, one per line, for a prompt."""
        return "\n".join(f"      {t.code}: {t.description}" for t in self.terms)

def extract_document_records(
    notes: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    patient_records: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    checkpoint_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    return_qc: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple:
    """Extract one structured record from each clinical note.

    A research abstraction aid: records need human review and are not clinical
    documentation. Each note is one LLM request with the settings of
    ``config.document_extraction``; the answer is decoded under the record's JSON
    schema (remote backends with ``structured_outputs``), validated, and every
    evidence quote is located in the note's own text. An answer that fails is
    retried with the problems named (``max_attempts``, then once with thinking
    off when ``reasoning_off_fallback`` is on). When the last attempt's only
    problems are quotes not found in the note, the items left without any found
    quote are dropped and the record is ``partial``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    notes : pd.DataFrame
        One row per note: ``patient_id``, ``note_text``, ``note_date`` (missing
        dates stay unknown) and optionally ``note_id`` (unique) and
        ``note_type`` (the record system's label, shown to the model as a hint).
        Without ``note_id`` each note gets a stable id from a hash of its
        patient, date, type and text.
    patient_records : pd.DataFrame, optional
        Output of :func:`extract_patient_records`. Its diagnoses are listed in
        each prompt so that items can name the cancers they concern
        (``cancer_ids``), as the lung abstraction did after its patient pass.
    checkpoint_dir : path, optional
        Each finished document is appended to ``document_records.jsonl`` there;
        a rerun reuses complete and partial records whose note, context and
        extraction contract are unchanged and retries failed ones. The file
        holds patient-derived text: keep it where the notes may be kept.
    return_metadata, return_qc : bool
        Also return a metadata dict (schema version, prompt and schema hashes,
        model metadata, per-document attempts) and a QC report.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Called as ``progress_callback(finished_notes, total_notes)`` before the
        first request and then every few seconds while requests run.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        One row per note with text, in patient and date order:
        ``patient_id``, ``note_id``, ``note_date``, ``note_type``,
        ``document_type``, ``extraction_status`` (``complete``, ``partial`` or
        ``failed``), ``error``, ``item_count`` and ``record`` (the record dict;
        None when failed). :func:`extraction_items` flattens the records to one
        row per item.
    """
    resolved = config or load_default_preset()
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None.")
    frame, counts = normalize_notes(notes)
    extensions = resolve_extensions((getattr(resolved, SECTION, None) or {}).get("extensions") or [])
    extra_types = extension_item_types(extensions)
    item_types = item_types_for("document", extra_types)
    linking = patient_records is not None
    cancers = known_cancers(patient_records) if linking else {}
    schema = document_response_schema(extra_types, linking=linking)
    settings = section_settings(resolved, SECTION, "clinical_document_record", schema)
    template = load_prompt_text(PROMPT_FILE)
    guide = render_field_guide("document", extra_types, linking=linking)
    guidance = extension_guidance(extensions)
    limit = settings.values.get("max_document_characters", 200000)
    if type(limit) is not int or limit < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{SECTION}.max_document_characters must be a positive integer")
    ncit_resource = settings.values.get(
        "ncit_resource", resolved.good_option_catalog.get("ncit_resource", "Thesaurus_26.07d.FLAT.zip")
    )
    contract = digest({
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION, "template": template, "guide": guide,
        "guidance": guidance, "schema": schema, "ncit": settings.ncit_agent_codes,
    })
    debug = resolved.debug_mode

    notes_list = [
        {"patient_id": r.patient_id, "note_id": r.note_id, "note_date": r.note_date,
         "note_type": r.note_type, "text": r.note_text}
        for r in frame.itertuples(index=False)
    ]
    contexts = {
        n["note_id"]: linking_block(cancers.get(n["patient_id"], [])) if linking else ""
        for n in notes_list
    }
    inputs = {
        n["note_id"]: digest([n["patient_id"], n["note_date"], n["note_type"], n["text"],
                              contexts[n["note_id"]]])
        for n in notes_list
    }
    path = Path(checkpoint_dir) / CHECKPOINT_FILE if checkpoint_dir is not None else None
    saved: dict[str, dict] = {}
    if path is not None and path.exists():
        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            entry = json.loads(line)
            if (
                entry.get("contract_sha256") == contract
                and entry.get("input_sha256") == inputs.get(entry.get("note_id"))
                and entry.get("extraction_status") in {"complete", "partial"}
            ):
                saved[entry["note_id"]] = entry

    outcomes: dict[str, dict] = {}
    attempts: dict[str, list] = {}
    pending = []
    for note in notes_list:
        note_id = note["note_id"]
        if note_id in saved:
            outcomes[note_id] = saved[note_id]
            attempts[note_id] = saved[note_id].get("attempts", [])
        elif len(note["text"]) > limit:
            outcomes[note_id] = {"extraction_status": "failed", "record": None,
                                 "error": f"document exceeds {SECTION}.max_document_characters"}
        else:
            pending.append(note)
    reused = len(saved)
    by_id = {n["note_id"]: n for n in notes_list}

    def messages(note):
        content = fill(template, {
            "field_guide": guide,
            "extension_guidance": f"\n{guidance}\n" if guidance else "",
            "linking": f"\n{contexts[note['note_id']]}" if contexts[note["note_id"]] else "",
            "note_date": note["note_date"] or "unknown",
            "note_type": note["note_type"] or "none",
            "note_text": note["text"],
        })
        return [{"role": "user", "content": content}]

    finished: list[str] = []

    def write(note_ids):
        if path is None or not note_ids:
            return
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
        with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for note_id in note_ids:
                outcome = outcomes[note_id]
                handle.write(json.dumps({
                    "note_id": note_id, "patient_id": by_id[note_id]["patient_id"],
                    "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION, "contract_sha256": contract,
                    "input_sha256": inputs[note_id], **outcome,
                    "attempts": attempts.get(note_id, []), "completed_at": now,
                }, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    model_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if pending:
        chunk_size, chunks_in_flight = settings.queue_shape
        queue = RequestQueue(
            get_llm_backend(resolved), settings.runtimes, chunk_size=chunk_size,
            chunks_in_flight=chunks_in_flight,
            model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved.model_metadata_cache_dir,
        )
        # Prompts are built as requests are sent, so a large run never holds
        # every rendered prompt at once.
        waiting = iter(pending)

        def feed():
            note = next(waiting, None)
            if note is not None:
                original = messages(note)
                queue.add((note["note_id"], 1, original), original, "main")

        for _ in range(2 * chunk_size * chunks_in_flight):
            feed()

        def record(item, answer, reasoning, finish_reason, provenance):
            note_id, attempt, original = item
            note = by_id[note_id]
            group = attempt_group(attempt, settings)
            entry = attempt_entry(attempt, group, finish_reason, provenance, debug=debug,
                                  answer=answer, reasoning=reasoning)
            attempts.setdefault(note_id, []).append(entry)
            if finish_reason == "error":
                entry["error"] = "request failed"
                outcomes[note_id] = {"extraction_status": "failed", "record": None,
                                     "error": "the LLM request failed after its transport retries"}
                finished.append(note_id)
                feed()
                return
            final = attempt >= settings.total_attempts
            try:
                value = parse_answer(answer, finish_reason)
            except ValueError as exc:
                check, error = None, str(exc)
            else:
                check, error = check_document_answer(
                    value, note, item_types, linking=linking,
                    known_ids={c["item_id"] for c in cancers.get(note["patient_id"], [])},
                ), None
            problems = [] if check is None else check.problems
            if error is None and not problems:
                status = "complete"
            elif error is None and final and not check.structural:
                status = "partial"
            else:
                entry["problems"] = [error] if error else [p.code for p in problems]
                if not final:
                    queue.add((note_id, attempt + 1, original),
                              retry_messages(original, answer, check is not None, problems, error),
                              attempt_group(attempt + 1, settings))
                    return
                outcomes[note_id] = {"extraction_status": "failed", "record": None,
                                     "error": "no valid answer after every attempt: "
                                     + "; ".join(entry["problems"][:5])}
                finished.append(note_id)
                feed()
                return
            built = build_document_record(note, value, check, item_types, extensions)
            if settings.ncit_agent_codes:
                add_ncit_codes(built, ncit_resource)
            outcome = {"extraction_status": status, "record": built, "error": None}
            if status == "partial":
                entry["problems"] = [p.code for p in check.grounding]
                outcome["dropped_items"] = check.dropped
                outcome["dropped_quotes"] = len(check.grounding)
            outcomes[note_id] = outcome
            finished.append(note_id)
            feed()

        def flush():
            write(finished)
            finished.clear()
            if progress_callback is not None:
                progress_callback(len(outcomes), len(notes_list))

        if progress_callback is not None:
            progress_callback(len(outcomes), len(notes_list))
        logger.info("Extracting document records for %d notes.", len(pending))
        model_metadata = queue.run(record, progress=flush)

    rows = []
    for note in notes_list:
        outcome = outcomes[note["note_id"]]
        built = outcome.get("record")
        rows.append({
            "patient_id": note["patient_id"], "note_id": note["note_id"],
            "note_date": note["note_date"], "note_type": note["note_type"],
            "document_type": built["document_type"] if built else None,
            "extraction_status": outcome["extraction_status"], "error": outcome.get("error"),
            "item_count": sum(map(len, built["items"].values())) if built else 0,
            "record": built,
        })
    result = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=DOCUMENT_COLUMNS)
    statuses = result.set_index("note_id").extraction_status if len(result) else pd.Series(dtype=str)
    metadata = {
        "package": package_metadata(),
        "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved),
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "contract_sha256": contract,
        "prompt_sha256": digest(template),
        "response_schema_sha256": digest(schema),
        "extensions": [e.name for e in extensions],
        "linking": linking,
        "structured_outputs": settings.structured,
        "model_metadata": model_metadata,
        "counts": {
            "documents": len(notes_list), "reused": reused,
            **{s: int((statuses == s).sum()) for s in ("complete", "partial", "failed")},
            **counts,
        },
        "documents": {
            n["note_id"]: {
                "extraction_status": outcomes[n["note_id"]]["extraction_status"],
                "attempts": attempts.get(n["note_id"], []),
                **{k: outcomes[n["note_id"]][k] for k in ("dropped_items", "dropped_quotes")
                   if k in outcomes[n["note_id"]]},
            }
            for n in notes_list
        },
    }
    outputs: list[Any] = [result]
    if return_metadata:
        outputs.append(metadata)
    if return_qc:
        truncated = [i for i, a in attempts.items() if any(e["finish_reason"] == "length" for e in a)]
        outputs.append(pd.DataFrame(qc_rows([
            ("documents_failed_extraction", list(statuses[statuses == "failed"].index)),
            ("documents_partial_extraction", list(statuses[statuses == "partial"].index)),
            ("documents_truncated_llm_response", truncated),
        ], len(notes_list))))
    return outputs[0] if len(outputs) == 1 else tuple(outputs)

def extract_patient_records(
    notes: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    checkpoint_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    return_qc: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple:
    """Extract one structured record per patient from all of their notes.

    A research abstraction aid: records need human review and are not clinical
    documentation. Each patient's notes are read in date order in chunks of
    ``patient_extraction.chunk_tokens`` tokens (a longer note is split, with
    ``chunk_overlap_tokens`` overlap); each chunk is one LLM request that sees
    the record so far and returns the chunk's new and changed items (decoded
    under the JSON schema with remote ``structured_outputs``). Answers are
    validated and their evidence quotes located in the chunk's notes; a failed
    answer is retried with its problems named (``max_attempts``, then once with
    thinking off when ``reasoning_off_fallback`` is on). On the last attempt,
    items whose quotes are all missing from the notes are dropped; a chunk with
    no valid answer is skipped and listed in ``failed_chunks``. A request that
    fails in transport stops that patient (``failed``); a rerun with the same
    ``checkpoint_dir`` resumes it at that chunk.

    Parameters
    ----------
    notes : pd.DataFrame
        One row per note: ``patient_id``, ``note_text``, ``note_date``, and
        optionally ``note_id`` and ``note_type``, as for
        :func:`extract_document_records`.
    checkpoint_dir : path, optional
        Each patient's progress is saved after every chunk (one JSON file per
        patient under ``patient_records/``, named by a hash of the patient id);
        a rerun with unchanged notes and settings resumes where it stopped. The
        files hold patient-derived text.
    return_metadata, return_qc : bool
        Also return a metadata dict and a QC report.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Called as ``progress_callback(finished_chunks, total_chunks)`` before the
        first request and then every few seconds while requests run.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        One row per patient: ``patient_id``, ``extraction_status``
        (``complete``, ``partial`` when a chunk failed or ungrounded items were
        dropped, or ``failed``), ``error``, ``note_count``, ``chunk_count``,
        ``failed_chunks``, ``item_count`` and ``record`` (None when failed).
    """
    resolved = config or load_default_preset()
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None.")
    frame, counts = normalize_notes(notes)
    extensions = resolve_extensions((getattr(resolved, SECTION, None) or {}).get("extensions") or [])
    extra_types = extension_item_types(extensions)
    item_types = item_types_for("patient", extra_types)
    schema = patient_response_schema(extra_types)
    settings = section_settings(resolved, SECTION, "clinical_patient_record_update", schema)
    values = settings.values
    chunk_tokens = values.get("chunk_tokens", 40000)
    overlap = values.get("chunk_overlap_tokens", 500)
    if type(chunk_tokens) is not int or chunk_tokens < 256:
        raise ValueError(f"{SECTION}.chunk_tokens must be an integer of at least 256")
    if type(overlap) is not int or not 0 <= overlap < chunk_tokens // 2:
        raise ValueError(f"{SECTION}.chunk_overlap_tokens must be from 0 to half of chunk_tokens")
    context = values.get("context_tokens")
    if context is None:
        context = values.get("local", {}).get("engine", {}).get("max_model_len")
    max_tokens = int(settings.runtime["sampling_params"].get("max_tokens", 0))
    tokenizer_name = settings.runtime.get("tokenizer_name", settings.runtime["model_name"])
    template = load_prompt_text(PROMPT_FILE)
    guide = render_field_guide("patient", extra_types)
    guidance = extension_guidance(extensions)
    ncit_resource = values.get(
        "ncit_resource", resolved.good_option_catalog.get("ncit_resource", "Thesaurus_26.07d.FLAT.zip")
    )
    contract = digest({
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION, "template": template, "guide": guide,
        "guidance": guidance, "schema": schema,
    })
    debug = resolved.debug_mode
    folder = Path(checkpoint_dir) / CHECKPOINT_SUBDIR if checkpoint_dir is not None else None

    patients = {
        str(pid): patient_note_list(group)
        for pid, group in frame.groupby("patient_id", sort=False)
    }
    inputs = {
        pid: digest({
            "notes": [[n["note_id"], n["note_date"], n["note_type"], digest(n["text"])] for n in ns],
            "chunk_tokens": chunk_tokens, "overlap": overlap, "tokenizer": tokenizer_name,
        })
        for pid, ns in patients.items()
    }
    states: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    reused = 0
    for pid in patients:
        saved = None
        path = folder / f"{digest(pid)[:32]}.json" if folder is not None else None
        if path is not None and path.exists():
            candidate = read_json(path)
            if (
                candidate.get("patient_id") == pid
                and candidate.get("contract_sha256") == contract
                and candidate.get("input_sha256") == inputs[pid]
            ):
                saved = candidate
        if saved is not None:
            reused += saved["status"] in {"complete", "partial"}
            states[pid] = {
                "state": PatientState.from_json(item_types, saved["state"]),
                "next_chunk": saved["next_chunk"], "chunk_count": saved["chunk_count"],
                "failed_chunks": saved["failed_chunks"], "dropped": saved["dropped"],
                "attempts": saved["attempts"],
                "status": "running" if saved["status"] == "failed" else saved["status"],
                "error": None, "path": path,
            }
        else:
            states[pid] = {
                "state": PatientState(item_types), "next_chunk": 0, "chunk_count": None,
                "failed_chunks": [], "dropped": 0, "attempts": {}, "status": "running",
                "error": None, "path": path,
            }
    pending = [pid for pid, s in states.items() if s["status"] == "running"]
    chunks: dict[str, list[list[dict]]] = {}
    if pending:
        tokenizer = load_tokenizer(tokenizer_name)
        for pid in pending:
            chunks[pid] = pack_fragments(
                note_fragments(patients[pid], tokenizer, chunk_tokens - 64, overlap), chunk_tokens
            )
            states[pid]["chunk_count"] = len(chunks[pid])

    def save(pid):
        s = states[pid]
        if s["path"] is None:
            return
        atomic_json(s["path"], {
            "patient_id": pid, "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION, "contract_sha256": contract,
            "input_sha256": inputs[pid], "chunk_count": s["chunk_count"],
            "next_chunk": s["next_chunk"], "failed_chunks": s["failed_chunks"],
            "dropped": s["dropped"], "status": s["status"], "error": s["error"],
            "attempts": s["attempts"], "state": s["state"].to_json(),
        })

    def messages(pid):
        s = states[pid]
        index = s["next_chunk"]
        content = fill(template, {
            "field_guide": guide,
            "extension_guidance": f"\n{guidance}\n" if guidance else "",
            "record": s["state"].render(),
            "part": str(index + 1),
            "parts": str(s["chunk_count"]),
            "notes": render_chunk(chunks[pid][index]),
        })
        if context and max_tokens:
            prompt_tokens = len(tokenizer(content, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"])
            if prompt_tokens + max_tokens + 1024 > context:
                return None
        return [{"role": "user", "content": content}]

    def finish(pid):
        s = states[pid]
        s["status"] = "partial" if s["failed_chunks"] or s["dropped"] else "complete"
        save(pid)

    model_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if pending:
        chunk_size, chunks_in_flight = settings.queue_shape
        queue = RequestQueue(
            get_llm_backend(resolved), settings.runtimes, chunk_size=chunk_size,
            chunks_in_flight=chunks_in_flight,
            model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved.model_metadata_cache_dir,
        )

        def start(pid):
            """Queue the patient's next chunk, or finish the patient."""
            s = states[pid]
            if s["next_chunk"] >= s["chunk_count"]:
                finish(pid)
                return
            original = messages(pid)
            if original is None:
                s["status"] = "failed"
                s["error"] = (
                    f"part {s['next_chunk'] + 1}: the record so far and the notes exceed "
                    f"{SECTION}.context_tokens with the output reserve"
                )
                save(pid)
                return
            queue.add((pid, s["next_chunk"], 1, original), original, "main")

        def record(item, answer, reasoning, finish_reason, provenance):
            pid, index, attempt, original = item
            s = states[pid]
            group = attempt_group(attempt, settings)
            entry = attempt_entry(attempt, group, finish_reason, provenance, debug=debug,
                                  answer=answer, reasoning=reasoning)
            s["attempts"].setdefault(str(index), []).append(entry)
            if finish_reason == "error":
                s["status"] = "failed"
                s["error"] = f"part {index + 1}: the LLM request failed after its transport retries"
                save(pid)
                return
            final = attempt >= settings.total_attempts
            try:
                value = parse_answer(answer, finish_reason)
            except ValueError as exc:
                check, error = None, str(exc)
            else:
                check, error = check_patient_answer(value, chunks[pid][index], s["state"]), None
            problems = [] if check is None else check.problems
            accept = error is None and (not problems or (final and not check.structural))
            if not accept:
                entry["problems"] = [error] if error else [p.code for p in problems]
                if not final:
                    queue.add((pid, index, attempt + 1, original),
                              retry_messages(original, answer, check is not None, problems, error),
                              attempt_group(attempt + 1, settings))
                    return
                s["failed_chunks"].append(index)
            else:
                if problems:
                    entry["problems"] = [p.code for p in check.grounding]
                    s["dropped"] += len(check.dropped)
                s["state"].apply(check)
            s["next_chunk"] = index + 1
            save(pid)
            start(pid)

        def report():
            if progress_callback is not None:
                total = sum(s["chunk_count"] or 0 for s in states.values())
                finished = sum(
                    (s["chunk_count"] or 0) if s["status"] != "running" else s["next_chunk"]
                    for s in states.values()
                )
                progress_callback(finished, total)

        for pid in pending:
            start(pid)
        report()
        logger.info("Extracting patient records for %d patients.", len(pending))
        model_metadata = queue.run(record, progress=report)

    rows = []
    for pid, s in states.items():
        built = None
        if s["status"] != "failed":
            built = build_patient_record(
                pid, s["state"], patients[pid], chunk_count=s["chunk_count"],
                failed_chunks=s["failed_chunks"], extensions=extensions,
            )
            if settings.ncit_agent_codes:
                for item in built["items"].get("treatments", []):
                    item["agents_ncit"] = ncit_agent_codes(item["agents"], ncit_resource)
        rows.append({
            "patient_id": pid, "extraction_status": s["status"], "error": s["error"],
            "note_count": len(patients[pid]), "chunk_count": s["chunk_count"],
            "failed_chunks": list(s["failed_chunks"]),
            "item_count": sum(map(len, built["items"].values())) if built else 0,
            "record": built,
        })
    result = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=PATIENT_COLUMNS)
    statuses = {pid: s["status"] for pid, s in states.items()}
    metadata = {
        "package": package_metadata(),
        "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved),
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "contract_sha256": contract,
        "prompt_sha256": digest(template),
        "response_schema_sha256": digest(schema),
        "extensions": [e.name for e in extensions],
        "structured_outputs": settings.structured,
        "model_metadata": model_metadata,
        "counts": {
            "patients": len(states), "notes": int(len(frame)), "reused": reused,
            "chunks": sum(s["chunk_count"] or 0 for s in states.values()),
            **{k: sum(v == k for v in statuses.values()) for k in ("complete", "partial", "failed")},
            **counts,
        },
        "patients": {
            pid: {"extraction_status": s["status"], "attempts": s["attempts"],
                  "failed_chunks": s["failed_chunks"], "dropped_items": s["dropped"]}
            for pid, s in states.items()
        },
    }
    outputs: list[Any] = [result]
    if return_metadata:
        outputs.append(metadata)
    if return_qc:
        truncated = [
            pid for pid, s in states.items()
            if any(e["finish_reason"] == "length" for a in s["attempts"].values() for e in a)
        ]
        outputs.append(pd.DataFrame(qc_rows([
            ("patients_failed_extraction", [p for p, v in statuses.items() if v == "failed"]),
            ("patients_partial_extraction", [p for p, v in statuses.items() if v == "partial"]),
            ("patients_truncated_llm_response", truncated),
        ], len(states))))
    return outputs[0] if len(outputs) == 1 else tuple(outputs)

def extraction_items(records: pd.DataFrame | list[dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per extracted item of document or patient records.

    ``records`` is the output of :func:`extract_document_records` or
    :func:`extract_patient_records` (its ``record`` column), or a list of record
    dicts. Columns: ``ITEM_COLUMNS``, then every field of the items (a date field
    ``x`` becomes ``x``, ``x_precision`` and ``x_source``), ``evidence`` and the
    complete ``item`` dict. Failed records (None) contribute no rows.
    """
    if isinstance(records, pd.DataFrame):
        if "record" not in records:
            raise ValueError("records must have a record column")
        values = list(records["record"])
    else:
        values = list(records)
    primary = _primary_dates()
    rows = []
    for record in values:
        if not isinstance(record, dict):
            continue
        document = record["level"] == "document"
        for items in record["items"].values():
            for item in items:
                row = {
                    "patient_id": record["patient_id"],
                    "level": record["level"],
                    "note_id": record.get("note_id"),
                    "note_date": record.get("note_date"),
                    "document_type": record.get("document_type"),
                    "item_type": item["item_type"],
                    "item_id": item.get("item_id"),
                }
                date_field = primary.get(item["item_type"])
                if date_field is not None and isinstance(item.get(date_field), dict):
                    when = item[date_field]
                    row.update(date=when["value"], date_precision=when["precision"],
                               date_source=when["source"])
                elif document and record.get("note_date"):
                    row.update(date=record["note_date"], date_precision="day",
                               date_source="note_date")
                else:
                    row.update(date=None, date_precision="unknown", date_source="unknown")
                for name, value in item.items():
                    if name in {"item_type", "item_id", "evidence"}:
                        continue
                    if isinstance(value, dict) and {"value", "precision", "source"} <= set(value):
                        row[name] = value["value"]
                        row[f"{name}_precision"] = value["precision"]
                        row[f"{name}_source"] = value["source"]
                    else:
                        row[name] = value
                row["evidence"] = item["evidence"]
                row["item"] = item
                rows.append(row)
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if frame.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=[*ITEM_COLUMNS, "evidence", "item"])
    rest = [c for c in frame.columns if c not in ITEM_COLUMNS and c not in {"evidence", "item"}]
    return frame[[*ITEM_COLUMNS, *rest, "evidence", "item"]]

def record_json_schema(level: str, extra: Iterable[ItemType] = ()) -> dict:
    """The JSON schema of the records :func:`extract_document_records` (``level``
    ``"document"``) or :func:`extract_patient_records` (``"patient"``) return."""
    items = {
        t.key: {"type": "array", "items": item_record_schema(t, level)}
        for t in item_types_for(level, extra)
    }
    common = {
        "schema_version": {"const": SCHEMA_VERSION},
        "level": {"const": level},
        "patient_id": {"type": "string"},
        "extensions": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    }
    if level == "document":
        specific = {
            "note_id": {"type": "string"},
            "note_date": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
            "note_type": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
            "document_type": {"type": "string", "enum": list(v.DOCUMENT_TYPES.codes)},
            "document_type_text": {"type": "string"},
        }
    else:
        specific = {
            "note_count": {"type": "integer"},
            "first_note_date": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
            "last_note_date": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
            "chunk_count": {"type": "integer"},
            "failed_chunks": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer"}},
        }
    schema = _object({**common, **specific, "items": _object(items)})
    schema["$schema"] = "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
    schema["title"] = f"MatchMiner-AI {level} extraction record ({SCHEMA_VERSION})"
    return schema

def register_extension(extension: Extension, *, replace: bool = False) -> None:
    """Make ``extension`` selectable by name. Its item types must not reuse a core
    item type's name, list key or id prefix."""
    if extension.name in _REGISTRY and not replace:
        raise ValueError(f"Extension {extension.name!r} is already registered")
    core = {(t.name, t.key, t.id_prefix) for t in CORE_ITEM_TYPES}
    taken = {value for triple in core for value in triple}
    for item_type in extension.item_types:
        if {item_type.name, item_type.key, item_type.id_prefix} & taken:
            raise ValueError(f"{item_type.name} reuses a core item type's name, key or prefix")
    _REGISTRY[extension.name] = extension

docs.title: Good Option Catalog and Scoring
docs.text:
Good Option scoring is a patient-trial ranking signal, not an eligibility determination, response probability, or treatment recommendation. Research and patient scoring are separate, versioned stages.

Use the existing trial and matching stage namespaces:

from matchminer_ai.trials import build_good_option_catalog, load_good_option_catalog
from matchminer_ai.matching import check_good_options

# Public-only research stage; run once before patient scoring.
catalog = await build_good_option_catalog(nct_ids, "drug_catalog", config=config)

# candidate_pairs: patient_id, trial_id, cancer_history_summary
scores = check_good_options(candidate_pairs, catalog="drug_catalog", config=config)

check_good_options is the supported on-demand entry point; see On-demand check. score_good_options_with_llm is the lower-level scorer it wraps.

Patient summaries reach the configured LLM endpoint in LLM mode. Use an endpoint authorized for the sensitivity of the input. Catalog construction accepts NCT IDs only and never receives patient context.

The old matchminer_ai.good_options namespace and its submodules remain compatibility aliases. Trial research is implemented in trials/drug_catalog.py, trials/drug_research.py, and trials/drug_evidence.py; patient scoring is in matching/good_options.py.

docs.title: Build the patient-free catalog
docs.text:
build_good_option_catalog accepts a list of NCT IDs. It fetches each current ClinicalTrials.gov record, then uses the configured LLM to screen every DRUG, BIOLOGICAL, and COMBINATION_PRODUCT entry in its public trial and arm context. Only concrete named agents with direct anticancer treatment intent proceed to normalization and research. Antitumor medicines, biologics, cell/gene therapies, therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals, and genuine named anticancer comparators are retained; supportive/procedural medicines (including toxicity protection such as sodium thiosulfate and GVHD prophylaxis such as tacrolimus, unless the trial uses them as anticancer therapy), anesthetics, hemostatic agents, diagnostic tracers, devices, prevention-only agents, dosing/cohort labels, and unnamed standard-of-care placeholders are excluded fail-closed. The screen also resolves retained agents' investigational, uncertain, control, background (given the same way to every participant), or supportive roles; an agent given only in a comparator arm is control.

Each active entity is one agent named by its entry's own text (ctgov name, aliases, description, or the descriptions of its arms), or a component of a regimen named there: "Pemetrexed + Cisplatin /Carboplatin" becomes three agents, and a standard acronym such as FOLFIRI is expanded from knowledge into fluorouracil, leucovorin, and irinotecan, with the acronym listed in regimen_names. Agents are named by generic name (INN/USAN) or development code, never by a treatment category; an abbreviation, misspelling, or brand or shortened name that a generic name replaces ("LV", "5-Flurouracil") is listed in regimen_names the same way. A name of three or more letters and digits may be any part of the entry's text with spacing and punctuation removed; a two-character one ("SG", "LV") must be whole words of it, and a single character a whole field. Validation rejects agent names absent from the entry's text unless such a regimen or spelling is listed, and a regimen name listed as an agent; a listed regimen name the text does not contain is dropped with a logged count rather than failing the trial, and grounds no agent. A combination-spelled name or an ungrounded one gets one more attempt. With a remote backend the answer is decoded under INTERVENTION_SCREENING_JSON_SCHEMA (good_option_catalog.structured_outputs).

Every decision is retained in trial_intervention_screening.parquet, including the disposition, exclusion category, confidence, rationale, supported active-entity names, and expanded regimen names (regimen_names_json). Excluded entries never enter trial_drug_index.parquet, the unique-drug set, web queries, evidence retrieval, or synthesis. Retained identities are normalized with the bundled NCIt snapshot and deduplicated across the complete run. A name, its parenthetical-free form, or a parenthetical alone that is an exact NCIt name or synonym wins; otherwise NCIThesaurusDrugIndex.resolve_drug_name accepts a concept only when one rule finds exactly one: the same drug_name_key (case, spacing, separators, salt abbreviations, isotope notation, liposome word order), the same key without salts (the parent molecule when salts tie), route/dosage-form/biosimilar words moved or dropped, or one misspelled word of eight or more letters corrected. An unmatched drug's NAME: identity is a hash of its drug_name_key.

Each unique drug is researched once across mechanism and targets, human efficacy by tumor type and histology, biomarker prevalence, biomarker-directed human efficacy, and safety. The retriever uses bounded authoritative-source adapters plus full-text general-web documents. General-web queries include the explicit phrase cancer treatment to reduce name-collision results. Technical failures are retried with Retry-After or exponential backoff; successful empty results remain distinct from exhausted technical failures. Searches accept drug identity only and can never receive patient text.

Retrieval runs on three axes, and every passage records which one found it in query_scope.

The drug axis is the one above: the agent's own name and aliases.

The indication axis searches efficacy by tumor, biomarker prevalence, and biomarker-directed efficacy with a disease as a required clause. The same three facets run for both drug–disease and class–disease searches. The diseases come from the conditionsModule.conditions of the trials the drug appears in, which the build already fetches and stores, so the axis stays patient-free and cacheable. Without it the drug evidence never names the patient's cancer for most patient-drug pairs, and the first rubric criterion fires far less often when the disease is absent than when it is present. The axis is bounded as a whole by max_indication_passages_per_drug, interleaved across diseases, sources, and search facets, so it cannot swamp the agent's own corpus or let efficacy results crowd out prevalence findings. Research settings are part of the checkpoint fingerprint: catalogs built before the disease-specific prevalence searches need a fresh build to include them.

The class axis retrieves literature for the pharmacologic classes a drug belongs to, once per class rather than once per drug, so agents that share a class share a corpus. Classes are normalized to the bundled NCIt hierarchy. A class is an NCIt concept above a drug concept, in the Pharmacologic Substance branch, other than the fixed NCIT_UMBRELLA_CLASSES (Pharmacologic Substance, Antineoplastic Agent, Enzyme Inhibitor, and the like); the chemical-structure branch is not used. A classify stage between research and synthesis assigns an NCIt-matched drug every class above its concept in code. A local search of NCIt class names and synonyms against the drug's name, NCIt definition, and mechanism passages then finds up to class_candidate_limit candidate classes, and the LLM may add, by code, those the passages show the drug belongs to; an added class brings its NCIt ancestors, codes outside the candidates are rejected, the hierarchy is never removed, and an NCIt-classified drug with no candidates gets no LLM call. A drug NCIt leaves unclassified gets its classes from the LLM: candidates, or a new class (class_source="llm") only where none fits. The answer is decoded under DRUG_CLASS_JSON_SCHEMA with a remote backend. Only the matched drug's record and its candidates' names and short definitions enter the prompt, never the ontology.

An NCIt class's class_id is NCIT:<code>, its name NCIt's display or preferred name, and its aliases NCIt synonyms; its definition joins its corpus as a citable passage. A new class's identity is a hash of its normalized name, so "PD-L1 inhibitor" and "PD-L1 Inhibitors" resolve to one corpus, and a new name that spells an NCIt class is stored as that class. Assignments are stored in drug_classes.parquet, with ncit_code, class_source (ncit or llm), and assigned_by (ncit_hierarchy, llm_added_ncit, llm_added_ncit_ancestor, or llm_new); only LLM-chosen rows carry a basis, target, confidence, and support IDs. The corpus is stored in class_evidence/.

The configured LLM synthesizes the evidence ledger into structured facts with validated passage support IDs. A matched bundled NCIt definition is materialized as its own citable ledger passage rather than supplied as uncitable side context. Synthesis retains supported evidence across maturity levels—including ontology, preclinical, first-in-human, phase 1, ctgov, and mature clinical evidence—and labels its level without requiring approval, randomization, publication, or mature outcomes. Token-limited or blank final responses are retried, and the default synthesis completion budget is 100,000 tokens; if every ordinary attempt is token-limited, the final attempt disables thinking. The bundle stores two clean projections: a GoodOption summary without safety and a summary with safety (help_me_choose_summary, named for the removed Help Me Choose comparison). URLs, queries, source labels, ctgov metadata, and failure notices remain in the internal Parquet ledger and do not appear in the patient-bearing prompt.

Each class corpus is synthesized in its own call on its own budget, and stored in class_summaries.parquet. Keeping it separate is deliberate: the drugs that most need class evidence already fill the agent budget, so pooling the two would let a flood of same-class passages evict the agent's own data. Every fact carries a scope of agent or class, assigned in code from the corpus synthesis ran over rather than asked of the model, and both projections print it, so the rubric's instruction to prefer agent-specific evidence has something to bind to.

Catalog publication and its intermediate JSON checkpoints are atomic. By default, checkpoints are stored beside the requested catalog in <catalog>_checkpoints. Completed ctgov fetches, intervention screens, drug research, and drug syntheses are reused when the same build is restarted. Technically blocked fetches are retried. The checkpoint manifest fingerprints the NCT list, source/research settings, ontology version, the text of the catalog prompts, and teacher configuration; incompatible checkpoints fail explicitly instead of silently mixing evidence generations. Pass checkpoint_path to select another directory or reset_checkpoint=True to discard a recognized checkpoint bundle.

validate_good_option_catalog verifies file hashes, the catalog's compatibility_id (a fingerprint of those hashes), intervention-screen decisions, trial-drug references, terminal research states, and structured-fact evidence support. load_good_option_catalog validates by default.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
matchminer-ai-build-good-option-catalog builds and validates a complete catalog, drug classes included, against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

matchminer-ai-build-good-option-catalog \
  --nct-ids-file trial_ids.txt \
  --output data/no_phi/good_option_catalog \
  --server-url http://gpu-host:8001/v1

The served model is read from the endpoint's /v1/models, and its registered sampling profile (see LLM Server Helper) is applied to llm_good_option and every good_option_catalog.*_llm stage override. Checkpoints default to <output>_checkpoints; rerun the same command to resume.

Research requests to ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, and the NCBI E-utilities are paced per host across every subject; --host-requests-per-second HOST=RATE overrides a default, and --ncbi-api-key-file supplies an NCBI API key for the higher E-utilities rate (see good_option_catalog). The command prints the rates it uses and whether a key is set, never the key. --llm-batch-size sets how many trials are screened, and drugs classified, at once (build_good_option_catalog(llm_batch_size=...)). None of these options is part of the checkpoint fingerprint, so a build can resume with different values.

docs.title: Score a patient-trial candidate
docs.text:
evaluate_good_options and score_good_options_with_llm require a loaded catalog. The prompt contains the patient cancer-history summary first, followed only by evidence for scoreable investigational or unresolved drugs in the trial. Control, background, and supportive drugs are indexed but are never scored.

Agent and class evidence are merged only here, at prompt time. After the per-drug sections the prompt carries one labelled DRUG CLASS EVIDENCE block per distinct class across the trial's drugs, naming which drugs each block covers; two drugs sharing a class produce one block, not two.

docs.title: Evidence packing
docs.text:
The catalog's stored projections are fixed-size renders made at build time. The scoring prompt does not use them; pack_good_option_evidence re-renders every drug and class from its stored structured facts, sized to how much evidence the trial has in total:

  1. good_option_evidence_budget takes the teacher's context window (good_option_prompt.context_tokens, or llm_good_option.local.engine.max_model_len when unset), subtracts the active backend's llm_good_option max_tokens completion allowance, safety_tokens, room for a parse retry, and the fixed prompt text, and converts the rest at chars_per_token (3.5, conservative for Gemma 4, which averages ~4.4 on catalog text, and for the default Nemotron 3.5 Super, whose tokenizer matches Gemma 4's 4.6 on ctgov eligibility criteria). With the default preset that leaves roughly 500,000 characters.
  2. Drugs and classes share it by weighted max-min fair share, drugs at twice a class's weight. A subject needing less than its share releases the rest. max_drug_section_tokens and max_class_section_tokens (20,000 each) bound any one subject.
  3. A subject that fits its share is rendered in full. One that does not steps down to condensed (attribution capped at 160 characters, statements at 300) or brief (100 and 160) if that fits, so every fact stays visible; the space saved is offered to the others. On v12 class syntheses the two levels render at a median 88% and 58% of full size.
  4. Only when even brief overflows are facts dropped, by the projection's ranking (strongest evidence first, tumor types interleaved) with an omission count; the survivors keep condensed detail so their numbers survive.

Subjects without stored facts, such as hand-built summaries, fall back to their stored projection, truncated if needed. Scoring metadata records a summary of granularities and truncations, and debug mode adds per-row good_option_evidence_packing.

The rubric awards each scoreable drug up to four binary points:

  1. evidence of benefit in the patient's disease type;
  2. the targeted biomarker is commonly expressed in that disease type;
  3. the patient's tumor is documented to have the targeted biomarker; and
  4. human evidence of benefit from targeting that biomarker.

The code-derived LLM score is total_points / (4 * scoreable_drug_count). Trials with missing catalog data, exhausted research, or missing synthesis are returned as explicitly unscored; there is no live-search or legacy-snippet fallback.

docs.title: On-demand check
docs.text:
check_good_options runs the LLM rubric for patient-trial pairs with production defaults from the good_option_check preset section:

  • catalog may be a loaded GoodOptionCatalog or a bundle path. A path is loaded with load_good_option_catalog(path, cache=True), which validates once and reuses the catalog until any bundle file's size or modification time changes.
  • The llm_good_option completion is capped at max_output_tokens (50,000) on a copy of the config, leaving more of the context for evidence.
  • Unless good_option_prompt.context_tokens is set, the evidence budget follows the smallest max_model_len that the configured OpenAI-compatible servers report at /v1/models. If the lookup fails, packing uses the configured context and the warning is returned.
  • Invalid answers get max_parse_attempts (3) attempts in total, then one attempt with thinking disabled when reasoning_off_fallback is true.

Output columns match score_good_options_with_llm. With debug_mode, each row also carries the answer and reasoning texts, finish reason, parse error, evidence packing, good_option_parse_attempts (requests sent for the pair) and good_option_reasoning_off_fallback_used. With return_metadata=True, metadata["good_option_check"] reports max_output_tokens, context_tokens, context_source (configured, endpoint, or preset), and context_warning. The caller's config is never mutated, and the llm_good_option section that fingerprints catalog builds is left unchanged.

docs.title: Deprecated: GoodOptionChecker
docs.text: The trained four-logit GoodOptionChecker classifier is deprecated. It saw one patient summary and one drug summary per example, never the class evidence the teacher prompt carries, and no checker artifact is published. score_good_options, evaluate_good_options(method="classifier"), and build_good_option_checker_text still run but emit DeprecationWarning; the good_option_checker preset section remains only so existing configs load.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.trials
docs.text:
Trial processing APIs.

Each trial step is its own function, so callers can run some and skip others: :func:extract_cohorts (ctgov listings) or :func:extract_protocol_cohorts (full protocols) screen for cancer treatment and extract each cohort's complete criteria; :func:merge_equivalent_cohorts combines a trial's cohorts with essentially the same criteria; :func:remove_boilerplate_criteria tags every criteria line inclusion or exclusion and boilerplate or not, and separates key from boilerplate criteria. :func:process_trials runs all of them, on ctgov listings or protocols, in that order.

Notes

Both read each space's cohort_key_criteria from load_guideline_catalog: its nine fields in the layout of a trial cohort's key criteria. Catalog embeddings are computed once per call for all supplied patients, or reused from the optional verified cache. Only missing/changed text is embedded. Patient embeddings always use the same model configuration. Ranking is at space level, not disease/trial level. All retrieved candidates are scored with filter_low_quality=False so a cutoff cannot silently remove the requested top N. Low scores remain flagged by match_quality_pass. Ties use similarity, then the space ID. A score is a prioritization signal, not a probability of clinical appropriateness.
