def load_guideline_catalog(
    catalog: str | Path | pd.DataFrame | list[str | Path],
    *,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    refresh: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Load complete catalog records, retaining menus and source provenance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    catalog : path, DataFrame, or list of paths
        An external completed disease output directory, its ``paradigms.jsonl``,
        a list of those paths, or the DataFrame returned by ``summarize_guidelines``.
        The standalone prototype's JSONL exports are also supported. CSV space
        exports omit the menus and cannot be used here.
    return_metadata : bool, optional
        Also return the catalog fingerprint, file hashes, source editions, and
        any recorded audit status. No source PDFs or model calls are needed.
    refresh : bool, default False
        Force rereading and validating supplied files, replacing cached versions.
        Otherwise unchanged files reuse previously validated records in memory.
        DataFrame input is always copied and validated without caching.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Receives file-change checking, loading/validation, and cache reuse updates.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame or tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        Complete, validated catalog records. Stored clinical text, conditions,
        categories, evidence, and uncertainties are preserved without rewriting.
        Each record also gets ``cohort_key_criteria``, which TrialSpace retrieval
        and the decision model's match questions read: the record's stored
        cohort-style ``key_criteria`` (protocol-style sentences the endpoint wrote
        for the space, since 2026-11-14) when present, else its nine-field space
        laid out as a trial cohort's key criteria (one "Label: value." line per
        field under "Inclusion criteria:" and "Exclusion criteria:", NA fields
        left out). The column itself is set on every load and excluded from
        ``catalog_sha256`` (a stored ``key_criteria`` is part of the record and
        its hash); a supplied column of that name is recomputed.

    Notes
    -----
    A present ``status.json`` must say complete. A present ``validation.json``
    must report a passing audit whose export hash matches the JSONL. This loader
    checks stored structure and export integrity; it does not repeat the full
    source audit or establish clinical correctness. Bare JSONL/DataFrame inputs
    have no verified audit status. Catalogs remain source-derived local data.
    The process-local cache checks file identity, size, modification time, and
    change time for the JSONL and its status/audit files on every call. It follows
    the filesystem's metadata visibility (including network filesystem delays);
    use ``refresh=True`` to force a full read. Cache entries are bounded to 128
    files and 512 MiB of source JSONL, and disappear on process restart. Returned
    records are independent copies, including nested menus and evidence.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    from ._guideline_schema import format_key_criteria

    if progress_callback is not None and not callable(progress_callback):
        raise TypeError("progress_callback must be callable or None.")

    def progress(message):
        if progress_callback is not None:
            try:
                progress_callback(message)
            except Exception:
                logging.getLogger(__name__).exception(
                    "Guideline catalog progress callback failed"
                )

    artifacts = []
    cached_files = 0
    loaded_files = 0
    if isinstance(catalog, pd.DataFrame):
        progress("Validating supplied guideline records")
        # A loaded catalog passed back in keeps its fingerprint: the key criteria are derived.
        catalog = catalog.drop(columns=KEY_CRITERIA_COLUMN, errors="ignore")
        frame = pd.DataFrame(
            copy.deepcopy(catalog.to_dict("records")), columns=catalog.columns
        )
        artifacts.append(
            {"input_type": "dataframe", "recorded_source_audit": "unavailable"}
        )
        _validate_catalog(frame)
    else:
        paths = catalog if isinstance(catalog, (list, tuple)) else [catalog]
        if not paths:
            raise ValueError("Supply at least one guideline catalog.")
        progress("Checking guideline catalog files for changes")
        records = []
        for index, value in enumerate(paths, 1):
            if not isinstance(value, (str, Path)):
                raise TypeError("catalog must be a DataFrame, path, or list of paths.")
            # Resolve links before choosing sidecars, so a JSONL symlink cannot
            # bypass the completion/audit files beside its actual target.
            path = Path(value).resolve()
            if path.is_dir():
                path = path / "paradigms.jsonl"
            if path.suffix != ".jsonl":
                raise ValueError(
                    "Use a completed catalog directory or paradigms.jsonl; CSV lacks considerations."
                )
            rows, artifact, hit = _load_catalog_file(
                path,
                refresh=refresh,
                progress=lambda: progress(
                    f"Loading and validating guideline catalog {index}/{len(paths)}"
                ),
            )
            records.extend(rows)
            artifacts.append(artifact)
            cached_files += int(hit)
            loaded_files += int(not hit)
        frame = pd.DataFrame(records)
        if frame.empty:
            _validate_catalog(frame)
        # Individual files are validated once per version. Collection-level
        # uniqueness and legacy numbering still depend on this call's selection.
        if frame["space_trial_id"].duplicated().any():
            raise ValueError(
                "Catalog space_trial_id values must be unique, including across supplied files."
            )
    # Early standalone exports omitted these two standard trial-space columns.
    # Add bookkeeping only; no clinical field or menu is changed.
    if "clinical_space_number" not in frame:
        frame["clinical_space_number"] = None
    # Mixed old/new inputs can contain the column but lack it on legacy rows.
    # Allocate unused numbers within each guideline without changing stored ones.
    for _, group in frame.groupby("trial_id", sort=False):
        existing = group["clinical_space_number"].dropna()
        if (
            any(
                isinstance(number, bool)
                or not isinstance(number, (int, float))
                or not float(number).is_integer()
                or number < 1
                for number in existing
            )
            or existing.duplicated().any()
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Catalog space numbers must be unique positive integers per trial_id."
            )
        used = set(existing)
        number = 1
        for index in group.index[group["clinical_space_number"].isna()]:
            while number in used:
                number += 1
            frame.loc[index, "clinical_space_number"] = number
            used.add(number)
    frame["clinical_space_number"] = frame["clinical_space_number"].astype(int)
    if "general_exclusion_criteria" not in frame:
        frame["general_exclusion_criteria"] = "NA"
    else:
        frame["general_exclusion_criteria"] = frame[
            "general_exclusion_criteria"
        ].fillna("NA")
    sources = {}
    for source in frame["source"]:
        sources[source["source_fingerprint"]] = {
            key: source[key]
            for key in (
                "disease",
                "title",
                "version",
                "source_sha256",
                "source_fingerprint",
            )
        }
    metadata = {
        "package": package_metadata(),
        "catalog_sha256": digest(frame.to_dict("records")),
        "catalog_spaces": len(frame),
        "artifacts": artifacts,
        "sources": list(sources.values()),
        "clinical_correctness": "not established",
        "validation_cache": {
            "cached_files": cached_files,
            "loaded_files": loaded_files,
            "storage": "process_memory",
        },
    }
    frame = frame.reset_index(drop=True)
    frame[KEY_CRITERIA_COLUMN] = [_key_criteria(row) for row in frame.to_dict("records")]
    if artifacts and not isinstance(catalog, pd.DataFrame):
        progress(
            f"Guideline catalogs ready: reused {cached_files} validated catalogs; "
            f"loaded and validated {loaded_files} catalogs"
        )
    return (frame, metadata) if return_metadata else frame

docs.title: get_guideline_considerations
docs.text:
get_guideline_considerations(catalog: str | Path | DataFrame | list[str | Path], *, space_trial_id: str | None = None, clinical_space_summary: str | None = None, return_metadata: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]

Return the stored diagnostic/treatment considerations for an exact space.

Select by space_trial_id, exact clinical_space_summary text, or both. No fuzzy lookup, model generation, or inferred menu applicability is used. An unknown ID/text or a mismatched ID/text pair raises KeyError. If the exact definition occurs in multiple supplied source editions, text lookup returns all matching records with their provenance; use an ID to select one. Return conventions match load_guideline_catalog.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/trials/guideline_catalog.py 
def get_guideline_considerations(
    catalog: str | Path | pd.DataFrame | list[str | Path],
    *,
    space_trial_id: str | None = None,
    clinical_space_summary: str | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Return the stored diagnostic/treatment considerations for an exact space.

    Select by ``space_trial_id``, exact ``clinical_space_summary`` text, or both.
    No fuzzy lookup, model generation, or inferred menu applicability is used.
    An unknown ID/text or a mismatched ID/text pair raises ``KeyError``. If the
    exact definition occurs in multiple supplied source editions, text lookup
    returns all matching records with their provenance; use an ID to select one.
    Return conventions match ``load_guideline_catalog``.
    """
    if space_trial_id is None and clinical_space_summary is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "Supply space_trial_id or clinical_space_summary for an exact catalog lookup."
        )
    for value in (space_trial_id, clinical_space_summary):
        if value is not None and (not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip()):
            raise ValueError("Space lookup values must be nonempty strings.")
    frame, metadata = load_guideline_catalog(catalog, return_metadata=True)
    keep = frame.index == frame.index
    if space_trial_id is not None:
        keep &= frame["space_trial_id"] == space_trial_id
    if clinical_space_summary is not None:
        keep &= frame["clinical_space_summary"] == clinical_space_summary
    result = frame.loc[keep].reset_index(drop=True)
    if result.empty:
        raise KeyError("The requested space is not present in this guideline catalog.")
    return (result, metadata) if return_metadata else result

docs.title: Trial steps, separately or end to end
docs.text: Each step is its own function, so a caller can run some and skip others: extract_cohorts (ClinicalTrials.gov, "ctgov", listings; named summarize_trials before November 2026, a deprecated alias) or extract_protocol_cohorts (full protocols) screen for cancer treatment and extract each cohort's complete criteria; merge_equivalent_cohorts combines a trial's cohorts with essentially the same criteria; remove_boilerplate_criteria splits each cohort's criteria into key and boilerplate criteria; screen_trials runs only the screen. process_trials runs the screen, cohort extraction, merge and boilerplate removal in the order training uses them, on ctgov listings (source="ctgov", the default) or full protocols (source="protocol", with that section's settings for every step), and returns merged cohorts with cohort_key_criteria and cohort_boilerplate_criteria (each step's metadata with return_metadata=True; output_dir saves and reuses each trial's results). Until November 2026 the package called ClinicalTrials.gov "registry"; outputs from then keep cohort_criteria_source="registry".

docs.title: Three-step treatment screening and cohort extraction
docs.text:
The default trial.extraction_method is cohorts. extract_cohorts accepts one row per trial with trial_id, trial_title, brief_summary, and eligibility_criteria; IDs must be unique and nonempty. Each listing becomes one document, Title: ..., Brief summary: and Eligibility criteria: with source formatting preserved, and goes through the same workflow and prompts as full protocols (extract_protocol_cohorts, below; matchminer_ai.trials.cohort_workflow). Every trial gets separate requests:

  1. Screen (trial.cohorts.screen.user.txt): {"cancer_treatment_trial": "yes"} or {"cancer_treatment_trial": "no"}. Only direct anti-cancer treatment strategies qualify (including PK/PD, safety, dose or surrogate-endpoint studies); diagnostic, supportive-care, survivorship, primary-prevention and non-cancer trials do not. A "no" ends the trial.
  2. Cohort names (trial.cohorts.list.user.txt): {"cohorts": ["Part A, dose escalation", "Part B, dose expansion (disease X)"]}, one or more distinct names in source order: the cohorts the trial defines (parts, phases, arms or groups that enroll participants), at the lowest level of any hierarchy, without comparing their criteria. Stratification factors, crossover, extension and rollover phases, and optional sub-studies are not cohorts; closed cohorts are kept, and cohorts limited to countries that exclude the United States are omitted. A single population is one cohort (for example "All participants").
  3. Criteria, one request per cohort (trial.cohorts.criteria.user.txt): {"eligibility_criteria": "Inclusion criteria:\n...\nExclusion criteria:\n..."}, the complete criteria of the named cohort: criteria stated for every participant, for a part or group containing it, or for a disease it can include, and no criterion that applies only to other cohorts. The request lists every cohort name and ends with the target name.

The criteria prompt keeps enrollment criteria only and copies every criterion that applies to the cohort verbatim, boilerplate included: consent, compliance, samples or biopsies, measurable disease, contraception, pregnancy and lactation, vaccine restrictions, study-staff and catch-all investigator-judgment exclusions are never left out. The optional boilerplate step (below) separates them afterwards. Criteria that apply only to people already in the study (crossover, retreatment, rollover) or to optional sub-studies are omitted. Only United States versions of country-specific criteria are kept, references are resolved by restating their content, applicability lead-ins and mentions of other cohorts are removed once a criterion's placement is decided, qualifiers are never deleted, and gaps or damaged source text are flagged with a "Source limitation:" statement.

Every prompt starts with the same preamble and document, and the criteria prompt puts the cohort list and target name last, so a server's prefix cache reuses a trial's document across its requests. Each answer is validated by its own contract (parse_screen, parse_cohort_list, parse_criteria): exactly the one field, lowercase "yes"/"no", distinct nonempty names, nonempty criteria that are not placeholders, a stop finish. One complete outer Markdown fence is accepted; duplicate keys, extra fields, surrounding prose and truncation fail validation and never become negative decisions. With a remote backend and trial.cohorts.structured_outputs: true (the default), each request sets a response_format with its step's schema (JSON_SCHEMAS). Only failed requests are retried, with the full document, the original instructions and the validation error, up to trial.cohorts.max_attempts; a cohort that fails every attempt fails its trial. A remote backend keeps trial.cohorts.chunk_size * chunks_in_flight requests in flight, each sent as another returns; a local backend gets batches of chunk_size requests of one step, chunks_in_flight at once. Cohorts whose extracted criteria are identical are combined into one row with both names.

A trial's decision (schema trial-cohorts-stepwise-v1) is

{
  "cancer_treatment_trial": "yes",
  "multiple_cohorts": "yes",
  "cohorts": [
    {"cohort_name": "Part A", "eligibility_criteria": "Inclusion criteria: ..."},
    {"cohort_name": "Part B", "eligibility_criteria": "Inclusion criteria: ..."}
  ]
}

or {"cancer_treatment_trial": "no"}; multiple_cohorts is derived from the number of cohorts. The returned DataFrame contains accepted cohorts only:

Column Meaning cohort_trial_id <trial_id>-cohort-<zero-based number>; distinct from legacy space IDs. trial_id Source trial identifier. cohort_number Zero-based population index in source order. cohort_name The cohort's name from step 2, also for a single population. Kept out of eligibility text and embeddings. cohort_eligibility_criteria That cohort's complete criteria from its own request. cohort_criteria_source ctgov (extract_cohorts; registry before November 2026) or protocol (extract_protocol_cohorts). Older outputs used llm and eligibility_criteria. cancer_treatment_trial yes for every returned row. multiple_cohorts yes when the trial has more than one cohort.

Rows use representation_version="trial-treatment-cohorts-v5". Earlier generations (single-request schemas trial-registry-cohorts-v1 and trial-protocol-cohorts-v2, rows v4 with cohort_specific_eligibility_criteria and common_eligibility_criteria) remain readable with cohort_schema.parse_cohort_response for audits, but are not produced. Rejected trials produce no rows; empty and all-rejected runs keep the column schema.

from matchminer_ai.trials import extract_cohorts

cohorts, metadata, qc = extract_cohorts(
    trials, config=config, return_metadata=True, return_qc=True
)
print(metadata["trial_decisions"])
print(metadata["trial_cohort_names"])
print(metadata["trial_errors"])

Decisions, rejections, errors, schema and representation versions, and the prompt-set hash (prompt_sha256, with prompt_sha256_by_step) also appear in cohorts.attrs. Returned metadata includes each trial's attempts per step (with serving endpoints), cohort names, combined cohorts and model provenance. Debug mode adds every step's answer and reasoning and each row's input document. QC separates treatment rejections, exhausted inference errors and truncated responses.

Do not rename these columns to legacy space columns or reuse saved space embeddings as if the representations were interchangeable. hierarchical and one_shot remain explicit legacy modes with their previous space schema; the current Space applications opt into that mode.

docs.title: Cohort extraction from full protocol documents
docs.text:
extract_protocol_cohorts runs the same three steps and prompts on complete protocol documents. It accepts one row per trial with a unique trial_id and a protocol_path to a PDF or a UTF-8 text file (.txt or .md). PDFs are converted locally with ocr_pdf; pass text_output_dir to keep the converted text, which is otherwise written to a temporary directory and removed. Each document is sent whole; documents longer than protocol_cohort_extraction.max_document_characters fail rather than being truncated. The prompts cover protocol-specific sources: eligibility anywhere in the document (study design, part or module sections, appendices), body text over abbreviated synopsis criteria, current text over superseded amendment text, and PDF-conversion damage.

Settings come from protocol_cohort_extraction (max_attempts, chunk_size, chunks_in_flight, structured_outputs, and optional prompt_files mapping screen/list/criteria to other packaged prompt files). With output_dir, each decided trial is saved as soon as it is decided to <output_dir>/<trial_id>/extraction.json (decision, cohort names, combined cohorts, every attempt per step with its serving endpoint, prompt hashes, schema version and source-document SHA-256) with reasoning.json. A rerun with the same output_dir reuses a saved decision only when the prompts, schema and document bytes are unchanged, and sends the rest.

The result has the extract_cohorts cohort columns, with cohort_criteria_source set to "protocol"; return_metadata=True adds per-trial decisions, attempts and errors, source-document hashes and page counts, and the config snapshot. The whole document reaches the configured LLM endpoint, so use only documents without patient data unless that endpoint is authorized for their sensitivity. Outputs are research abstractions for human review, not eligibility determinations.

docs.title: Merging equivalent cohorts
docs.text: merge_equivalent_cohorts takes cohort rows from either extractor and asks the LLM once per trial with more than one cohort (trial.cohorts.merge.user.txt) which cohorts have essentially the same criteria, such as arms that differ only in treatment or dose. The model returns only a grouping of cohort numbers; each group becomes its first cohort's row, with the merged names joined by "; ", renumbered cohort_number and cohort_trial_id, and merged_from. Criteria are never regenerated. A trial whose answer never validates keeps its cohorts unmerged (merge_errors). With output_dir, each grouping is saved to <output_dir>/<trial_id>/merge.json and reused while the prompt and the trial's cohorts are unchanged.

docs.title: Key and boilerplate criteria
docs.text:
remove_boilerplate_criteria separates each cohort's key criteria, the criteria that define its population, from its boilerplate criteria, the general requirements most cancer trials share: consent, compliance, samples and biopsies, measurable disease, prognosis, performance status, organ function, brain metastases, toxicities of earlier treatment, washout periods of 30 days or less, recovery from recent major surgery, non-cancer conditions, unrelated other cancers, simultaneous participation in another trial, contraception, pregnancy and lactation, vaccines, and study-staff and catch-all exclusions, each unless it is central to what the trial studies. Each cohort's criteria are split into one item per line, and each item gets its own request (trial.cohorts.deboilerplate.user.txt, schema trial-cohorts-deboilerplate-v4) showing the cohort's numbered criteria and asking two things, answered as {"criterion_type": "inclusion" | "exclusion", "boilerplate": true | false}: whether the item is an inclusion or an exclusion criterion (an item under an "Inclusion criteria:" or "Exclusion criteria:" heading takes that heading's type even when worded negatively; sub-items, notes and introductory lines take the type of the criterion they belong to), and whether it is boilerplate. Code sorts the unchanged items, so no criterion is lost or reworded.

The result keeps cohort_eligibility_criteria unchanged (all the criteria) and adds:

Column Meaning cohort_key_criteria The criteria that are not boilerplate; all the criteria for a cohort in deboilerplate_errors. Read by TrialSpace retrieval and the decision model's match questions. cohort_boilerplate_criteria The boilerplate criteria; None for a cohort in deboilerplate_errors. Read by the decision model's boilerplate question. cohort_criteria_items Every item with its tags, as a JSON string: a list of {"number", "heading", "text", "criterion_type", "boilerplate"} in the original order (criterion_type null for an item whose answer never validated). Read by check_eligibility_criteria.

A cohort without items, or whose items are all classified as boilerplate, is reported in deboilerplate_errors; an item whose answer never validates counts as key, has no criterion type, and is reported in unclassified_items. The metadata's criterion_type_heading_disagreements counts items whose type differs from the heading above them. With output_dir, each trial's results are saved to <output_dir>/<trial_id>/deboilerplate.json: per cohort, key_criteria and boilerplate_criteria (or error) and every item's attempts with their answers and reasoning. Classifications are reused while the prompt and the cohort's name and criteria are unchanged.

Both steps are optional at inference. They take section="trial" (ctgov listings) or "protocol_cohort_extraction" (protocols) for their LLM settings; training runs the merge first, then the boilerplate step.

Guideline catalog spaces have no boilerplate. Their cohort_key_criteria come from one of two sources: - Since 2026-11-14: the endpoint writes protocol-style criteria for each space and stores them as key_criteria. For an older catalog, add_guideline_cohort_criteria writes a derived edition that has them. - Older catalogs: load_guideline_catalog lays the nine population fields out the same way.

See the guideline extraction guide.

docs.title: Cancer-treatment screen only
docs.text: screen_trials runs only the workflow's first step (trial.cohorts.screen.user.txt, with the same settings and response contract) on listings (title or trial_title, brief_summary, eligibility_criteria) or full documents (trial_text). It returns trial_id, cancer_treatment_trial ("yes", "no", or None when no answer validated) and screen_error; a trial whose answer never validates is reported, not rejected. With output_dir, every attempt's answer and reasoning is appended to <output_dir>/screen.jsonl as requests return, and saved decisions are reused while the prompt and the trial's document are unchanged. Training draws its trial sample from the trials this screen accepts.

docs.title: Synthetic protocols seeded by ctgov records
docs.text:
generate_synthetic_protocols writes one fabricated full protocol per ctgov seed, for building training corpora of realistic, often messily specified eligibility text. Seeds have a unique trial_id and optional title, brief_summary, detailed_description and eligibility_criteria strings; missing fields are marked as not provided. The record is a seed, not a specification. The prompt pair trial.synthetic_protocol.system.txt and trial.synthetic_protocol.user.txt asks for a prospective sponsor-style protocol in Markdown with no synthetic-document disclaimer, and assigns each trial one of the weighted eligibility layouts in data/synthetic_protocol_layouts.json (stable per trial ID).

Requests run through the configured backend in chunks, with several chunks in flight. Remote runs use the shared endpoint pool, so adaptive concurrency, vLLM load feedback and remote.server_urls_file registries (which can give each endpoint its own served model ID) apply. With output_dir, each trial's protocol.md, reasoning.txt and meta.json are written as its chunk returns, completed trials with the same prompt hash are skipped on rerun, and the returned frame holds file paths. Empty or truncated outputs are retried. Outputs are fabricated and must be labeled as synthetic wherever they are used.

docs.title: Hierarchical extraction
docs.text:
Set trial.extraction_method to hierarchical to use the legacy space workflow. It builds a tree in this fixed order: age, cancer primary site, sex, histology, disease state, prior treatment requirements, and biomarker requirements. One request handles one parent and one field, returning a JSON array of alternative values rather than a full list of spaces. Independent parents are batched through the configured backend. A trial with one branch throughout uses eight logical calls: seven fields and one separate boilerplate call.

Every population-field request includes:

  1. The hierarchy's purpose and the current field.
  2. The complete trial source.
  3. "For a patient with this set of characteristics:" followed by the inherited characteristics of exactly one candidate branch and its source-grounded scope.
  4. "What sets of [age ranges / prior treatment requirements / biomarker requirements / etc.] are relevant for determining eligibility for this trial?"
  5. Shared anti-boilerplate instructions and authored omissions.
  6. Only the current field's verbatim instructions and examples from the active trial.user.primer.txt, followed by the JSON response contract.

Other fields' definitions are absent. The shared anti-boilerplate boundary uses the primer's definition and examples of general exclusions; the omission text retains its measurable-disease/biopsy-target and treatment-washout instructions. The primary-site request includes the exact diagnosis-enumeration paragraph now contained in that authored section. Biomarker requests also receive the exact treatment-defining population example. Each branch adds only the current field and retains shared requirements. A condition assigned to this field must survive in its value, not only its scope. Biomarker fields include only restrictions on results: positive or negative status, specific alterations, or expression thresholds. A requirement to test or know a biomarker's status, while allowing either result, is omitted; use NA when no result restriction remains. Screening-assessment notes accompany actual result restrictions only. This rule is shared with one-shot extraction through the primer. The separate single boilerplate request uses the full source, a trial-wide scope, the authored boilerplate paragraph (including logical negation examples), and shared omissions. It does not receive the population fields' definitions.

The internal scope describes the applicable eligibility pathway. It preserves cross-field dependencies and conditional exceptions; it is not included in the final space text. Equal values with different scopes remain separate until the remaining fields are resolved. No Cartesian product of independent field lists is made. Python copies ancestors into each completed leaf, removes exact duplicate leaves, renders all seven labels, and adds numbering. Public column names and zero-based space IDs remain unchanged.

The model returns {"branches": [{"value": "...", "scope": "..."}], "prune_reason": ""} for a field. Empty branches require an explicit source incompatibility and cannot be used at the root. Boilerplate instead returns {"exclusions": ["..."]} and retains subgroup qualifications. Malformed JSON, wrong keys, multiline values and truncated answers are rejected. Retries include the specific error, latest rejected answer, and a valid JSON structure, including explicit array/object closure guidance. After two invalid answers (or on the last retry with a smaller budget), thinking stays off; Beam stays at low reasoning effort. After repeated failures, the malformed draft is omitted and the model regenerates from the original source plus the error and schema. Exhausted nodes still fail the trial rather than exporting only its successful branches.

When every population branch is explicitly pruned, a separate study-scope call reviews the full source. It must independently confirm that there is no human therapeutic cancer population and supply a verbatim source excerpt. Confirmed rejections produce no spaces and are recorded in metadata.trial_rejections, separately from inference failures. A review decision triggers targeted re-extraction of the pruned fields, with the review explanation and original parent context. Up to two recovery rounds are allowed per trial. Recovery feedback does not authorize inventing eligibility, changing parent fields, or overriding the source. Corrective requests have distinct checkpoint keys and retain their recovery round and replaced request key in traces. Completed nodes remain reusable; replaying a previously failed trial reaches these new recovery requests instead of permanently repeating its cached pruning decision. Exhausted recovery, malformed reviews and unsupported rejection excerpts remain failures. This is a targeted review of empty trees, not a replacement screening pass. Original field prompts, successful node identities, and the seven-field space format are unchanged.

Configuration under trial.hierarchy:

Setting Default Meaning max_attempts 4 Validation attempts per node; backend transport retries remain separate. max_nodes 4096 Maximum branches at a field; exceeding it fails rather than truncates. max_calls 20000 Logical node calls per trial, excluding retries. batch_size 256 Maximum parent requests in a synchronous local backend batch. active_trials 32 Minimum rolling remote trial window; enlarged to at least total endpoint concurrency. checkpoint_dir unset Optional directory of successful node responses.

Remote extraction uses one dependency-ready queue across trials and field levels. Each validated parent immediately releases its children, without waiting for siblings or other trials. Boilerplate starts independently of the field tree. A finished trial admits another immediately. Persistent clients share the configured remote.max_concurrent_requests cap per endpoint across all these requests, including retries. Only parent-child dependencies impose ordering; calls for the same branch cannot skip ahead. Leaves retain the model's original branch order, so response timing does not affect space IDs and cached wave-based responses keep their existing numbering. Synchronous local vLLM generation retains batched field waves with one resident model.

Set the remote request cap in the top-level remote configuration, for example config.remote["max_concurrent_requests"] = 32, or in YAML:

remote:
  max_concurrent_requests: 32

The default is 32 per server. With N endpoints the total ceiling is N times this value, shared across trials, field branches, boilerplate and retries within one extraction call. trial.hierarchy.active_trials controls how much work is available; it does not multiply the request cap. Separately launched clients each have their own cap. Set the value before starting extraction.

Node checkpoints fingerprint source, parent, scope, prompts, algorithm version, and runtime configuration. Changed inputs/configuration never reuse old nodes. Trial extraction defaults to a 50,000-token output ceiling (reasoning plus final answer) and a 100,000-token local context. Each request still reduces its output allowance when necessary to fit the configured context without truncating source. Debug trial_reasoning_text contains a JSON audit of the node responses, reasoning and validation attempts. Configured context limits reserve output space without truncating the source. Model sampling and parser selection still use the existing backend profiles.

The shared introduction and JSON response contracts live in src/matchminer_ai/prompts/trial.hierarchy.*.txt. Each field component expands {{field_rules}} with its exact section from trial.user.primer.txt, under FIELD-SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS (verbatim):. The combined treatment field receives the original treatment section, and the combined biomarker field receives the original biomarker section. Age retains its existing instructions because the primer has no separate age section. Changed section boundaries fail explicitly rather than silently dropping guidance. One-shot extraction uses the same active primer; it now emits the same seven labels. trial.user.question.txt is unchanged. The shared engine, hierarchy prompts and primer are mirrored in training, with cross-repository contract tests.

This hierarchy is trial-hierarchy-v5, the combined-requirements prompt contract. Primary site is still fixed before sex; final text retains the established age, sex, primary-site label order. Prompt and version fingerprints prevent reuse of v1/v2/v3/v4 extraction checkpoints. Compatible treatment screening can be retained.

This design increases the number of calls and repeats source text. It improves structural control but does not establish clinical completeness: an erroneous early branch or an unsupported model interpretation can still propagate. Review the node traces and final populations against the source before adopting new spaces or regenerating embeddings. Existing saved spaces are not migrated.

docs.title: ClinicalTrials.gov records
docs.text: matchminer_ai.trials.ctgov_records fetches one public ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 study by NCT ID and accepts no patient context. fetch_trial_eligibility_criteria reads protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria, preserves multiline criteria formatting, and returns the NCT ID, public study URL, retrieval timestamp, and ctgov last-update date with the text. fetch_trial_ctgov_document also accepts an official ClinicalTrials.gov study URL and wrangles the official or brief title, brief summary, detailed description, and eligibility criteria into explicit fields for extract_cohorts consumers. URL parsing never changes the request host: the API request is always sent to ClinicalTrials.gov using the normalized NCT ID. The GoodOption catalog fetches its studies with fetch_trial_study.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.trials.ctgov_records
docs.text: ClinicalTrials.gov record lookup: GoodOption catalog studies, trial-space extraction documents and complete eligibility criteria. Requests carry only an NCT ID, never patient context.

docs.title: fetch_trial_eligibility_criteria
docs.text:
fetch_trial_eligibility_criteria(nct_id: str, *, client: Client | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0) -> TrialEligibilityCriteria

Fetch current complete eligibility criteria for one NCT ID.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/trials/ctgov_records.py 
def fetch_trial_eligibility_criteria(
    nct_id: str,
    *,
    client: httpx.Client | None = None,
    timeout: float = 30.0,
) -> TrialEligibilityCriteria:
    """Fetch current complete eligibility criteria for one NCT ID."""

    document = fetch_trial_ctgov_document(
        nct_id,
        client=client,
        timeout=timeout,
    )
    return TrialEligibilityCriteria(
        nct_id=document.nct_id,
        eligibility_criteria=document.eligibility_criteria,
        source_url=document.source_url,
        fetched_at_utc=document.fetched_at_utc,
        last_update_post_date=document.last_update_post_date,
    )

docs.title: fetch_trial_ctgov_document
docs.text:
fetch_trial_ctgov_document(nct_reference: str, *, client: Client | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0) -> TrialCtgovDocument

Fetch and wrangle one NCT ID or ClinicalTrials.gov study URL.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/trials/ctgov_records.py

    nct_reference: str,
    *,
    client: httpx.Client | None = None,

docs.title: normalize_nct_reference
docs.text:
normalize_nct_reference(value: Any) -> str

Normalize an NCT ID or an official ClinicalTrials.gov study URL.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/trials/ctgov_records.py 
def normalize_nct_reference(value: Any) -> str:
    """Normalize an NCT ID or an official ClinicalTrials.gov study URL."""

    raw_value = str(value or "").strip()
    if NCT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw_value):
        return normalize_nct_id(raw_value)
    if raw_value.casefold().startswith(
        ("clinicaltrials.gov/", "www.clinicaltrials.gov/")
    ):
        raw_value = f"https://{raw_value}"
    parsed = urlparse(raw_value)
    hostname = (parsed.hostname or "").casefold()
    if parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https"} or hostname not in {
        "clinicaltrials.gov",
        "www.clinicaltrials.gov",
    }:
        raise ValueError(
            "Enter an NCT ID or a ClinicalTrials.gov study URL."
        )
    for segment in parsed.path.split("/"):
        if NCT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(segment):
            return normalize_nct_id(segment)
    raise ValueError("ClinicalTrials.gov URL does not contain a valid NCT ID.")

docs.title: Trial-space eligibility criteria
docs.text:
extract_trial_space_eligibility_criteria accepts one clinical-space summary and the path to a UTF-8 .txt file produced by OCR. It sends the complete text and trial space to the configured local or OpenAI-compatible LLM backend and returns one JSON-compatible object:

from matchminer_ai.trials import extract_trial_space_eligibility_criteria

criteria = extract_trial_space_eligibility_criteria(
    clinical_space_summary,
    "Eligibility-Eligibility_Checklist.txt",
    config=config,
)

{
  "trial_space": "the original clinical-space summary",
  "inclusion_criteria": ["complete relevant criterion"],
  "exclusion_criteria": ["complete relevant criterion"]
}

The original trial space is attached by code. Every criterion must be a verbatim excerpt from the OCR text after conservative OCR normalization. This collapses whitespace, joins a line-broken ordinal suffix such as 9 th, removes repeated page-edge boilerplate, and skips a trailing footnote only when its marker is referenced earlier on that page. Invalid, ungrounded, duplicated, or overlapping lists are retried and then rejected. Universal criteria and criteria whose scope is ambiguous remain in scope, while criteria explicitly limited to an incompatible population are omitted.

No web search is used. With a remote backend, the entire OCR document reaches the configured endpoint. Use protocol documents without patient data unless the endpoint is authorized for the document's sensitivity. OCR and LLM outputs must be compared with the complete, current protocol and do not establish eligibility.

New space text uses Cancer primary site allowed, Prior treatment requirements, and Biomarker requirements. Treatment and biomarker fields each retain both positive and negative conditions. Extraction postprocessing, QC and training's 0c sampling accept these seven fields as well as saved legacy nine-field spaces; they do not rewrite saved text or mix extraction checkpoints. Match-label and synthetic-patient prompts preserve clause polarity and AND/OR logic. The PDQ catalog retains its separate JSON required/excluded fields. Existing trained models can consume the new text, but their quality on this prompt generation still requires evaluation; regenerate embeddings for changed spaces.

Hierarchical response parsing accepts one complete outer Markdown code fence (json, case-insensitive, or no language tag). It then applies the same strict JSON/schema, duplicate-key, and completion-status validation. Prose outside the fence, malformed JSON, and truncated responses still fail. Raw responses and reasoning remain unchanged in the audit. This presentation-only parser fix is compatible with existing v5 prompts and successful node checkpoints.

docs.title: Extraction-Based Workup Checks
docs.text:
Review aids, not determinations

Results say whether structured items extracted from the notes document a guideline workup step. An LLM wrote the query and an LLM extracted the items: check every cited quote against its note. Not documented means no extracted item matched, not that the step was not done. This does not establish overall guideline concordance.

This is a second way to check guideline workup, beside the note-reading reviews (review_patient_workup, review_population_workup). It reads the records of Structured Clinical Extraction instead of the notes:

  1. Compile once per requirement. compile_workup_queries asks the workup_query_compile LLM to translate each guideline diagnostic_workup item (name, conditions, category), with the guideline population's key criteria as context, into a declarative JSON query. The model's only power is answering with a query: it has no tools, browsing, files or shell, and it never sees patient data. Code validates the query; an invalid answer is retried with its problems named.
  2. Evaluate in code. check_workup_with_extractions runs every query on every patient's extraction items. The evaluator is pure Python with no I/O and no model calls: the same query and records always give the same result.
from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.patients import (
    check_workup_with_extractions,
    compile_workup_queries,
    extract_document_records,
)

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote.update(enabled=True, server_urls=["http://localhost:8000/v1"],
                     request_timeout=14400)

compiled = compile_workup_queries(
    space["diagnostic_workup"], config=config,
    population_context=space["cohort_key_criteria"], cache=my_cache,
)
documents = extract_document_records(notes, config=config)
report = check_workup_with_extractions(documents, compiled)

SQL-Agent Workup Checks read the same records with queries that an LLM agent writes in SQL after exploring the extracted data.

For a population, matchminer_ai.population.check_population_workup_with_extractions takes a cohort (with its space), the compiled queries and the document and patient records, links records to the cohort's own notes by note id, and returns the cohort with a report in the shape of the full-note population review (method extraction_queries).

docs.title: The query language
docs.text:
A query is one JSON object, decoded under query_response_schema() with vLLM structured outputs and validated by validate_workup_query(). The schema is strict and non-recursive (no $ref, null, minLength or pattern).

Key Meaning summary One sentence: what the query checks. expressible false when the item types cannot check the requirement (examinations, laboratory panels, consultations, multidisciplinary evaluation, counseling). Then criteria is [], every expression is {"all_of": []} and not_expressible_reason says why; the result is unknown. approximations What was left out or approximated ("upper abdomen" by the abdomen region). Shown as limitations. criteria Up to 24 named matchers of one item type each: id, label, item_type, status (performed, planned, any), filters, window, min_count. requirement What must be documented. applies_when Documented facts that make a conditional step apply ({"all_of": []}: the whole population). not_applicable_when Documented facts that make it not apply. It needs at least one criterion that is not negated: a step is never not applicable because something is undocumented.

Expressions are AND-of-OR, with up to 24 groups of up to 12 literals: {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "id", "negated": false}, ...]}, ...]}. Alternatives are literals of one group; components that are all required are separate groups; a negated literal holds when its criterion does not. A requirement needs at least one criterion that is not negated, and every criterion must be used.

A filter is {"field", "op", "values", "if_not_stated"}; all of a criterion's filters must hold. Fields are the item type's fields (record_json_schema), level, document_type, relation (imaging studies and procedures) and procedure_group. Operators:

Operator Fields Holds when in, not_in codes the code is (is not) one of values contains_any, contains_all, contains_none lists of codes (body_regions) the list contains any, all or none of values text_contains_any, text_contains_none text, text lists a value occurs as a whole word or phrase, ignoring case and punctuation (ALK does not match "alkaline"; PD-L1 matches "PD L1") text_equals_any text, text lists the text equals a value, ignoring case and punctuation stage_group_in stage_group the stage's main group (0, I-IV, read from "IIIA", "Stage IVB" or "4") is in values number_at_least, number_at_most integers compared with values[0] is_stated any the field has a value (values is [])

Choice values must be the field's vocabulary codes. if_not_stated decides what a filter means for an item whose field was not stated (not_stated, "", [], or a line_of_therapy of 0): unknown (the usual choice), no_match or match.

A window is {"anchor", "anchor_criterion", "days_before", "days_after", "if_no_anchor"}: the item's date must lie from days_before days before the anchor to days_after days after it (-1: no limit; 0: not after or not before). Anchors are any_time (no limit; both days -1), reference_date (the evaluation date, by default the patient's latest note date), diagnosis_date (the earliest dated extracted diagnosis, or a supplied one), and criterion_earliest / criterion_latest (the earliest or latest certain match of another criterion, such as the first systemic therapy; anchors may not form a cycle). if_no_anchor is unknown, or reference_date to use the evaluation date when the anchor does not exist (a patient not yet treated). An anchor that may exist but is undated or only possibly matched is unknown and never replaced by the evaluation date; an undated certain match makes the earliest anchor's interval open-ended.

Example: a brain MRI, or a contrast head CT, before the first systemic therapy, when stage III-IV is documented:

{
  "summary": "Brain MRI or head CT before the first systemic therapy, if stage III-IV.",
  "expressible": true, "not_expressible_reason": "",
  "approximations": ["Whether MRI was possible is not extracted; head CT is accepted."],
  "criteria": [
    {"id": "brain_mri", "label": "Brain MRI", "item_type": "imaging_study", "status": "performed",
     "filters": [{"field": "modality", "op": "in", "values": ["mri"], "if_not_stated": "no_match"},
                 {"field": "body_regions", "op": "contains_any", "values": ["brain"], "if_not_stated": "unknown"}],
     "window": {"anchor": "criterion_earliest", "anchor_criterion": "systemic", "days_before": -1,
                "days_after": 0, "if_no_anchor": "reference_date"}, "min_count": 1},
    {"id": "systemic", "label": "Systemic therapy", "item_type": "treatment", "status": "performed",
     "filters": [{"field": "treatment_type", "op": "in", "values": ["systemic_therapy"], "if_not_stated": "no_match"}],
     "window": {"anchor": "any_time", "anchor_criterion": "", "days_before": -1, "days_after": -1,
                "if_no_anchor": "unknown"}, "min_count": 1},
    "... head_ct, stage_3_4 and stage_0_2 criteria ..."
  ],
  "applies_when": {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "stage_3_4", "negated": false}]}]},
  "not_applicable_when": {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "stage_0_2", "negated": false}]},
                                     {"any_of": [{"criterion": "stage_3_4", "negated": true}]}]},
  "requirement": {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "brain_mri", "negated": false},
                                         {"criterion": "head_ct", "negated": false}]}]}
}

The compile prompt's worked examples (matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries.language.EXAMPLES) are complete, validated queries for CT chest within 30 days, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as one or several studies, core or excisional biopsy, this brain MRI, EGFR and ALK testing, and a requirement that cannot be expressed.

docs.title: How results are evaluated
docs.text:
Each test is yes, unknown or no, combined with Kleene logic (AND takes the lower, OR the higher, NOT swaps yes and no).

Dates are intervals of days:

Item date Interval day precision (written, or a report's own study dated by its note) that day month or year precision every day of that month or year evidence_note_date (a patient-level study dated by its earliest evidence note) on or before that date unknown, document level (for example previously_performed with no date) on or before the note's date unknown, planned on or after the note's date unknown, patient level on or before its earliest evidence note

An item is inside a window when its whole interval is, outside when none of it is, and unknown otherwise; anchors are intervals too. So a month-precision CT is unknown against "within 30 days" unless the whole month fits, and an undated "outside CT was done" mention counts for "any time" but is unknown against a recent window.

Deduplication. The same study, procedure, result or course documented in several notes, or at both levels, is one cluster: same item type and kind (for imaging, the modality and overlapping body regions; for procedures, the procedure type; for biomarkers, the marker, result and alteration; for treatments, the type and agents or regimen), compatible dates and the same performed or planned status. An undated or less precise mention joins the most recent compatible dated cluster. A cluster is dated by its most precise member, and passes a filter when a member does, except that the report's own study (this_report) decides when it contradicts a mention. Criteria count clusters: a CT report and a later note mentioning that CT count once.

Criteria. A criterion holds when at least min_count clusters certainly match (status, filters and window), is unknown when enough clusters might, and does not hold otherwise. Planned items never satisfy performed.

Status and applicability:

Status When reason met the requirement holds documented not_met no extracted item documents it not_documented, or planned_only when only planned or ordered items match unknown a matching item's date or details leave it open, its anchor is missing, some of the patient's notes failed extraction or have no record, there are no records, or the requirement is not expressible uncertain_dates, fields_not_stated, anchor_unavailable, incomplete_extraction, no_extraction, not_expressible, query_unavailable not_applicable not_applicable_when holds documented_not_applicable

applicability is applies (no condition, or applies_when holds), not_applicable (documented contrary facts) or uncertain (the condition is not documented, or the facts conflict). Not applicable always needs documented facts.

Each result also carries a machine-made bottom_line (for example "Met: CT chest: CT (chest, abdomen, pelvis), with contrast, 2024-03-02 (day precision, dated by its report, note note-1a2b)"), every criterion's certain and possible counts and anchor, the matching clusters with their dates and mentions, the closest_non_matches (items of the same kind, such as the same modality or marker, that failed only some filters or the window, with what differed; a not-documented explanation names the closest one), and the evidence quotes with their note_id, note_date and character offsets. Matches are listed certain first, then precisely dated before undated mentions, then most recent. aggregate_extraction_workup counts statuses, applicability and reasons per requirement; met / applicable assessed counts met among patients it applies to whose result is met or not met.

docs.title: Compile settings, retries and caching
docs.text:
The workup_query_compile preset section defaults to Nemotron 3.5 Super with sampling_profile: auto, thinking on and structured outputs, 40,000 output tokens in a 131,072-token context (its prompt is about 8,000 tokens). An answer that is not complete JSON or fails validation is retried with its problems named (max_attempts: 3), then once with thinking off (reasoning_off_fallback): three retries in all. Each entry records its attempts (finish reasons and problems, no reasoning) and first_attempt_valid.

Distinct requirements are compiled once per call. Pass cache (any mapping, such as a dict or a folder of JSON files) to reuse compilations across calls: the key (workup_query_cache_key) covers the requirement's name, conditions and category, the population context, the extraction schema version, the query language version (mmai-workup-query-v1), and the prompt and response-schema hashes. A cached query is validated again before use. Compiled queries contain guideline text only.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries
docs.text:
Extraction-based workup checks: guideline requirements as queries over extracted items.

A research review aid beside the note-reading workup reviews (:func:~matchminer_ai.patients.review_patient_workup): an LLM compiles each guideline workup requirement once into a declarative JSON query (:func:compile_workup_queries; its only power is returning the query), code validates it, and code evaluates it deterministically on every patient's structured extraction records (:func:check_workup_with_extractions), with no I/O and no model calls. Results are met, not met (not documented), unknown or not applicable, each with the matching items, their dates and evidence quotes, and a machine-made explanation. They need human review against the source notes.

docs.title: compile_workup_queries
docs.text:
compile_workup_queries(requirements: Sequence[dict], *, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, population_context: str | None = None, cache: MutableMapping[str, dict] | None = None, extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None, progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None, return_metadata: bool = False) -> list[dict] | tuple[list[dict], dict]

Compile each workup requirement into a validated query.

requirements are guideline diagnostic_workup items (name, conditions, category; other keys are ignored). population_context is the guideline population's key criteria, shown to the model as context. Each distinct requirement is one request with config.workup_query_compile; a cached compilation (cache[key] from :func:workup_query_cache_key) is revalidated and reused without a request, and each new successful one is stored in cache.

Returns one entry per requirement, in order: requirement, cache_key, status (compiled or failed), query (None when failed), error, attempts (finish reasons and problems; no reasoning), first_attempt_valid, cached, model and the compile contract. No patient data is involved.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/compile.py 
def compile_workup_queries(
    requirements: Sequence[dict],
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    population_context: str | None = None,
    cache: MutableMapping[str, dict] | None = None,
    extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> list[dict] | tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """Compile each workup requirement into a validated query.

    ``requirements`` are guideline ``diagnostic_workup`` items (``name``,
    ``conditions``, ``category``; other keys are ignored). ``population_context``
    is the guideline population's key criteria, shown to the model as context.
    Each distinct requirement is one request with ``config.workup_query_compile``;
    a cached compilation (``cache[key]`` from :func:`workup_query_cache_key`) is
    revalidated and reused without a request, and each new successful one is
    stored in ``cache``.

    Returns one entry per requirement, in order: ``requirement``, ``cache_key``,
    ``status`` (``compiled`` or ``failed``), ``query`` (None when failed),
    ``error``, ``attempts`` (finish reasons and problems; no reasoning),
    ``first_attempt_valid``, ``cached``, ``model`` and the compile ``contract``.
    No patient data is involved.
    """
    resolved = config or load_default_preset()
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None.")
    if population_context is not None and not isinstance(population_context, str):
        raise TypeError("population_context must be text or None.")
    texts = [requirement_text(r) for r in requirements]
    extensions = default_extensions(resolved) if extensions is None else list(extensions)
    schema = query_response_schema(extensions)
    contract = compile_contract(extensions)
    keys = [workup_query_cache_key(t, population_context, contract=contract) for t in texts]
    settings = section_settings(resolved, SECTION, "workup_query", schema)
    model = settings.runtime.get("model_name")
    progress = progress_callback or (lambda done, total: None)
    entries: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for key in dict.fromkeys(keys):
        saved = cache.get(key) if cache is not None else None
        if (
            isinstance(saved, dict)
            and saved.get("status") == "compiled"
            and saved.get("contract") == contract
            and not validate_workup_query(saved.get("query"), extensions)
        ):
            entries[key] = {**saved, "cached": True}
    pending = [(key, texts[keys.index(key)]) for key in dict.fromkeys(keys) if key not in entries]
    total, done = len(set(keys)), len(entries)
    progress(done, total)
    model_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if pending:
        queue = RequestQueue(
            get_llm_backend(resolved), settings.runtimes, chunk_size=settings.batch_size,
            chunks_in_flight=settings.batches_in_flight,
            model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved.model_metadata_cache_dir,
        )
        attempts: dict[str, list] = {}
        requirement_of = dict(pending)
        for key, text in pending:
            original = [{"role": "user", "content": render_compile_prompt(
                text, population_context, extensions=extensions)}]
            queue.add((key, 1, original), original, "main")

        def finish(key, status, query, error):
            nonlocal done
            history = attempts.get(key, [])
            entries[key] = {
                "cache_key": key,
                "requirement": requirement_of[key],
                "population_context_sha256": digest((population_context or "").strip()),
                "status": status,
                "query": query,
                "error": error,
                "attempts": history,
                "attempt_count": len(history),
                "first_attempt_valid": status == "compiled" and len(history) == 1,
                "contract": contract,
                "model": model,
                "compiled_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                "cached": False,
            }
            if status == "compiled" and cache is not None:
                cache[key] = {k: v for k, v in entries[key].items() if k != "cached"}
            done += 1
            progress(done, total)

        def record(item, answer, reasoning, finish_reason, provenance):
            key, attempt, original = item
            group = attempt_group(attempt, settings)
            entry = attempt_entry(attempt, group, finish_reason, None, debug=False,
                                  answer=None, reasoning=None)
            attempts.setdefault(key, []).append(entry)
            if finish_reason == "error":
                entry["problems"] = ["request failed"]
                finish(key, "failed", None, "the LLM request failed after its transport retries")
                return
            try:
                value = parse_answer(answer, finish_reason)
            except ValueError as exc:
                value, problems, error = None, [], str(exc)
            else:
                problems, error = validate_workup_query(value, extensions), None
            if error is None and not problems:
                finish(key, "compiled", canonical_query(value), None)
                return
            entry["problems"] = [error] if error else problems[:_MAX_PROBLEMS]
            if attempt < settings.total_attempts:
                queue.add((key, attempt + 1, original),
                          _retry(original, answer, value is not None, problems, error),
                          attempt_group(attempt + 1, settings))
                return
            finish(key, "failed", None, "no valid query after every attempt: "
                   + "; ".join(entry["problems"][:5]))

        logger.info("Compiling %d workup queries.", len(pending))
        model_metadata = queue.run(record)
    results = [{**entries[key], "requirement": text} for key, text in zip(keys, texts, strict=True)]
    if not return_metadata:
        return results
    metadata = {
        "contract": contract,
        "model": model,
        # Cached queries keep the model that compiled them, which may differ from model.
        "compiled_by": sorted({entries[key]["model"] for key in set(keys)
                               if entries[key].get("model")}),
        "structured_outputs": settings.structured,
        "requirements": len(texts),
        "distinct": total,
        "cached": sum(1 for key in set(keys) if entries[key].get("cached")),
        "compiled": sum(1 for key in set(keys) if entries[key]["status"] == "compiled"),
        "requests": sum(entries[key].get("attempt_count", 0) for key in set(keys)
                        if not entries[key].get("cached")),
        "first_attempt_valid": sum(1 for key in set(keys) if not entries[key].get("cached")
                                   and entries[key].get("first_attempt_valid")),
        "model_metadata": {k: v for k, v in model_metadata.items() if k != "responses"},
    }
    return results, metadata

docs.title: check_workup_with_extractions
docs.text:
check_workup_with_extractions(records, compiled: Sequence[dict], *, patient_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None, reference_dates: Mapping[str, object] | str | None = None, anchors: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] | None = None, coverage: Mapping[str, Mapping] | None = None) -> dict

Check every compiled workup query on every patient's extraction records.

records: extract_document_records and/or extract_patient_records output (a DataFrame or a list of them), extraction_items output, or record dicts. compiled: :func:compile_workup_queries output (one entry per requirement, in order). patient_ids adds patients with no records (their results are unknown) and fixes the order. reference_dates is one date for everyone or dates by patient; anchors gives a patient's diagnosis_date; coverage adds counts such as notes_without_records by patient.

Returns {"patients": [{"patient_id", "review": {"assessments", "notice", "metadata"}}], "aggregate": [...], "notice"}; each assessment carries the requirement, its status, applicability, reason, bottom_line, criteria, evidence and limitations. Pure computation: no I/O.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/evaluate.py 
def check_workup_with_extractions(
    records,
    compiled: Sequence[dict],
    *,
    patient_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    reference_dates: Mapping[str, object] | str | None = None,
    anchors: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] | None = None,
    coverage: Mapping[str, Mapping] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Check every compiled workup query on every patient's extraction records.

    ``records``: ``extract_document_records`` and/or ``extract_patient_records``
    output (a DataFrame or a list of them), ``extraction_items`` output, or
    record dicts. ``compiled``: :func:`compile_workup_queries` output (one entry
    per requirement, in order). ``patient_ids`` adds patients with no records
    (their results are unknown) and fixes the order. ``reference_dates`` is one
    date for everyone or dates by patient; ``anchors`` gives a patient's
    ``diagnosis_date``; ``coverage`` adds counts such as
    ``notes_without_records`` by patient.

    Returns ``{"patients": [{"patient_id", "review": {"assessments", "notice",
    "metadata"}}], "aggregate": [...], "notice"}``; each assessment carries the
    requirement, its ``status``, ``applicability``, ``reason``, ``bottom_line``,
    criteria, ``evidence`` and ``limitations``. Pure computation: no I/O.
    """
    data = patient_data(records, coverage=coverage)
    ids = [str(p) for p in patient_ids] if patient_ids is not None else sorted(data)
    if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        raise ValueError("patient_ids repeat")
    extensions = _all_extensions()
    queries = []
    for entry in compiled:
        query = entry.get("query") if entry.get("status") == "compiled" else None
        queries.append(check_workup_query(query, extensions) if query is not None else None)
    patients = []
    for pid in ids:
        patient = data.get(pid) or PatientData(pid)
        if isinstance(reference_dates, Mapping):
            reference = reference_dates.get(pid)
        else:
            reference = reference_dates
        assessments = []
        for number, (entry, query) in enumerate(zip(compiled, queries, strict=True)):
            result = evaluate_workup_query(query, patient, reference_date=reference,
                                           anchors=(anchors or {}).get(pid), extensions=extensions)
            assessments.append({
                "recommendation_index": number,
                "recommendation": copy.deepcopy(entry["requirement"]),
                "name": entry["requirement"]["name"],
                **result,
                "query_key": entry.get("cache_key"),
            })
        patients.append({
            "patient_id": pid,
            "review": {
                "assessments": assessments,
                "notice": NOTICE,
                "metadata": {"method": "extraction_queries", "coverage": patient.coverage()},
            },
        })
    requirements = [entry["requirement"] for entry in compiled]
    return {"patients": patients, "aggregate": aggregate_extraction_workup(patients, requirements),
            "notice": NOTICE}

docs.title: evaluate_workup_query
docs.text:
evaluate_workup_query(query: dict | None, patient: PatientData, *, reference_date=None, anchors: Mapping[str, object] | None = None, extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> dict

Evaluate one compiled query on one patient's items (:func:patient_data).

reference_date (YYYY-MM-DD) dates reference_date windows and the if_no_anchor fallback; it defaults to the patient's latest note date. anchors may supply diagnosis_date instead of the earliest extracted diagnosis. Returns status, reason, applicability, a machine-made explanation, each criterion's matches with dates and evidence, and the flattened evidence quotes (note id, note date, quote, character offsets).

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/evaluate.py 
def evaluate_workup_query(
    query: dict | None,
    patient: PatientData,
    *,
    reference_date=None,
    anchors: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
    extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Evaluate one compiled query on one patient's items (:func:`patient_data`).

    ``reference_date`` (YYYY-MM-DD) dates ``reference_date`` windows and the
    ``if_no_anchor`` fallback; it defaults to the patient's latest note date.
    ``anchors`` may supply ``diagnosis_date`` instead of the earliest extracted
    diagnosis. Returns ``status``, ``reason``, ``applicability``, a machine-made
    ``explanation``, each criterion's matches with dates and evidence, and the
    flattened ``evidence`` quotes (note id, note date, quote, character offsets).
    """
    extensions = _all_extensions() if extensions is None else list(extensions)
    if query is None:
        return _result("unknown", "query_unavailable", "uncertain",
                       "Unknown: no valid query could be compiled for this requirement.")
    query = check_workup_query(query, extensions)
    if not query["expressible"]:
        return _result("unknown", "not_expressible", "uncertain",
                       "Unknown: not checkable from extracted items ("
                       f"{query['not_expressible_reason'].strip()})", query=query)
    if not patient.has_records:
        return _result("unknown", "no_extraction", "uncertain",
                       "Unknown: no extraction records are available for this patient.",
                       query=query)
    if reference_date is None:
        reference_date = patient.last_note_date
    reference, reference_text = None, None
    if reference_date is not None:
        value, precision = parse_date(reference_date)
        if value is not None:
            reference, reference_text = date_interval(value, precision), value
    ctx = Context(patient, reference, reference_text, anchors or {},
                  criteria={c["id"]: c for c in query["criteria"]},
                  types={t.name: t for t in item_types(extensions)})
    applies, applies_groups = evaluate_expression(ctx, query["applies_when"])
    excluded, excluded_groups = (
        evaluate_expression(ctx, query["not_applicable_when"])
        if query["not_applicable_when"]["all_of"] else (NO, [])
    )
    if excluded == YES and applies == YES and query["applies_when"]["all_of"]:
        applicability = "uncertain"
    elif excluded == YES:
        applicability = "not_applicable"
    elif applies == YES:
        applicability = "applies"
    else:
        applicability = "uncertain"
    met, groups = evaluate_expression(ctx, query["requirement"])
    notes = []
    if applicability == "uncertain" and query["applies_when"]["all_of"] and applies != YES:
        notes.append("Applicability uncertain: " + "; ".join(
            _explain(ctx, applies_groups, MAYBE if applies == MAYBE else NO)) + ".")
    elif applicability == "uncertain":
        notes.append("Applicability uncertain: documented facts both support and contradict it.")
    evidence = _evidence(ctx, groups)
    if applicability == "not_applicable":
        status, reason = "not_applicable", "documented_not_applicable"
        text = "Not applicable: " + "; ".join(_explain(ctx, excluded_groups, YES)) + "."
        evidence = _evidence(ctx, excluded_groups, (YES,))
    elif met == YES:
        status, reason = "met", "documented"
        text = "Met: " + "; ".join(_explain(ctx, groups, YES)) + "."
    elif met == MAYBE:
        status = "unknown"
        found = {r for state, literals in groups if state == MAYBE for lit, s in literals
                 if s == MAYBE for r in evaluate_criterion(ctx, lit["criterion"]).reasons}
        reason = ("anchor_unavailable" if "anchor_unavailable" in found
                  else "uncertain_dates" if any("date" in r or "mention" in r or "plan" in r
                                                for r in found)
                  else "fields_not_stated")
        text = "Unknown: " + "; ".join(_explain(ctx, groups, MAYBE)) + "."
    else:
        planned = _planned(ctx, groups)
        phrases = _explain(ctx, groups, NO)
        count = sum(len(c.members) for t in ctx.by_type for c in ctx.by_type[t])
        if patient.incomplete:
            status, reason = "unknown", "incomplete_extraction"
            text = ("Unknown: not found in the extraction records (" + "; ".join(phrases)
                    + "), but " + _incomplete(patient) + ".")
        elif planned:
            status, reason = "not_met", "planned_only"
            plans = ", ".join(f"{describe_item(p.cluster.rep)} ({_date_text(p.cluster.rep)})"
                              for p in planned[:3])
            text = (f"Not documented as performed: {'; '.join(phrases)}. Planned or ordered: "
                    f"{plans}.")
            evidence = _evidence_planned(planned)
        else:
            status, reason = "not_met", "not_documented"
            text = (f"Not documented in the extraction records: {'; '.join(phrases)} "
                    f"(among {count} extracted items of the queried types). A missing item "
                    "does not mean the step was not done.")
    if notes and status != "not_applicable":
        text += " " + " ".join(notes)
    criteria = [_criterion_entry(evaluate_criterion(ctx, c["id"])) for c in query["criteria"]]
    limitations = list(query["approximations"])
    if patient.incomplete and status != "unknown":
        limitations.append(_incomplete(patient).capitalize() + ".")
    return _result(status, reason, applicability, text, query=query, criteria=criteria,
                   evidence=evidence, limitations=limitations,
                   reference_date=reference_text)
