The default 0526 TrialSpace and checker models were trained on clinical-space summaries and separate general exclusions, which the example notebook also uses. They accept cohort key and boilerplate criteria but have not been evaluated on them. To run the established workflow, select its legacy extraction mode explicitly:

config = load_preset("default")
config.trial["extraction_method"] = "hierarchical"
trial_spaces = extract_cohorts(trials, config=config)

The patient-centric workflow with those legacy trial spaces has these main steps:

  1. Turn trial descriptions and eligibility criteria into structured trial summaries with extract_cohorts.
  2. Turn patient notes into cancer history summaries with summarize_patients.
  3. Convert the trial and patient summaries into embeddings with embed_for_matching so they can be compared.
  4. Find likely patient-trial pairs with generate_candidate_matches.
  5. Score how reasonable each patient-trial match looks with either score_match_quality or score_match_quality_with_llm.
  6. Screen matched patient-trial pairs for possible exclusion criteria with either exclusion_criteria_check or exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Before installing matchminer-ai, check that you have the compute environment and data needed for the workflow you want to run.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text:
This package requires Python 3.12+.

Steps that use an LLM, such as summarizing patient notes, can run using a model hosted locally or through a remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint. You therefore do not necessarily need a GPU on the computer running matchminer-ai. See our documentation on choosing an inference setup for more information.

Warning

Before sending clinical text to any remote endpoint, make sure the endpoint is approved for your data and institution.

Other parts of the workflow generate embeddings or run classification models locally. These models may be able to run on CPU, but CPU performance has not been formally evaluated and may be impractically slow. We recommend using a GPU for these steps.

See our GPU recommendations documentation for examples of hardware we have used to run the full workflow.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
If you are starting from the beginning of the patient-centric workflow, you need two input tables:

  • trial-level data for extract_cohorts
  • note-level patient data for summarize_patients

docs.title: Trial input
docs.text:
Trial summarization expects one row per trial with trial identifiers, title, brief summary, and eligibility criteria.

If you are preparing trial input from ClinicalTrials.gov, first obtain the study records as JSON and then build one row per study by selecting these fields:

extract_cohorts column ClinicalTrials.gov JSON field trial_id protocolSection.identificationModule.nctId trial_title protocolSection.identificationModule.briefTitle brief_summary protocolSection.descriptionModule.briefSummary eligibility_criteria protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria

docs.title: Patient input
docs.text:
Patient summarization expects one row per clinical note. Each row should include a patient identifier, note text, and note date.

Users are responsible for preparing note-level input data approved for their environment.

docs.title: Detailed input requirements
docs.text:
See the extract_cohorts and summarize_patients API docs for current DataFrame column requirements.

The example notebook uses sample input data from examples/data/, which is the best place to inspect the expected input shape when preparing your own data.

You do not always have to start at the beginning. There are entry points later in the workflow if you already have summaries, embeddings, candidate matches, or other intermediate results. The input requirements for those entry points are documented with the corresponding Package API pages.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Most package behavior is controlled through configuration. Configuration tells matchminer-ai which models to use, whether LLM calls should run locally or through a remote endpoint, where to cache model metadata, and how individual workflow steps should be run.

Most users can start with the built-in default settings. You usually only need to change configuration when you want to change models, switch between local and remote inference, adjust runtime settings, enable debug output, or point the package at a different endpoint.

Use load_default_preset() when you want to start from the package defaults and change a few values in Python:

from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote["enabled"] = True
config.remote["server_urls"] = ["http://localhost:8000/v1"]

docs.title: Custom Config Files
docs.text:
The optional guideline extractor uses config.guideline with the same task-level remote.model_name, remote.request_params, and remote.extra_body structure. It requires shared remote mode and writes to an explicit external output directory. See guideline extraction for context, output reserve, reasoning, concurrency, and source-provenance settings. Existing custom YAML files without a guideline section continue to load; copy that section from the default preset before using this optional API.

For package installs, treat the built-in preset files as read-only package data. For larger or reusable changes, copy the default preset values into a YAML file in your project, edit them, and load that file by path:

from matchminer_ai import load_config

config = load_config("my_config.yaml")

docs.title: debug_mode
docs.text: Boolean flag used by summarization postprocessing. When true, selected intermediate columns are retained in output tables.

docs.title: model_metadata_cache_dir
docs.text: Directory path used by model metadata helpers to cache Hugging Face model metadata JSON files.

docs.title: Returned Metadata
docs.text:
Functions with return_metadata=True return the package version, resolved configuration snapshot, and model provenance collected by the package. Model metadata is keyed by the public operation that used the model:

{
  "model_metadata": {
    "summarize_patients": {
      "model_name": "organization/model",
      "model_sha": "..."
    }
  }
}

For HTTP inference, the entry describes the requested remote.model_name looked up on Hugging Face. When that name is not a Hub model ID, model_sha is openai-compatible-endpoint and metadata_error records the lookup failure. Where the server reports per-response provenance, it is listed under responses. Neither verifies the weights the endpoint actually serves.

Payloads written before 0.6 used role keys such as embedding_model and match_quality_checker. Readers of saved embedding metadata still accept embedding_model.

docs.title: remote
docs.text:
Global transport settings used when remote.enabled is true and LLM tasks send OpenAI-compatible chat completion requests to external endpoints. The default tested setup is a vLLM server with a compatible reasoning parser. Task-specific request payload settings live under each task's remote block. The remote backend reads the API key from the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable. API keys are not stored in preset files.

Google Agent Platform (Gemini and MaaS) is supported through its OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions route. Set remote.provider to google_agent_platform; the package then uses Google Application Default Credentials (ADC), refreshes the OAuth access token for each request, converts a leading system message to the user-first form required by managed open models, and omits vLLM-only extra_body values. Install-time dependencies include google-auth; credential files and tokens are never stored in package configuration.

docs.title: remote.enabled
docs.text: Selects the remote LLM backend when true.

docs.title: remote.provider
docs.text:
Authentication and message-compatibility profile. openai is the default and reads OPENAI_API_KEY. google_agent_platform uses ADC and ignores OPENAI_API_KEY. databricks_anthropic sends structured requests to Claude through a Databricks AI Gateway's Anthropic Messages route, authenticated with a Databricks profile (databricks_profile). Only structured requests support it, such as the SQL workup agent; see SQL-agent workup checks.

For example, Gemma 4 26B A4B IT MaaS in a project named profile-notes uses:

config.remote.update(
    {
        "enabled": True,
        "provider": "google_agent_platform",
        "google_project_id": "profile-notes",
        "server_urls": [
            "https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/profile-notes/"
            "locations/global/endpoints/openapi"
        ],
    }
)
for task in (
    config.trial,
    config.patient,
    config.llm_match_quality,
    config.llm_exclusion_criteria,
    config.llm_good_option,
):
    task["remote"]["model_name"] = "google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-maas"

Set up ADC through the runtime environment, an attached service account, or gcloud auth application-default login. The selected endpoint must still be authorized for the sensitivity of any clinical text sent to it.

check_openai_endpoint() uses a minimal patient-free chat completion for this provider because the MaaS OpenAI route does not document /models.

Gemini 3.8 Flash uses the same global endpoint and ADC profile with model google/gemini-3.8-flash. System messages are retained for Gemini. Its supported reasoning efforts are low, medium, and high; the provider maps an xhigh request to high. Explicit sampling fields and vLLM extensions are omitted, because Gemini 3.8 manages sampling internally.

For patient summarization and review_patient_workup, configure the patient task after setting the Google remote profile above:

config.patient.update(
    sampling_profile="none", reasoning_effort="high",
    context_window=1048576, tokenizer_mode="bytes",
)
config.patient["local"]["engine"]["max_model_len"] = 1048576
config.patient["local"]["chat_template_kwargs"] = {}
config.patient["remote"].update(
    model_name="google/gemini-3.8-flash",
    tokenizer_name="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
    request_params={"max_tokens": 65536, "reasoning_effort": "high"},
    extra_body={},
)

The local tokenizer supplies chunk boundaries only; byte accounting conservatively bounds the hosted-model prompt instead of claiming exact Gemini token counts. Workup review skips vLLM discovery/tokenization routes, refreshes ADC for structured requests, and retains its normal JSON schema and exact patient-note quote validation. These settings do not change a separately configured guideline catalog run.

docs.title: remote.google_project_id
docs.text: Optional Google Cloud quota project supplied when remote.provider is google_agent_platform. The endpoint URL still determines the project that receives the inference request.

docs.title: remote.server_urls
docs.text:
List of OpenAI-compatible base URLs. Values are passed to the OpenAI client as base_url. For the default Nemotron 3.5 Super configuration, the server should be a vLLM chat endpoint launched with the nemotron_v3 reasoning parser, the qwen3_coder tool-call parser and --trust-remote-code; the package start_vllm_servers() helper adds these flags from the selected LLM task's reasoning_parser, tool_call_parser and local engine settings.

Model names and request parameters are configured per LLM task under that task's backend block. For example, trial.local.model_name is the model loaded by local vLLM, trial.remote.model_name is the model string sent to the endpoint, trial.remote.request_params contains top-level chat completion request fields, and trial.remote.extra_body contains fields sent through request extra_body.

Remote mode expects the endpoint to return final answer text in message.content. The default vLLM/Nemotron setup can expose reasoning separately via vLLM reasoning parser support. Other OpenAI-compatible endpoints may work only if they return final answer text in message.content; endpoints that include reasoning text in message.content are not currently supported.

docs.title: remote.max_concurrent_requests
docs.text: Maximum number of concurrent requests per remote server; default 32. Guideline clients in one Python process share this cap across diseases for the same endpoint. Independent processes have separate caps, so use the collection runner rather than launching multiple independent 32-request processes.

docs.title: remote.request_timeout
docs.text: Request timeout in seconds.

docs.title: remote.max_retries
docs.text: Maximum retry attempts for a failed remote request. The package disables the OpenAI SDK's separate internal retry loop so this setting is the single retry bound.

docs.title: remote.batch_size
docs.text: Number of prompts processed per remote-server batch.

docs.title: remote.retry_backoff_base
docs.text: Base value, in seconds, for exponential retry backoff.

docs.title: Model-aware sampling and reasoning
docs.text:
The default preset sets sampling_profile: auto and reasoning_effort: xhigh on every LLM stage: trial, patient, llm_match_quality, llm_exclusion_criteria, and guideline. The selected model determines defaults for both in-process vLLM and OpenAI-compatible vLLM requests. Quantized model IDs containing the same family name are recognized. Guideline discovery applies the profile after /v1/models identifies the actual served model.

Model / mode Temperature Top-p Top-k Other sampling defaults Nemotron 3.5 Super (default) 1.0 0.95 Disabled (-1) min-p 0, presence penalty 0, repetition penalty 1 Gemma 4 1.0 0.95 64 Engine defaults for penalties Qwen 3.8, thinking 1.0 0.95 20 min-p 0, presence penalty 0, repetition penalty 1 Qwen 3.8, non-thinking 0.7 0.8 20 min-p 0, presence penalty 1.5, repetition penalty 1 Reflection Beam 1.0 0.7 0.99 Disabled (-1) min-p 0, presence penalty 0, repetition penalty 1

Nemotron's temperature and top-p follow NVIDIA's model card (checked 2026-10-15); its other sampling controls are neutral. The others follow the vendor recommendations checked on 2026-09-24: Google Gemma 4, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, and Qwen3.8-27B. Beam's temperature, top-p, and repetition penalty follow its generation configuration, verified on 2026-10-16; its other sampling controls are neutral. Official Beam 1.0 IDs, quantized variants, and the short aliases beam and reflection-beam are recognized. Local server startup selects beam for both reasoning and tool parsing and requires a Beam-compatible vLLM build. Beam always reasons. The workspace defaults chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort to medium rather than the upstream template's max, without inferring an enable_thinking switch. Explicit template or API effort overrides and output budgets are retained. When both API and template effort are supplied, they must agree.

Qwen defaults to thinking enabled, preserved thinking, and xhigh effort. Supported effort values are xhigh, medium, and low. Remote requests send reasoning_effort at the API level and in chat_template_kwargs; local prompt rendering and endpoint token counting use the same template setting. Gemma 4 supports thinking enabled/disabled, not graded reasoning effort: its profile sets enable_thinking: true and does not invent an xhigh control.

Explicit local.generation, local.chat_template_kwargs, remote.request_params, and remote.extra_body values override profile defaults. To turn thinking off, set the applicable chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking to false. The Qwen profile then selects the non-thinking sampling defaults. Set a stage's sampling_profile to none to use entirely explicit settings; gemma4, qwen3.8, and reflection-beam (or beam) also allow explicit family selection for endpoint aliases. Unknown model families receive no automatic vendor settings. Existing custom configs without sampling_profile keep their explicit behavior, with one exception: a section without sampling_profile served by Nemotron 3.5 Super (any ...nemotron-3.5-super-vl... model name, profile replaces_task_sampling; user instruction 2026-11-05) sends NVIDIA's sampling (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k -1, min_p 0, repetition_penalty 1.0) in place of its fixed values, on the local and remote paths, keeping an explicit thinking switch. Name a profile (explicit keys then win) or set sampling_profile: none to keep a section's own sampling for Nemotron.

This intentionally replaces the earlier preset's greedy patient/checker LLM sampling and mismatched Gemma top-k. Matching model versions, output budgets, and clinical prompts are unchanged. Existing generated artifacts retain their original settings; changed extraction settings require a fresh run directory.

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote["enabled"] = True
config.remote["server_urls"] = ["http://your-server:8001/v1"]
config.remote["max_concurrent_requests"] = 32
config.trial["remote"]["model_name"] = "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next"
# For patient summarization, update both model_name and tokenizer_name.
# Optional explicit override:
config.trial["remote"]["request_params"]["reasoning_effort"] = "medium"

Model-specific reasoning text: the literal Reasoning: high system header is added only for GPT-OSS model identities. Gemma, Nemotron, Qwen, and other families use their configured chat-template/API thinking controls; task instructions are preserved without the GPT-OSS header. Unknown model identities receive no header.

docs.title: trial
docs.text: Task configuration for trial summarization.

docs.title: trial.local
docs.text:
Local in-process vLLM runtime settings:

  • model_name: model identifier loaded by local vLLM and used for local tokenizer/chat-template rendering and model metadata lookup.
  • engine: keyword arguments passed to vllm.LLM(...); the package passes model=trial.local.model_name separately. Every default engine serves Nemotron 3.5 Super as the production servers do: trust_remote_code, language_model_only, enable_prefix_caching, mamba_backend: flashinfer, mamba_ssm_cache_dtype: float16, enable_mamba_cache_stochastic_rounding, mamba_cache_philox_rounds: 5 and mamba_cache_mode: align, with tensor_parallel_size: 1 (the NVFP4 build needs a Blackwell GPU). The vLLM server helpers pass these keys as the same vllm serve flags.
  • generation: keyword arguments passed to vllm.SamplingParams(...).
  • chat_template_kwargs: keyword arguments passed to tokenizer chat-template rendering.

Additional engine and generation keys may be included if they are valid vLLM keyword arguments. vLLM validates those keys when the engine/request is created.

docs.title: trial.prompt_files
docs.text: Prompt template filenames loaded from matchminer_ai.prompts for the legacy one_shot method (primer, question).

docs.title: trial.cohorts
docs.text: Settings of the default cohorts method, the three-step workflow shared with protocol_cohort_extraction: max_attempts (per request, 1-10, default 3), structured_outputs (default true; each remote request is constrained by its step's JSON schema), chunk_size (default 500) and chunks_in_flight (default 2, at most 16), and optional prompt_files mapping screen, list and criteria to other packaged prompt files. A remote backend keeps chunk_size * chunks_in_flight requests in flight, sending each on its own as another returns, so one slow answer holds up only itself; a local backend gets batches of chunk_size requests of one step, chunks_in_flight at once. The merge and boilerplate steps (merge_equivalent_cohorts, remove_boilerplate_criteria) and screen_trials use the same settings.

docs.title: trial.reasoning_parser
docs.text: vLLM reasoning parser name. The default auto resolves known model names, including the default nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 to nemotron_v3 and google/gemma-4-31B-it to gemma4. Set this explicitly when using a model not covered by the package mapping, or use none to disable reasoning parsing for a non-reasoning model. This setting applies to local vLLM execution and vLLM server launch helpers; non-vLLM remote endpoints may ignore it or return no separate reasoning field.

docs.title: trial.remote
docs.text:
Task-specific remote chat completion request settings:

  • model_name: model name sent in OpenAI-compatible chat completion requests and used for remote endpoint metadata.
  • request_params: top-level chat completion request fields sent as-is, including the output-token budget. Use max_tokens for vLLM and many compatible endpoints, or max_completion_tokens for endpoints that require it.
  • extra_body: provider-specific fields sent as request extra_body when non-empty.

The package interprets model_name and fills missing values from the selected sampling profile. Explicit values inside request_params and extra_body otherwise pass through; the Qwen profile validates its supported reasoning levels. The OpenAI client or remote endpoint validates other API fields.

docs.title: trial.boilerplate_marker
docs.text: Line marker used by trial postprocessing to identify the boilerplate exclusion section heading.

docs.title: patient
docs.text: Task configuration for patient summarization.

docs.title: patient.chunk_size
docs.text: Maximum character count used when splitting patient notes into serial summary chunks.

docs.title: patient.chunk_overlap
docs.text: Character overlap between adjacent patient-note chunks.

docs.title: patient.prompt_margin_tokens
docs.text: Token margin reserved when truncating patient chunks before prompt rendering.

docs.title: patient.scheduling
docs.text:
How serial summarization shares the backend among patients: continuous (default) or rounds. Each patient's chunks are always summarized in order, each prompt carrying the summary accepted for the previous chunk.

  • continuous: with a remote backend, each patient's next chunk is sent as soon as the previous one is final, after its quality retries. Up to the endpoints' request capacity is in flight: each listed server's remote.max_concurrent_requests, or with an endpoint pool the sum of its registry's per-server ceilings (upstream_concurrency), reread while it runs; an adaptive pool's requests above its current limits wait for its slots. Waiting patients start longest remaining chain first, so a patient with many chunks starts early instead of finishing last. A local engine, which batches prompts itself, uses rounds.
  • rounds: the first chunk of every patient is sent as one batch, then every second chunk, and so on, so each round waits for its slowest patient.

Prompts are built in patient.prompt_build_workers processes under both. The two give the same prompts, quality checks, retries and results, and either can resume the other's checkpoint_dir, including round files from runs before the chunk journal (see Resuming patient summarization). Under an endpoint pool, rounds also reports its first round's per-request endpoints in model_metadata["responses"]; continuous reports where each request ran only in the debug attempt traces.

docs.title: patient.local
docs.text: Local in-process vLLM runtime settings. See trial.local. The patient context (engine.max_model_len, 200,000 tokens) also bounds remote requests: each one's output budget (max_tokens, 50,000) is reduced to what fits after its prompt.

docs.title: patient.prompt_files
docs.text: Prompt template filenames loaded from matchminer_ai.prompts.

docs.title: patient.reasoning_parser
docs.text: vLLM reasoning parser name. The default auto resolves known model names, including the default nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 to nemotron_v3 and google/gemma-4-31B-it to gemma4. Set this explicitly when using a model not covered by the package mapping, or use none to disable reasoning parsing for a non-reasoning model. Non-vLLM remote endpoints may return no separate reasoning field.

docs.title: patient.remote
docs.text: Task-specific remote chat completion request settings. See trial.remote. Patient summarization also supports tokenizer_name, which is the local tokenizer used for patient chunk truncation and prompt sizing before sending requests to the remote endpoint. For self-hosted vLLM this is usually the same as patient.remote.model_name.

docs.title: patient.text_token_threshold
docs.text: Maximum token count used by local truncation before patient summarization.

docs.title: document_extraction
docs.text:
Configuration for patients.extract_document_records, which extracts one structured record per note (see Structured Clinical Extraction). Its local, remote, sampling_profile, reasoning_effort and reasoning_parser fields follow the other LLM task sections; the default model is Nemotron 3.5 Super with its own sampling (sampling_profile: auto).

  • max_document_characters (default 200,000): longer notes fail rather than being truncated.
  • max_attempts (1-10, default 3): attempts per note for an answer that fails validation, including a quote that is not in the note. With reasoning_off_fallback (default true) one more attempt runs with thinking off. After the last attempt, items left without any quote found in the note are dropped and the record is partial; any other problem fails the note.
  • structured_outputs (default true): with the remote backend, each request carries the record's strict JSON schema as response_format (vLLM structured outputs).
  • batch_size (default 256) and batches_in_flight (default 2, at most 16): a local backend gets batches of batch_size, batches_in_flight at once. A remote backend keeps as many requests in flight as its servers take, remote.max_concurrent_requests for each listed server, each sent as another returns, so that cap alone sets a run's concurrency; it is never fewer than batch_size * batches_in_flight, which also applies to servers from a registry file (remote.server_urls_file, whose own ceilings then limit each server).
  • extensions (default []): disease-specific item types and guidance by name; the package provides thoracic.
  • ncit_agent_codes (default false): add each treatment agent's NCIt concept from the bundled NCIt snapshot (ncit_resource, by default good_option_catalog.ncit_resource).

The default completion budget is 50,000 tokens, reasoning included (Nemotron often reasons for 10,000-15,000 tokens before an answer whose quotes add more; one synthetic molecular report took 29,867), in a 131,072-token local context. A remote completion of that length can take far longer than the default remote.request_timeout of 600 seconds on a busy server; raise it (for example to 7,200 seconds), since the endpoint pool retries timed-out requests from the start.

docs.title: patient_extraction
docs.text:
Configuration for patients.extract_patient_records, which builds one record per patient from all of their notes. It takes the document_extraction keys above except max_document_characters, plus:

  • chunk_tokens (default 40,000) and chunk_overlap_tokens (default 500): notes are packed in date order into chunks of at most chunk_tokens tokens of the model's tokenizer (remote.tokenizer_name, or the model name); a longer note is split at token boundaries with that overlap.
  • context_tokens (default null, meaning local.engine.max_model_len): a chunk's prompt, including the record so far, plus the completion budget must fit; a patient whose next prompt would not fit fails rather than being truncated.

The default local batch is 64 requests, the completion budget 60,000 tokens and the local context 200,000 tokens. A remote backend keeps remote.max_concurrent_requests requests per server in flight, as for document_extraction; each patient's chunks still run one after another.

docs.title: workup_sql_agent
docs.text:
Configuration for patients.compile_workup_sql (see SQL-Agent Workup Checks). For each distinct workup requirement, an LLM agent explores an extraction database with read-only SQL in an isolated worker and accepts one cohort-level query. It needs an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (remote.enabled; a local vLLM server works), not an in-process engine. Exploration results are patient-derived extracted values (no ids, note text or quotes) and reach that endpoint.

Top-level keys: - max_attempts (3): attempts per turn for an invalid action. - structured_outputs (true): JSON-schema responses; false sends the schema in the prompt only. - tokenizer_mode (bytes): conservative local prompt budgets; endpoint counts with /tokenize. - context_window (null): null uses local.engine.max_model_len, then the endpoint's /v1/models. - request_timeout (600): seconds a turn's request may go without data before it is retried, instead of the shared remote.request_timeout. A 429 or 503 is waited out (from 10 s, at most 60 s) within max_attempts. - sampling_profile, reasoning_effort (high) and reasoning_parser, as for other LLM sections. - local / remote: the model, with 32,000 completion tokens per turn by default.

limits keys: - max_actions (12) and max_submits (3). - submit_by (6): the action by which the agent is asked to submit a first candidate. - max_review_queries (3): checking queries allowed after a valid submission. Then code removes the query action, and the agent accepts the submission or submits a revision. - max_rows (30), max_cell_chars (160) and max_result_chars (6,000): what the agent sees of a result. - max_memory_chars (4,000), max_recent_steps (8), max_sql_chars (16,000). - max_search_terms (8) and max_search_rows (50): words per search, and matching text values a search shows. - max_detail_chars (300) and max_evidence_items (8): per-patient output. - sample_rows_per_status (3): example rows shown after a submission. - max_concurrent_items (8): requirements explored at once, sharing one worker. Each turn is one request, so the agent's request cap is raised to at least this. - query_timeout_seconds (20) and final_timeout_seconds (120). - worker_memory_mb (4,096) and duckdb_memory_mb (2,048).

docs.title: trial_space_criteria_extraction
docs.text:
Configuration for extracting the complete inclusion and exclusion criteria relevant to one trial space from a UTF-8 OCR text file. Its local, remote, and reasoning_parser fields select the same LLM backend pattern as other tasks.

  • max_document_characters: hard input bound. Oversized documents fail rather than being silently truncated and losing criteria.
  • max_criteria_per_type: maximum number of inclusion criteria and maximum number of exclusion criteria accepted from the model.
  • response_retry_limit: retry bound for malformed JSON, invalid schemas, duplicate criteria, and criteria that are not grounded in the OCR text.

The default extraction task keeps model thinking enabled and allows up to 50,000 completion tokens. The default remote request uses JSON-object response formatting. The entire OCR document and trial space reach the configured LLM backend; no web search is used. Every accepted criterion must match a source excerpt after conservative whitespace, ordinal-suffix, repeated page-edge, and referenced trailing-footnote normalization.

docs.title: protocol_cohort_extraction
docs.text:
Configuration for extract_protocol_cohorts, which screens full protocol documents (PDF, OCR text or Markdown) and extracts their cohort eligibility criteria. Its local, remote, sampling_profile, reasoning_effort and reasoning_parser fields follow the other LLM task sections.

  • max_document_characters: hard input bound (default 800,000 characters). Oversized documents fail rather than being truncated.
  • max_attempts: validation attempts per request (1-10, default 3); only failed requests are retried, and a cohort that fails every attempt fails its protocol.
  • chunk_size (default 500) and chunks_in_flight (default 2, at most 16): a remote backend keeps chunk_size * chunks_in_flight requests in flight, each sent as another returns; a local backend gets batches of chunk_size requests of one step, chunks_in_flight at once. With output_dir, each protocol is saved as soon as it is decided.
  • structured_outputs: when true and the remote backend is enabled, each request carries a strict JSON-schema response_format for its step.
  • prompt_files (optional): maps screen, list and criteria to other packaged prompt files; by default protocols use the same three prompts as ctgov listings (trial.cohorts.screen.user.txt, trial.cohorts.list.user.txt, trial.cohorts.criteria.user.txt).

The default model context is 262,144 tokens with up to 50,000 completion tokens, so that full industry protocols (often 50,000-160,000 tokens) fit with room for reasoning.

docs.title: synthetic_protocol_generation
docs.text:
Configuration for generate_synthetic_protocols. Its local, remote, sampling_profile, reasoning_effort and reasoning_parser fields follow the other LLM task sections.

  • chunk_size (default 500) and chunks_in_flight (default 2, at most 16): a remote backend keeps chunk_size * chunks_in_flight requests in flight, each sent as another returns, so one slow protocol holds up only itself; a local backend gets batches of chunk_size, chunks_in_flight at once. Outputs are written when their request returns.
  • max_attempts: attempts per trial for empty or truncated outputs (1-10, default 3).
  • layouts_file: optional override of synthetic_protocol_layouts.json.

The default model context is 262,144 tokens with up to 100,000 completion tokens, so long protocols and reasoning traces fit.

docs.title: embedding
docs.text:
Configuration for TrialSpace embedding. Retrieval embeds key text only: patient key sections (cancer_history_summary) and cohort key criteria (cohort_key_criteria); see the embedding API.

The section maps onto the training repository's encoder settings (matchminer_ai.embedding.encoder.EncoderSettings), and embed_for_matching loads and encodes with the same functions training's mining uses, so the default encodes exactly as training encoded its model.

docs.title: embedding.model_path
docs.text:
Sentence-transformer model path or Hub id passed to SentenceTransformer(...).

The default is a local, unpublished directory, on purpose (user, 2026-11-12): the n=5000 run's round-2 TrialSpace, /ksg/kehl_mm_data/mmai/v23/data/no_phi/synthetic_dataset_n5000_screened_20261106/trialspace/models/trialspace_round2 (google/embeddinggemma-2 fine-tuned by finetune_embedder.py). A path that starts with / or ., or that exists, must be a readable directory; otherwise embedding (and embedding token counts) fail with FileNotFoundError, so runs off camus or its NFS mount stop instead of mixing vectors. Nothing falls back to ksg-dfci/TrialSpace-0526 or any Hub model. The model was saved by sentence-transformers 6.1 and needs 6.1 or later to load.

docs.title: embedding.device
docs.text: Device string passed to SentenceTransformer(...). Autocast applies on CUDA only, so CPU vectors (float32 throughout) are not interchangeable with CUDA vectors; the encoder identity stored with cached vectors records which was used.

docs.title: embedding.dtype, embedding.autocast
docs.text: Weight precision (float32 or bfloat16) and CUDA autocast precision (bfloat16). The defaults, float32 and bfloat16, are training's mining settings. Absent, the model's own dtype is kept and autocast is off.

docs.title: embedding.prompt_profile, embedding.default_prompt_name
docs.text: prompt_profile: trialspace applies trialspace_contract.model_prompts("trialspace") over the model's saved prompts, as mining does: patients are encoded with patient_summary and cohorts with this_space. A TrialSpace trained by matchminer-ai-training saves the same prompts. default_prompt_name (SentenceSimilarity) is the prompt for calls that name none. Absent, the model's saved prompts are used unchanged.

docs.title: embedding.include_prompt_in_pooling, embedding.text_only
docs.text: Mean pooling over the prompt tokens as well as the text (true, as trained), and loading EmbeddingGemma 2 without its vision and audio towers (true). These settings are specific to EmbeddingGemma 2 TrialSpace models; remove them when pointing model_path at another model family.

docs.title: embedding.batch_size
docs.text:
Texts per encoder batch (default 32, as mining encodes; 12 when absent).

On CUDA, embedding first uses PyTorch's default scaled-dot-product-attention dispatcher. If cuDNN reports that it cannot build a valid attention execution plan, the package retries with the CUDA flash, memory-efficient, or math attention backends and remembers that fallback for the same model and device. Other runtime errors are not retried.

docs.title: embedding.prompt_file
docs.text: Prompt filename loaded from matchminer_ai.prompts and used as the query prompt only for a model that saved none and has no prompt_profile (so never for the default); a model's saved prompts are never replaced. The file is prepended exactly as written (only its final newline is removed). The default, embedding.txt, is byte-identical to TrialSpace-0526's saved query prompt, including its trailing space. A TrialSpace model that saves prompts named patient_summary and this_space encodes each side with its own prompt.

docs.title: embedding.max_seq_length
docs.text:
Runtime truncation cutoff for embedding inputs (default 4096, the round-2 fit's cap; the n=5000 round-3 mining encoded at 8,192, which changed one synthetic cohort in 15,263). SentenceTransformer uses this value during encode(), so inputs longer than this limit are truncated before embedding generation. QC reports use the same value, counting tokens with each side's prompt, when flagging key text that exceeds the embedding input limit.

This value should match the model_path configured alongside it — it is specific to the embedding model in use, not a general-purpose default. Changing embedding.model_path to a different model without reviewing max_seq_length against that model's own native truncation cutoff (e.g. its sentence_bert_config.json) can silently truncate inputs at the wrong point, producing different embeddings than the model would otherwise produce for longer inputs.

docs.title: decision_model
docs.text: The decision model that answers the match, boilerplate and per-criterion yes/no questions (matchminer_ai.matching.decision_model; see the match-quality, exclusion-criteria and criteria-check APIs). It runs in-process with Transformers and the checkpoint's own System One code (trust_remote_code).

docs.title: decision_model.model_name
docs.text: A Hugging Face model id or a local checkpoint directory (default LiquidAI/d1-2B). A checkpoint fine-tuned by the training repository's train_decision_model.py is a local directory holding the weights, the d1 code and decision_contract.json, whose fingerprint is reported as model_sha.

docs.title: decision_model.revision
docs.text: The commit of a Hub model (default 652f920e544ea37f81e4b0ce89b81d4ed0da90b1, d1-2B's main on 2026-11-05). Required for every Hub model, because its code runs; ignored for a local directory.

docs.title: decision_model.backend
docs.text: transformers (the only backend).

docs.title: decision_model.device / decision_model.dtype
docs.text: Where the model runs (default cuda) and its weight type (default bfloat16).

docs.title: decision_model.max_length
docs.text: The fine-tuning request length (default 10000 tokens). Longer requests still run, without truncation, and are counted in the metadata's over_max_length.

docs.title: decision_model.set_size
docs.text: Questions read together after one state (null, the default, uses the model's trained size, 16). Larger is faster and departs from training.

docs.title: decision_model.token_budget / decision_model.batch_size
docs.text: Padded tokens per forward pass (default 65536) and requests per system_one_batch call (default 256).

docs.title: decision_model.compile
docs.text: torch.compile the model before use (default false).

docs.title: match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff
docs.text: Minimum P(reasonable) (match_quality_reasonableness, the decision model's potentially-eligible answer) for match_quality_pass == true (default 0.5); score_match_quality(filter_low_quality=True) keeps only passing pairs. match_quality_score ranks pairs and is not a pass criterion. Until 2026-11-17 the pass was match_quality_score >= score_cutoff (0.2), which only approximated this answer and rejected reasonable pairs whose cohort was not specific on any dimension; an old score_cutoff key is ignored.

docs.title: exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff
docs.text: Minimum P(yes) of the boilerplate question (yes = potentially eligible) for exclusion_criteria_pass == true (default 0.5).

docs.title: criteria_check.fail_cutoff
docs.text: A criteria line whose P(yes) (yes = the patient does not clearly fail the line) is below this is flagged criterion_clearly_fails (default 0.5).

docs.title: llm_match_quality
docs.text: Configuration for the LLM-based match-quality checker.

docs.title: llm_match_quality.local
docs.text: Local in-process vLLM runtime settings. See trial.local. The default context is 100,000 tokens with 32,768 completion tokens, reasoning included (the training teacher's label budget for the same prompt).

docs.title: llm_match_quality.prompt_file
docs.text: System prompt filename loaded from matchminer_ai.prompts. The default, match_quality.labels.system.txt, is the training teacher's five-label prompt; a replacement must return the same JSON contract.

docs.title: llm_match_quality.reasoning_parser
docs.text: vLLM reasoning parser name. The default auto resolves known model names, including the default nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 to nemotron_v3 and google/gemma-4-31B-it to gemma4. Non-vLLM remote endpoints may return no separate reasoning field.

docs.title: llm_match_quality.remote
docs.text: Task-specific remote chat completion request settings. See trial.remote.

docs.title: llm_exclusion_criteria
docs.text: Configuration for the LLM-based exclusion-criteria checker.

docs.title: llm_exclusion_criteria.local
docs.text: Local in-process vLLM runtime settings. See trial.local. The default context is 100,000 tokens with 32,768 completion tokens, reasoning included (the training teacher's boilerplate-label budget for the same prompt).

docs.title: llm_exclusion_criteria.prompt_file
docs.text: Prompt template filename loaded from matchminer_ai.prompts. The default, llm_exclusion_criteria.user.txt, asks whether the patient clearly fails any of the cohort's boilerplate criteria.

docs.title: llm_exclusion_criteria.reasoning_parser
docs.text: vLLM reasoning parser name. The default auto resolves known model names, including the default nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 to nemotron_v3 and google/gemma-4-31B-it to gemma4. Non-vLLM remote endpoints may return no separate reasoning field.

docs.title: llm_exclusion_criteria.remote
docs.text: Task-specific remote chat completion request settings. See trial.remote.

docs.title: llm_good_option
docs.text: Configuration for experimental-drug selection during patient-free research and for the patient-specific four-point-per-drug LLM scorer. Its local and remote blocks follow the same structure as trial.local and trial.remote. The default request enables model thinking, permits up to 100,000 completion tokens within a 262,144-token local context, and uses a repetition penalty of 1.1. Each scoring message describes exactly one patient; the backend may batch many independent messages in one run. score_good_options_with_llm can selectively retry code-validation failures with max_parse_attempts; each follow-up includes the prior invalid answer, exact parser error, and finish reason. Set reasoning_off_fallback=True to add one final attempt with thinking disabled after the ordinary attempts are exhausted.

docs.title: good_option_catalog
docs.text:
Configuration for patient-free trial drug extraction, evidence synthesis, and clean task-specific projections. synthesis_evidence_max_tokens bounds the raw evidence packed for one drug, and it bounds passage text only: the JSON scaffolding around the passages adds roughly 6.5%, so the real prompt costs about 1.08x this value. It defaults to 190,000, which pairs with the 262,144 max_model_len of the local synthesis engine and leaves roughly 50,000 tokens for a reasoning trace and the final JSON. Evidence beyond the budget is discarded round-robin across sources before the model sees it, so a lower value silently drops passages rather than failing; when serving a smaller context, reduce it to about (context - completion budget) / 1.08. Synthesis reads the ledger in synthesis_chunk_max_tokens chunks (default 60,000; classes use class_evidence_max_tokens). Each chunk's call sees the facts so far and returns only new or revised items, which code merges in: an existing fact is removed only when a validated item names it in replaces. The stage-specific synthesis_llm override defaults to a 100,000-token completion budget so reasoning-enabled models can think over a chunk and still finish the final JSON. Larger chunks are not better: on 40 multi-chunk drugs with Gemma 4 31B, 100,000-token chunks gave about 25% fewer facts and cited passages than 60,000, because the model condenses more of each chunk. A chunk plus passage metadata, the existing facts (up to about 25,000 tokens for the broadest classes), and this budget must fit together in the served context; lower both chunk limits when serving less than 262,144 tokens, since the endpoint rejects a request whose prompt plus max_tokens exceeds its context. A model that exhausts the budget mid-trace returns an empty answer with finish_reason=length, which is retried rather than silently accepted, and if every ordinary attempt ends that way the final attempt disables thinking. screening_max_attempts and synthesis_max_attempts control structured-output retries. screening_checkpoint_batch_size and class_checkpoint_batch_size (default 64 each) are how many trials are screened, and drugs classified, at once. With a remote backend each trial or drug is its own request and retries, validated and checkpointed as soon as it finishes, and the next waiting one starts in its place, so one slow answer holds one slot instead of a batch; the endpoint pool still caps each server's concurrent requests, and units beyond that wait for it. A local engine, which batches prompts itself and is not thread-safe, gets groups of these sizes instead, checkpointed when each group returns. Either way each trial or drug gets its own prompts, retries and checkpoint, recorded in input order, so the sizes only schedule. Both keys are still part of the checkpoint fingerprint, as they always were, so changing them here starts a new checkpoint directory; the command line's --llm-batch-size overrides both for one run without entering the fingerprint, so a build can resume with another value. Synthesis is not batched either: each drug or class is its own chain of chunk calls, checkpointed as soon as that chain finishes, with up to remote.max_concurrent_requests chains in flight. Screening and synthesis LLM overrides inherit from llm_good_option. With a remote backend, structured_outputs (default true) decodes the screening and class answers under their JSON schemas (response_format json_schema); set it to false for a server without that support, and the answers are parsed and validated from free text as before.

Evidence is also retrieved on two axes beside the drug's own name, and each has its own budget so that neither can evict the other.

The classify stage gives an NCIt-matched drug every NCIt class above its concept, below the fixed umbrella concepts, without an LLM call; those are not capped. class_max_per_drug (default 3) caps the classes the LLM may add on top, or name for a drug NCIt leaves unclassified; an added NCIt class's own ancestors do not count against it. class_candidate_limit (default 25) bounds the NCIt candidate classes, found by local search of class names and synonyms in the drug's name, definition, and mechanism passages, that the LLM may choose from by code. class_assignment_evidence_max_tokens (40,000) bounds the mechanism passages that stage reads and searches, and class_llm gives it its own completion budget. class_evidence_max_tokens (60,000) bounds each chunk of the corpus that class synthesis reads. Class synthesis is a separate call from agent synthesis rather than a larger pooled one: 165 drugs already use more than half the agent budget and the largest uses 91% of it, so pooling would let a flood of same-class passages evict the agent's own data. class_option_summary_max_tokens bounds each class's stored projection. The scoring prompt re-renders classes and drugs from their structured facts instead, under good_option_prompt.

Retrieval settings for both axes live on ResearchSettings rather than in this block: class_facets, class_sources, class_research_rounds, and the max_class_* record caps for the class axis, and indication_terms_per_drug (default 25), indication_facets, indication_sources, and the max_indication_* caps for the indication axis. Indication terms come from the conditionsModule.conditions of the trials a drug appears in, falling back to derivedSection.conditionBrowseModule.meshes, so the catalog stays patient-free and cacheable. Both axes call only the query-driven sources; the ctgov, label, and curation adapters search by exact agent name and return nothing for a class name.

indication_facets defaults to efficacy_by_tumor, biomarker_prevalence, and biomarker_directed_efficacy for both drug–disease and class–disease retrieval.

Research requests are paced per host, in one budget shared by every subject researched at once and by every stage, the ctgov record fetch included; retries and redirects count against it. Requests to a host take turns, each a full interval after the previous one actually left, over a connection pool of the host's own, so neither a busy event loop nor page downloads to other hosts can release them in bursts. The defaults keep each service about 30% under its per-IP ceiling:

Host Requests per second Ceiling clinicaltrials.gov 0.6 (36 a minute) none published; about 50 a minute per IP is the commonly reported limit dailymed.nlm.nih.gov 1.0 none published; its 429s carry Retry-After: 60 eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov 2.0, or 7.0 with an NCBI API key 3 a second per IP without a key, 10 with one

The 2026-11-12 catalog rerun paced only E-utilities, at 2.5 a second in the client's shared connection pool. A quarter of its ClinicalTrials.gov requests came back 429, in research and in the serial record fetch (about 74 a minute), as did 8% of its saved PubMed attempts and 4% of DailyMed's. Europe PMC, CIViC and cancer.gov returned none and stay unpaced; general-web searches are bounded by --web-search-concurrency instead.

  • host_requests_per_second (default {}): per-host overrides of these defaults, for example {eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov: 1.5}; 0 leaves a host unpaced. The command line's --host-requests-per-second HOST=RATE overrides it. A limit is per IP, so two builds on one machine should split it.
  • ncbi_api_key_file (default null): a file holding an NCBI API key, sent with PubMed's E-utilities requests and raising their default rate to 7 a second. --ncbi-api-key-file overrides it, and either overrides the NCBI_API_KEY environment variable, which is read when neither is set. The key travels only in request bodies, never in a URL, log line, error message, research attempt, checkpoint or manifest.

Both keys only schedule requests, so they are left out of the checkpoint fingerprint: an existing checkpoint directory resumes with new rates, or with a key added or removed.

docs.title: good_option_prompt
docs.text:
Patient-time packing of catalog drug and class evidence into the llm_good_option prompt. It lives outside llm_good_option and good_option_catalog because those sections fingerprint catalog checkpoints.

  • context_tokens (default null): the teacher's context window. null uses llm_good_option.local.engine.max_model_len (262,144); set it when a remote endpoint serves a different length.
  • chars_per_token (3.5): conversion rate for the budget. Conservative for Gemma 4, which averages about 4.4 characters per token on catalog text, and for Nemotron 3.5 Super, whose tokenizer averages the same as Gemma 4's (4.6) on ctgov eligibility criteria.
  • safety_tokens (4,096): margin kept beyond the completion allowance, which is the active backend's llm_good_option max_tokens.
  • max_drug_section_tokens, max_class_section_tokens (20,000 each): upper bound on any one drug or class, however much room remains; null removes it.

See Evidence packing for how the budget is shared and when evidence is condensed.

docs.title: good_option_check
docs.text:
Settings for check_good_options, the on-demand patient-trial check. They are applied to a copy of the config at call time and stay outside llm_good_option so catalog-build fingerprints are unaffected.

  • max_output_tokens (50,000): completion cap for the scoring request, replacing the active backend's llm_good_option max_tokens (100,000) so more of the context carries evidence. null keeps the llm_good_option value.
  • discover_context_tokens (true): when good_option_prompt.context_tokens is unset and remote inference is enabled with an OpenAI-compatible provider, size evidence packing to the smallest max_model_len the servers report at /v1/models.
  • discovery_timeout_seconds (10.0): timeout for each lookup. A failed lookup falls back to the configured context and is reported in the metadata.
  • max_parse_attempts (3): total attempts for answers that fail validation.
  • reasoning_off_fallback (true): add one final attempt with thinking disabled.

docs.title: good_option_checker
docs.text: Deprecated. Configuration for the retired GoodOptionChecker classifier, kept so existing configs load. GoodOption scoring uses the LLM teacher (llm_good_option); the classifier APIs emit DeprecationWarning.

docs.title: QC metrics
docs.text:
Patient and trial summarization can produce QC reports. These reports are meant to help you review how a summarization run behaved before using the outputs downstream.

To request a QC report, pass return_qc=True to summarize_patients or extract_cohorts.

QC reports summarize how the current pipeline behaves, given the current prompts, filters, and postprocessing rules. Metrics are returned as rows with metric, value, denominator, percent, and ids.

docs.title: Patient summarization QC
docs.text:
Returned by summarize_patients(..., return_qc=True).

  • patients_dropped_noninformative_summary: summaries removed because they were empty or began with No information.
  • patients_failed_inference: patients removed because LLM inference failed or the summary was still rejected after patient.summary_quality_max_attempts attempts.
  • patients_exclusion_criteria_not_extracted: summaries whose boilerplate section (general_exclusion_criteria_evidence, the text after Other relevant history:) is empty, Not documented., or identical to the key section.
  • patients_missing_keyword:<keyword>: key sections (cancer_history_summary) missing an expected keyword.
  • patients_exceed_embedding_token_limit: key sections whose embedding-tokenized length, with the TrialSpace patient prompt, exceeds embedding.max_seq_length, the configured truncation cutoff used during embedding generation.

docs.title: Trial summarization QC
docs.text:
Returned by extract_cohorts(..., return_qc=True).

The default cohorts method reports:

  • trials_rejected_cancer_treatment: valid negative treatment decisions; these trials produce no cohort rows and remain in trial_rejections metadata.
  • trials_failed_inference: responses that remain invalid or incomplete after the configured attempts. These are errors, not treatment rejections.
  • trials_truncated_llm_response: trials whose final attempt ended at its token limit. These are also counted as inference failures.

Each denominator is the number of input trials. Full eligibility cohorts do not run the legacy keyword, boilerplate-separation, or embedding-length checks.

Explicit legacy hierarchical and one_shot extraction reports:

  • trials_missing_in_output: trials present in the input but not represented in the output after summarization/postprocessing.
  • trials_failed_inference: trials whose LLM inference finished with an error after retries were exhausted. These trials are removed before postprocessing.
  • trials_truncated_llm_response: trials where the LLM stopped due to max token length.
  • spaces_per_trial_min|median|max: min/median/max number of spaces per trial.
  • trials_with_non_distinct_spaces: trials with duplicate space numbers or duplicate space text.
  • spaces_dropped_missing_keyword:<keyword>: trial spaces dropped due to missing a required keyword.
  • trials_exclusion_criteria_not_extracted: trials whose exclusion criteria was not extracted.
  • spaces_exceed_embedding_token_limit: trial spaces whose embedding-tokenized length exceeds embedding.max_seq_length, the configured truncation cutoff used during embedding generation.

docs.title: How the Good Options pipeline works
docs.text:
An end-to-end walkthrough, in the order things happen. Two halves: building the evidence catalog, which is done once, offline, with no patient involved; then scoring one patient against one trial.

For the API surface see Good Option Research and Scoring. For the settings named below see Configuration.

docs.title: What feeds the research step
docs.text:
You supply a list of NCT numbers. The build downloads each trial's full ClinicalTrials.gov record, then uses an LLM to read every DRUG, BIOLOGICAL, and COMBINATION_PRODUCT intervention in its arm context and decide which are actual anticancer agents under test — dropping placebos, premedications, imaging tracers, devices, unnamed standard-of-care placeholders, and drugs that protect against toxicity or transplant complications (sodium thiosulfate for ototoxicity, tacrolimus or mycophenolate as GVHD prophylaxis) unless the trial uses them against the cancer. Each survivor gets a role: investigational, control, background, supportive, or uncertain. Background means given the same way to every participant; an agent given only in a comparator arm is control, even when it is standard of care. Only investigational and uncertain drugs are ever scored.

Each agent's name must come from its entry's own text: the ctgov name, aliases, description, or the descriptions of its arms, so an entry named "Phase I Arm A" contributes the agent its description names. Every agent is one drug: a regimen is listed as its components ("Pemetrexed + Cisplatin /Carboplatin" is three drugs), and a standard acronym such as FOLFIRI is expanded into its agents from knowledge, with the acronym recorded in regimen_names. Each agent is named by its generic name (INN/USAN) or development code, so "LV" is leucovorin and "5-Flurouracil" fluorouracil, with the entry's own spelling also recorded in regimen_names; a treatment category such as "adjuvant chemotherapy" is never an agent. Code rejects names the entry's text does not contain unless they expand a regimen or spelling that text names, and asks once more about names spelled as combinations. A two-character name such as "SG" or "LV" counts as contained only as whole words of the text, never as part of a longer word. A listed regimen name the text does not contain is dropped, not failed, so the entry's other grounded agents are kept.

Surviving agent names are matched against the bundled NCI Thesaurus snapshot for a canonical name, synonyms, and definition, then deduplicated across the whole run. An exact NCIt name or synonym wins: the name as written, without its parentheticals, or a parenthetical on its own ("[177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 (AAA617)" is found by AAA617). Otherwise a concept is taken only when it is the single one a rule finds, the strictest rule first: the same name up to case, spaces, hyphens, separators ("/", "+", "and"), salt abbreviations, isotope notation ("Ac-225 X" is "Actinium Ac 225 X"), and "X liposome" for "liposomal X"; then without salts, taking the parent molecule when salts of it tie; then with route, dosage-form, and biosimilar words moved first or dropped ("Trastuzumab SC"); then with one misspelled word of eight or more letters corrected ("5-Flurouracil"). A wrong match is worse than none, so nothing else is tried: a name's first word alone ("Polatuzumab"), an abbreviation NCIt lacks ("LV"), and an agent NCIt does not file as a drug ("GM-CSF") stay unmatched. A drug with no NCIt match gets an identity hashed from the same normalized name, so "Interleukin 2" and "Interleukin-2" stay one drug. The result is the unique drug set plus a table of which drugs appear in which trials in which role.

docs.title: Step 1 — Research each drug on the open internet
docs.text:
For every unique drug the system searches five facets: mechanism and targets, efficacy by tumor type, biomarker prevalence, biomarker-directed efficacy, and safety.

It queries seven sources: ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed, Europe PMC, CIViC, DailyMed, cancer.gov, and a general web search that also downloads and extracts the text of the pages it finds. Each source gets a query written in its own syntax — boolean for the two literature indexes, prose for the web ones. The ctgov, label, and curation sources search by exact agent name and ignore the query, so each of their requests is sent once per drug and its response read by every facet and round.

Three adaptive rounds run: the first searches everything, later rounds re-search only facets that came back nearly empty, with broadened phrasing. Failures retry with Retry-After or exponential backoff, and a successful empty search stays distinct from an exhausted technical failure. If every source fails on a facet across all rounds the drug is marked blocked and never synthesized.

Many drugs are researched at once (--subject-concurrency), so requests to ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, and the NCBI E-utilities behind PubMed are paced per host in one shared budget, retries included: by default 0.6, 1.0, and 2.0 requests a second, about 30% under each service's per-IP limit. An NCBI API key raises E-utilities to 7 a second; give it as a file with --ncbi-api-key-file (or good_option_catalog.ncbi_api_key_file), or in the NCBI_API_KEY environment variable. Rates and key only schedule requests, so a checkpointed build resumes after either changes. See good_option_catalog.

Each result becomes a passage: up to 5,000 characters of text plus its source, URL, license, the query that found it, and a content hash. The drug's NCIt definition is materialized as a passage too, so the model can cite it like anything else.

A second pass searches the drug paired with a disease. The diseases come from the conditionsModule.conditions of the trials the drug appears in — up to indication_terms_per_drug, selected round-robin across trials — and re-runs efficacy by tumor, biomarker prevalence, and biomarker-directed efficacy against the four query-driven sources with the disease as a required clause. It is capped as a whole by max_indication_passages_per_drug and interleaved across diseases, sources, and search facets so efficacy results cannot crowd out prevalence findings. Every passage records the axis that found it in query_scope, so nothing downstream confuses drug-name evidence with disease-conditioned evidence.

docs.title: Step 2 — Work out each drug's pharmacologic class
docs.text:
Classes come from the NCI Thesaurus hierarchy in the bundled snapshot. A class is an NCIt concept above some drug concept, in the Pharmacologic Substance branch, other than a fixed list of umbrellas too broad to group agents that act alike (NCIT_UMBRELLA_CLASSES: Pharmacologic Substance, Antineoplastic Agent, Immunotherapeutic Agent, Biological Agent, Enzyme Inhibitor, Signal Transduction Inhibitor, Targeted Therapy Agent, and the Antineoplastic Protein/Enzyme Inhibitor, Biological Agent, Antibody, and Immunomodulating Agent concepts). Everything below them is kept, from Protein Kinase Inhibitor and Monoclonal Antibody down to PD1 Inhibitor. The chemical-structure branch (Organic Chemical, Nitrogen Compound, ...) is not used.

A drug matched to NCIt gets every class above its concept, in code, with no LLM call: pembrolizumab gets Anti-PD1 Monoclonal Antibody, Monoclonal Antibody, PD1 Inhibitor, Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor, and Immune Checkpoint Modulator. NCIt can leave a class out, so a local search of NCIt class names and synonyms against the drug's name, definition, and mechanism passages finds up to class_candidate_limit (25) candidate classes, and an LLM may add those the passages show the drug belongs to, by code: an FLT3 inhibitor class for emavusertib, which NCIt files only as an IRAK4 inhibitor. An added class brings its NCIt ancestors with it. The LLM never removes a hierarchy class, codes outside the candidates are rejected, and an NCIt-classified drug with no candidates is never sent to it.

A drug NCIt does not classify — no match, or only umbrellas above it, which is common for first-in-human agents such as golcadomide or the BCL6 degrader BMS-986458 — gets its classes from the LLM: candidates first, and a new class, marked class_source = "llm", only where no candidate fits. A new class is written in canonical form ("CD93 monoclonal antibody", "BRD9 degrader") and identified by a hash of its normalized name, so "PD-L1 inhibitor" and "PD-L1 Inhibitors" collapse to one thing; a new name that spells an NCIt class is stored as that class. class_max_per_drug (3) caps the classes the LLM adds or names per drug, each with a basis (target, mechanism, or modality), a target, a confidence, and citations to the passages that establish it.

An NCIt class's id is NCIT:<code>, its name NCIt's display or preferred name, and its aliases NCIt synonyms. Each drug_classes row records class_source (ncit or llm), ncit_code, and assigned_by: ncit_hierarchy, llm_added_ncit, llm_added_ncit_ancestor, or llm_new. Hierarchy rows carry no basis, target, confidence, or citations; the hierarchy is their evidence. Two drugs landing on the same class share everything downstream.

docs.title: Step 3 — Research each class
docs.text: The same machinery as step 1, with the class name and aliases as the subject, run once per class rather than once per drug. Three facets, four query-driven sources, one round. The class is also paired with the diseases named by its member drugs' trials, searching the same three disease-specific facets, including biomarker prevalence. An NCIt class's definition joins its corpus as a citable passage, as a drug's does.

docs.title: Step 4 — Synthesize the drug evidence
docs.text:
A drug's ledger is ordered round-robin across (query_scope, source) so no retrieval axis is starved, then split into chunks of at most synthesis_chunk_max_tokens (60,000) of passage text. Nothing is discarded: the chunks run in order, one LLM call each, with the chunk's passages numbered P1..Pn. Bigger chunks mean fewer calls but fewer facts: the model condenses more of a large chunk, and 100,000-token chunks gave about 25% fewer facts than 60,000 in a Gemma 4 comparison.

Each call sees the facts built so far, numbered F1..Fn, and returns JSON with six arrays — mechanism and targets, efficacy by tumor, biomarker prevalence, biomarker-directed efficacy, safety, limitations — holding only what this chunk adds. Every item must be one self-contained sentence carrying its numbers, plus support_ids citing passage numbers, plus labels for tumor type, histology, regimen, biomarker, and prevalence denominator where they apply. An item that corrects or supersedes an existing fact names it in replaces.

Code then checks the work: citations resolve back to real evidence IDs, uncited items are dropped, and each surviving fact is stamped scope: agent. The new items are merged in code: every existing fact is kept unless a validated item replaces it, and an item repeating an existing fact's text is dropped. Because existing facts never pass back through the model's output, a broad class that has accumulated hundreds of them cannot silently lose any. Failures retry with the exact validation error quoted back; a chunk that never validates leaves the facts so far unchanged.

docs.title: Step 5 — Synthesize the class evidence
docs.text:
The same chunked synthesis, once per class, with chunks bounded by its own class_evidence_max_tokens (60,000). Facts are stamped scope: class.

The separation is the point rather than an implementation detail. A pooled budget would let a flood of same-class passages evict an agent's own data, and the agent's own data is what the rubric asks the scorer to prefer.

docs.title: Step 6 — Render readable summaries
docs.text:
Structured facts become plain text. Each bullet carries its scope and attribution:

- [scope: agent | evidence level: mature trial results | tumor type: Colon Cancer
   | histology: Stage III dMMR | regimen: Atezolizumab and mFOLFOX6]
  In a phase 3 trial of resected stage III dMMR colon cancer, adjuvant
  atezolizumab plus mFOLFOX6 improved 3-year DFS to 86.3% versus 76.2%
  (HR 0.50, p<0.001).

Two versions per drug — one without safety for scoring, one with safety for Help Me Choose — plus one per class. The character budget is shared across sections by weighted max-min fair share: a section with one short line releases its remainder, and when every section overflows, tumor and biomarker efficacy get three and two shares to each other section's one.

Large classes synthesize hundreds of facts, so what the budget keeps matters:

  • Efficacy and safety facts are ranked by their evidence-level label (phase 3/regulatory/guideline, then randomized/phase 2/meta-analysis, then other human evidence, then case reports), taking turns across tumor types within a rank so one disease cannot crowd out another.
  • Efficacy findings labelled preclinical (in vitro, animal, xenograft, and nothing marking them as human) move out of the human efficacy sections into "Preclinical efficacy (not human evidence)", which only receives budget the other sections leave unused.
  • A truncated section ends with a count of omitted findings, passage handles such as (P3) are removed, and repeated statements are printed once.

Ranking reads free-text labels with patterns, so it is a heuristic ordering, not a validated evidence grade. It changes only the rendered text; structured facts are stored unchanged.

The stored scoring version is fixed-size. At scoring time the same renderer runs again from the stored facts with a budget sized to the trial (see Part B), so the ranking above decides what survives there too.

These renders are the only thing a patient-bearing prompt ever sees. URLs, source names, queries, and ctgov metadata stay in the internal tables.

docs.title: Step 7 — Write and validate
docs.text:
Everything is written to Parquet: trial records, screening decisions, the trial-drug index, drug summaries, drug passages, class assignments, class passages, class summaries, and a full audit log of every search attempt. A manifest records file hashes, a compatibility_id fingerprinting those hashes, a fingerprint of the catalog prompt text, and counts.

Validation re-checks the bundle: hashes match the files and the compatibility_id, every citation points at a passage that exists for that drug or class, drug facts carry scope: agent and class facts scope: class, no duplicate keys, roles are legal. load_good_option_catalog runs this by default.

Every stage checkpoints to disk, so a build that dies at hour six resumes rather than restarting.

docs.title: Part B — Scoring one patient against one trial
docs.text:
1. Look up the trial. If it is missing, its ctgov fetch failed, it has no scoreable drug, or any scoreable drug failed research or synthesis, the pair comes back explicitly unscored with a reason. There is no fallback to live search.
  2. Collect the stored facts for each scoreable drug.
  3. Collect one class block per distinct class across those drugs, each labelled with which drugs it speaks for. Two drugs sharing a class produce one block, not two. The drugs and classes are rendered from their facts to fit what the teacher's context leaves, not the fixed-size projections stored in the catalog. They share that room by weighted fair share, drugs ahead of classes; a subject short of room first shortens each line to keep every fact, and drops the weakest facts only when that is not enough.
  4. Build the prompt: the patient's cancer history first, then the drug summaries and class blocks, then the rubric, then the exact list of drug names to score.
  5. The model answers four yes-or-no questions per drug:
  6. Has this drug, or its class, helped people with what this patient has?
  7. Is the feature it targets common in this disease (20% or more)?
  8. Does this patient's tumor actually have that feature?
  9. Has targeting that feature helped people?

Each needs a rationale naming the specific evidence or the specific gap, and saying whether it relied on the agent's own evidence or its class's. 6. Code validates strictly — drug names must match exactly, points must be the integers 0 or 1, rationales must be non-empty — and computes the score as total points over four times the drug count. Malformed answers retry individually with the exact parser error, and optionally once more with model thinking disabled.

check_good_options runs these steps on demand with production defaults. It loads the catalog once and reuses it until its files change. It caps the model's answer at 50,000 tokens and fits the evidence to the context length the serving endpoint reports. A malformed answer gets three tries, then one more with thinking off. Those settings live in the good_option_check preset section.

A second scoring path, a four-logit classifier reading one patient and one drug summary, is deprecated: it never saw class evidence and no trained model was published.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text: Two soft spots, both the same shape. The disease-conditioned search picks diseases by what the drug is usually studied in rather than what the trial being scored is about, and the class search has no disease attached at all. Together they leave roughly a third of drug-trial pairs with no evidence retrieved for the patient's own disease.

docs.title: Guideline extraction
docs.text:
matchminer_ai.trials.summarize_guidelines turns one locally supplied NCCN guideline into canonical disease-state populations, each defined by nine population fields (stored as one line in clinical_space_summary). Loading a catalog lays those fields out as a trial cohort's key criteria (cohort_key_criteria; see Key criteria). Each population also has diagnostic/workup considerations, treatment/management options, source quotations, and uncertainties. All clinical content is extracted by the configured LLM. Python manages source ownership, record identity, validation, persistence, and export.

Generation prompts begin by explaining the library's purpose: later patient-summary matching and retrieval of source-supported workup and treatment considerations. They define a clinical space and explain that only its nine population fields enter the matching text; names and menus cannot supply missing criteria. Each call then receives its stage-specific task and schema, including any fixed-field restrictions.

This is an optional source-grounded extraction workflow, separate from trial matching. A guideline population is not a clinical trial, a treatment recommendation, or an eligibility determination. Structural checks do not establish clinical correctness or completeness. Review the original PDF when graphical relationships or clinical applicability are uncertain.

docs.title: Supply a local source library
docs.text:
No NCCN source files or generated catalogs are distributed with this package. Supply your own permitted local copies. The reader accepts the page-preserving nccn-pdf-to-markdown manifest format: a collection markdown/manifest.json, per-disease manifests and Markdown page files, plus the original PDFs alongside markdown/. Each page has a fenced text block and a recorded hash. PDF hashes, page coverage, and Markdown hashes must agree before any model call. Incomplete copies fail explicitly and can be retried after copying finishes.

For a new collection, the repository includes scripts/convert_guidelines.py. Install matchminer-ai[guideline-conversion] and Poppler's pdftotext, then run from a source checkout:

python scripts/convert_guidelines.py \
  --input-dir /path/to/local/guideline-pdfs \
  --output-dir /path/to/local/guideline-pdfs/markdown

The converter requires explicit external paths and makes no network or model calls. It preserves text, page addresses, and links; it does not perform OCR or recover every arrow, table relationship, superscript, or graphical decision branch. Retain the PDF for human review. Conversion provenance is in scripts/README.md.

docs.title: Extract one disease
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.trials import list_guidelines, summarize_guidelines

source = "/path/to/local/guideline-pdfs/markdown"
print(list_guidelines(source))  # Use the disease folder name from this table.

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote["enabled"] = True
config.remote["server_urls"] = ["http://camus:8002/v1"]
config.remote["request_timeout"] = 7200
config.remote["max_concurrent_requests"] = 32

spaces, metadata, qc = summarize_guidelines(
    source,
    disease="breast",
    output_dir="/path/to/private-derived-data/breast-run-1",
    config=config,
    return_metadata=True,
    return_qc=True,
    progress_callback=print,
)

The function accepts one disease per call and returns the same flag combinations as extract_cohorts: a DataFrame, optionally followed by metadata and/or a QC DataFrame. The standard columns are space_trial_id, trial_id, clinical_space_number, clinical_space_summary, and general_exclusion_criteria. Here trial_id has a guideline: namespace, and general_exclusion_criteria is NA because no trial protocol was summarized. These IDs must not be sent to services expecting NCT identifiers.

Additional columns include the nine-field space object, diagnostic_workup, treatment_options, evidence, source, uncertainties, and omitted context. Each menu item has its conditions, source-stated category, and evidence. Load the exported catalog with load_guideline_catalog to get each space's cohort_key_criteria, the text the retrieval APIs pass to TrialSpace and the decision model; this function does not load an embedding model or perform matching.

docs.title: Endpoint and budget configuration
docs.text:
The collection runner can give unstarted catalogs to another same-model server:

python examples/extract_guideline_collection.py \
  --source /path/to/local/guideline-pdfs/markdown \
  --output-dir /path/to/private-derived-data/collection \
  --endpoint http://original-server:8001/v1 \
  --additional-endpoint http://additional-server:8060/v1 \
  --new-disease-endpoint http://additional-server:8060/v1 \
  --model served-model-id --concurrency 32

Retain the original invocation's source, output, primary endpoint, model and completed-catalog arguments when resuming. Additional endpoints are preflighted for the same model ID and advertised context window. Each disease with an existing run_config.json keeps its recorded endpoint and checkpoints. With --new-disease-endpoint, every unstarted catalog goes to that server; otherwise unstarted work is balanced between configured endpoints. Separate disease-worker pools allow the additional server to start immediately. --concurrency applies per endpoint.
